### GG-120 — `run_band_monitor.py`'s dated-verdict writer ignored `--out`, letting synthetic pytest-fixture data leak into the tracked `verdicts/` directory

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-120 |
| Arm | MLB |
| Category | Test-isolation bug — CLI flag silently bypassed on one of two output paths |
| What was missed | `scripts/run_band_monitor.py::main()` writes three artifacts per run: `band_monitor_results.json` and `band_monitor_summary.json` (both correctly written under `args.out`, which respects the `--out` CLI flag), and a third, timestamped `band_monitor_<run_id>.json` written via `write_dated_verdict(results, VERDICTS_DIR, run_id)` — a call that used the hardcoded module constant `VERDICTS_DIR = OUT_DIR / "verdicts"` (`OUT_DIR = Path("exp_output/T255-BAND-MONITOR")`) instead of `args.out / "verdicts"`. `tests/test_band_monitor.py::test_healthy_book_returns_0` and `::test_anti_predictive_book_returns_1` both call `main(["--portfolio", ..., "--t4-ledger", ..., "--ci", "--out", str(tmp_path / "out")])`, correctly intending to isolate all three output artifacts under `tmp_path`. Because the dated-verdict write bypassed `--out` entirely, every run of those two tests instead wrote a real, UTC-timestamped file directly into the git-tracked `exp_output/T255-BAND-MONITOR/verdicts/` directory — using synthetic fixture data (a "healthy book" and an "anti-predictive book" scenario, `raw_n=40`/`raw_n=60`, fabricated edge/winrate values) indistinguishable at a glance from real production monitoring runs. |
| When it should have been caught | At the time `write_dated_verdict` was added (T-341, commit `7d339b6`, 2026-07-11) — the dated-artifact path should have been wired through the same `args.out` the two "latest" artifacts use, and the two new tests added alongside it should have asserted the dated file landed under `tmp_path`, not merely that `main()` returned the expected exit code. |
| Phases it survived | Live since T-341 (2026-07-11) through this session (2026-07-14) — roughly 3 days / at least 2 confirmed pytest invocations of `test_band_monitor.py` during that window (see Discovery). |
| Why it survived | No test asserted the dated-verdict file's actual location — both tests only check `main()`'s return code (0 / 1), not the filesystem side effect. The tracked `verdicts/` directory already legitimately accumulates one real file per Monday VPS cron run, so a handful of extra files with plausible-looking UTC timestamps did not visually stand out as anomalous until their `reason` field (an error string citing a `ledger not found` path) was read closely enough to notice it pointed at a pytest tmp directory (`/private/var/.../pytest-of-earlignacio/pytest-40N/test_healthy_book_returns_00/none.jsonl`). |
| Impact | Low direct risk (the leaked files are inert, never consumed by any downstream reader — C7 wiring is separately gated by `--no-c7` and untouched by this bug), but real repo-hygiene and audit-trail contamination: every future `pytest tests/test_band_monitor.py` run silently adds 2 more fake-data files to a directory the project otherwise treats as an authoritative history of real per-band monitoring verdicts. Same failure shape as GG-117 (`band_monitor_summary.json` git-tracked but cron-rewritten) and GG-102 — a third instance of this script's output-path handling not matching its actual write behavior. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-14, this session (Window 2, T-359/T-361 follow-on housekeeping check). 4 untracked files (`band_monitor_20260714T050538Z.json`, `...050542Z`, `...050929Z`, `...050932Z`) found sitting in `exp_output/T255-BAND-MONITOR/verdicts/` at session start. Ruled out both plausible innocent explanations before concluding it was a bug: (1) not the VPS cron — that runs Mondays only and on a separate machine, and 2026-07-14 is a Tuesday; (2) not deliberate diagnostic evidence from this session's own `run_t359_gg105_interaction_model.py` work — that script only imports `load_t4_ledger`/`filter_clean` helper functions from `run_band_monitor`, it does not invoke `main()`. Confirmed root cause by reading each leaked file's `T4M-PROJ.reason` field, which cited ledger paths of the exact shape `.../pytest-of-earlignacio/pytest-40{6,7}/test_healthy_book_returns_00/none.jsonl` and `.../test_anti_predictive_book_retu0/none.jsonl` — pytest's own truncated tmp-dir naming for the two test functions in `tests/test_band_monitor.py`, confirming two separate local `pytest tests/test_band_monitor.py` invocations this session (pytest-406, pytest-407), each producing one leaked file per test. |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED same session (2026-07-14, T-363).** `scripts/run_band_monitor.py::main()` changed to `write_dated_verdict(results, args.out / "verdicts", run_id)`; the now-dead `VERDICTS_DIR` module constant removed. Default behavior is unchanged (`args.out` defaults to `OUT_DIR`, so `args.out / "verdicts"` == the old `VERDICTS_DIR` on a normal, no-flag invocation). The 4 leaked files were deleted (never committed — caught while still untracked, so no git history cleanup was needed). Verified: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_band_monitor.py -q` → 28/28 passed, and `git status --porcelain exp_output/T255-BAND-MONITOR/` empty immediately after — confirms the fixture tests no longer write outside `tmp_path`. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (T-363). |

</details>

### GG-144 — CLAUDE.md Step 3's open-gap scan silently misses 12 of 26 OPEN gaps, and the miss is systematically biased toward the most important ones, because emphatic entries bold their status marker out of the grep's reach

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-144 |
| Arm | Cross-arm (governance process) |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a mandatory protocol check whose failure mode correlates with the severity of what it is meant to surface |
| What was missed | CLAUDE.md's MANDATORY SESSION-START PROTOCOL Step 3 runs `grep -n "| OPEN" "03_DECISIONS/GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md"` and instructs that "any OPEN entry must be addressed or explicitly deferred before implementation work". Two Status formats coexist in the log: the plain `| Status | OPEN — ...` and the emphatic `| Status | **OPEN — ...`. The grep pattern `"| OPEN"` matches the first and **not** the second, because the bold markers sit between the pipe and the word. Measured 2026-07-29: **16 Status lines match, 12 do not — 28 gaps are genuinely OPEN and the protocol reports 16.** |
| When it should have been caught | At any session-start since the first bolded-OPEN entry was written. Also by GG-132's `MEMORY_BANK.md` narrative-chain audit and by the several sessions that have specifically audited `governance_scan.sh` and `session_delta.sh` parsing (GG-138's neighbours at lines 2324/2434) — all of which examined the *hook* tooling and none of which validated the *CLAUDE.md protocol's own* grep against the file it reads. **Most directly: this is a recurrence of GG-122**, which found and fixed the identical bug in `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh` on 2026-07-16 (10 vs. true 19), and of T-370's 2026-07-15 `MEMORY_BANK.md` caveat naming the same defect. Both times the fix landed in the hook and the observation landed in a narrative log; neither propagated to CLAUDE.md Step 3 — the one command the protocol declares mandatory. The convenient copy was repaired and the authoritative one was not. |
| Phases it survived | Unknown start date; present through 2026-07-29. Every session-start protocol run in that window under-reported the open-gap set. |
| Why it survived | **The bias is the mechanism.** A routine gap gets a terse `| Status | OPEN.`; a gap the author considers severe or contested gets an emphatic, bolded, multi-clause status narrative — `| Status | **OPEN — remediation in progress ... Do not read this as resolved.**`. The very formatting that signals importance is what removes the entry from the scan. The result is not a random 43% sample loss but a systematic one: the hidden set is **GG-037** (calibration collapse / inverted edge), **GG-038** (T4 kill-switch SLA 12× too slow for continuous evaluation — a live Hard Rule 6 tension), **GG-039**, **GG-040**, **GG-041**, **GG-045** (depth ceiling), **GG-046** (T4 commercial validation untested — the T4 alpha thesis's own validation gap), **GG-105** (the anti-predictive edge finding, the single most consequential open gap in the project), **GG-125** (Brier/ECE ladder never invoked), **GG-132**, **GG-138**, **GG-140** (recalibration class exhausted). A session that trusted Step 3's output would conclude that neither GG-105 nor GG-140 nor GG-046 is open. |
| Impact | **HIGH on governance reliability; no direct capital or model impact.** The protocol's stated purpose is that no implementation work begins over an unaddressed OPEN gap; for an unknown number of sessions that guarantee has been void for the 12 most emphatically-flagged gaps. This is the same failure shape as GG-108 (a Step 4 grep pointed at a nonexistent filename, returning empty output indistinguishable from "healthy") and GG-001 (a stub that survived four gate clearances because no scan existed) — a check that returns a clean-looking answer while being structurally unable to see the thing it was written to catch. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-29, isolated worktree `session/20260729T054746Z-fable-strategic-analysis`, analysis-only strategic review. Found incidentally: after registering GG-142/GG-143 with bolded status markers, a verification `grep -c "| OPEN"` returned an unchanged count, revealing that the newly-added entries were invisible to the scan — which then prompted auditing the pre-existing set. |
| Resolution | **Fixed 2026-07-29, G1 session (commit 343ce86, worktree `session/20260729T234501Z-g1-protocol-repair`).** Implemented option (a)+(c) as recommended: CLAUDE.md's Step 3 command and `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh` (which already carried the GG-122 fix but had never propagated it here) both replaced with `grep -nE "^\| Status \| \*{0,2}OPEN"` plus a live reconciliation assertion (plain-OPEN count + bold-OPEN count = total anchored matches), so any future format divergence fails loudly rather than silently undercounting. Re-ran against the live log: true OPEN count = 28 (17 plain + 12 bold, one template row excluded); confirmed GG-105/GG-140/GG-046/GG-038 now surface. Option (b) (normalizing the 12 bolded markers to plain form) was not done — not needed once the scan itself is emphasis-insensitive, and normalizing would erase the narrative signal the bold markers carry. |

### GG-122 — `governance_scan.sh`'s OPEN-gap grep only matched literal `"| OPEN"`, undercounting bold-prefixed Status cells (10 vs. true 19)

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-122 |
| Arm | Core |
| Category | Incremental architecture — a measurement tool drifted out of sync with the format of the data it measures |
| What was missed | `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh`'s OPEN-gap counter (`OPEN=$(grep "| OPEN" ... )`) matched only the literal substring `"| OPEN"`. A number of this log's own Status cells are phrased `"| Status | **OPEN — ..."` (bold-markdown prefix on the word OPEN) — the literal grep does not match those, so every bold-prefixed OPEN entry was silently excluded from the count. |
| When it should have been caught | Whenever a Status cell was first written with a `**OPEN` bold prefix instead of a plain `OPEN` prefix — the hook should have been re-verified against the log's actual current formatting at that point, or the grep should have been format-tolerant from the start. |
| Phases it survived | Unknown number of sessions between the hook's introduction and this discovery (2026-07-15) — the hook runs on every `UserPromptSubmit` and nobody cross-checked its printed count against a manual count of the log in that window. |
| Why it survived | The hook's own output ("N open / M total") reads as authoritative and was never spot-checked against the source file by hand; a burn-down trend computed from an undercounted numerator still looks internally consistent (it just tracks the wrong baseline), so nothing about the hook's own output would have flagged the discrepancy. |
| Impact | MEDIUM, measurement-only. The undercounted total (10 instead of 19) fed the burn-down-trend calculation in `scripts/lib/governance_gap_burndown.py` and every session's printed "OPEN GOVERNANCE GAPS" summary — no capital, model, or gate decision relied on the raw count directly, but any session judging governance-debt trajectory from this hook's output for the affected period was working from a number roughly half the true value. No downstream gate (G6, Tier 1/2) reads this count directly. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-15, this session (T-372, digest-adoption + timestamp-check session), per explicit operator instruction to reconcile a burn-down-review discrepancy. Verified via two independent greps against the live log: literal `"| OPEN"` (10 matches) vs. a Status-cell-aware regex `^\| Status \|\s*\**OPEN\b` (20 raw matches, 19 after excluding the log's own field-format legend row at the "Gap Registration Template" section, which is itself phrased `"OPEN / IN PROGRESS / RESOLVED [date]"` and already correctly excluded by the existing `grep -v "OPEN / IN PROGRESS"` filter). Cross-checked all 19 real matches against their owning `### GG-NNN` headers by line-range lookup: GG-007, 020, 027, 037, 038, 039, 040, 041, 044, 045, 046, 056, 066, 072, 078, 094, 098, 105, 119. |
| Resolution | Fixed same session: `governance_scan.sh`'s grep changed from `grep "| OPEN"` to `grep -E "^\| Status \|\s*\**OPEN\b"`, anchored to the Status-cell line and tolerant of an optional bold-markdown prefix, while keeping the existing `grep -v "OPEN / IN PROGRESS"` / `grep -v "template"` exclusions. Re-ran the hook post-fix: now reports "19 open / 120 total (101 resolved, 15.8% open)". No GG entries were added or removed by this fix — it is a counting-tool correction only. |
| Status | **RESOLVED 2026-07-15.** True OPEN count as of this reading: **19** (see Discovery list). Re-check trigger: any future change to how Status cells are phrased in this log (e.g. a new markdown-emphasis convention) should be spot-checked against `governance_scan.sh`'s regex before assuming the hook's count still matches ground truth. |

</details>

### GG-123 — T2 MLB same-day gating formula uses full vig instead of half_spread as its cost term (magnitude bug, not GG-119's sign-flip pattern)

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


**Numbering note:** this gap was drafted and locally logged as "GG-122"/"T-372" before a concurrent session (`session/20260715T235138Z-digest-adoption-timestamp-check`) independently claimed and merged those exact same IDs to `main` (PR #30) for the unrelated `governance_scan.sh` fix immediately above — a genuine two-way ID collision, not a duplicate of the same finding. Renumbered to **GG-123/T-373** at merge-reconciliation time, following this project's established precedent for exactly this failure mode (the earlier T-368→T-372 collision, see `MEMORY_BANK.md`). The script filename (`scripts/run_t368_gg122_t2_vig_magnitude_diag.py`), its output directory (`exp_output/T368-GG122-T2-VIG-MAGNITUDE-DIAG/`), and `00_ADMIN/APR-0028_gg122-t2-vig-magnitude-decision-request.md`'s filename are left as-is per that same precedent (informal working numbers in filenames are tolerated; the canonical ID lives in the log/decision text, corrected here).

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-123 |
| Arm | MLB |
| Category | Fee/edge-frame magnitude bug — adjacent to but distinct from GG-113/GG-119's sign-flip pattern |
| What was missed | `run_t2_mlb_sameday.py` (~lines 416-423) computes `vig = current_mkt.vig` (the full bid-ask spread) and then `gross_edge = p_calibrated - mid - vig`, `net_edge = gross_edge - kalshi_fee`. The established codebase convention — `run_exp017.py`'s symmetric-cost framing, and T1's `run_mlb_paper_trade.py` (`half = mkt.half_spread; gross_edge = p_calibrated - mid - half`) — subtracts only `half_spread` (`vig / 2.0`), the actual one-sided transaction cost, per `kalshi_client.py::PlayerMarket`'s own docstring ("vig is the full spread ...; half-spread is the cost to enter"). T2 double-charges the spread relative to this convention. |
| When it should have been caught | When T2's local gating formula was first written, by checking it against `run_exp017.py`'s convention directly (as T1's formula apparently was). Flagged only as an adjacent, out-of-scope observation during GG-119's diagnosis (2026-07-14/15) rather than caught at implementation time. |
| Phases it survived | Live in production (T2 same-day MLB cron) since whenever `run_t2_mlb_sameday.py`'s gating formula was last touched — not separately dated here. |
| Why it survived | No test asserts T2's cost term matches `half_spread` specifically; GG-113's fix and GG-119's diagnosis were both scoped elsewhere (T4M-PROJ, T1) and only noted T2's formula in passing. |
| Impact | **CONFIRMED via direct code read, 2026-07-15 (originally logged T-368, isolated worktree `session/20260715T200705Z-gg-t2-half-spread-audit`).** Unlike GG-113/GG-119, this is NOT a sign-flip — `run_t2_mlb_sameday.py` has no NO-direction branch at all (`PAPER_YES_ONLY` defaults `true`; no `"NO"`/`EDGE_NO` string anywhere in the file), independently re-confirmed by direct code read. This is a magnitude-only bug, and it is **conservative-direction**: it under-computes edge and can cause T2 to reject bets that actually clear the gate under the correct (`half_spread`) formula — it costs profit by being too strict, the opposite of GG-113/GG-119's inflate-and-admit-bad-bets pattern. **Quantification (`scripts/run_t368_gg122_t2_vig_magnitude_diag.py`, full output `exp_output/T368-GG122-T2-VIG-MAGNITUDE-DIAG/t2_vig_magnitude_diag_results.json`):** T2's resolved ledger is n=2 (both YES, both WIN, `paper_portfolio_mlb.json` band="T2") — far too small for a dollar-denominated realized-P&L estimate analogous to GG-119's T1 finding (n=259), and none is asserted here. Structural gating impact instead assessed across all 39 evaluated candidates recorded in T2's 15 most-recent daily report files (`t2_mlb_*_1930.json`, 2026-07-01 through 2026-07-15), reconstructing `vig` algebraically from each row's stored `p_t2`/`mid_price`/`net_edge` (`vig = p_t2 - mid - kalshi_fee - net_edge_buggy`) and computing `net_edge_corrected = net_edge_buggy + half_spread`: 3 rows already clear T2's local `EDGE_YES=0.02` gate under the buggy formula; 1 additional row (Ketel Marte, 2026-07-12, threshold=1) flips PASS→YES at that local gate under correction (buggy 0.016 → corrected 0.021); **0 of 39 rows would additionally clear the binding `MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE` (0.04, `risk.py` CHECK 3) — the actual determinant of whether a bet is placed — meaning zero realized bet-outcome changes in the observed sample.** One near-miss exists (Junior Caminero, 2026-07-04, corrected edge 0.0345, 0.0055 below the 0.04 floor; this row already cleared the local gate under the buggy formula too but was rejected downstream). Reconstructed `half_spread` across all 39 rows: mean $0.0085, median $0.01, max $0.015, min $0.005 — small but real and nonzero on every row, meaning the exposure is currently unrealized but structural, not hypothetical. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-15 (originally logged T-368, corrected to T-373), isolated worktree `session/20260715T200705Z-gg-t2-half-spread-audit`, explicit follow-on to GG-119's Impact field and ADR-0045's "Proposed D3" (which flagged this exact question as deliberately deferred, out-of-scope adjacent observation, and not yet its own governance gap). |
| Resolution | **FIX APPLIED 2026-07-15 (T-373), per Earl's explicit verbal DS sign-off** ("Okay - yes proceed with the fix now, you have my authority") on `00_ADMIN/APR-0028_gg122-t2-vig-magnitude-decision-request.md`'s Proposed D1. `run_t2_mlb_sameday.py`'s cost term changed from `vig = current_mkt.vig; gross_edge = p_calibrated - mid - vig` to `half_spread = current_mkt.half_spread; gross_edge = p_calibrated - mid - half_spread`, matching `run_exp017.py`/T1's (`run_mlb_paper_trade.py`) convention. The `vig=vig` parameter passed to `open_position()` for recordkeeping is unchanged (mirrors T1's own pattern of keeping full `vig` for recordkeeping while using `half_spread` only in the edge computation). Scoped regression run (`tests/test_t191_mlb_t2.py`, `tests/test_t195_mlb_silent_fallback.py`): 46/46 passed. **Proposed D2 (CURRENT_LOGIC_EPOCH bump), same session (T-373):** initially deferred while the parallel T1/ADR-0045 branch remained unmerged (global-counter collision risk). That branch has since merged (PR #28, `6f37629`; its own commit `13202bc` advanced the epoch to 5, confirmed T1-scoped only — band gate in `paper_trader.py::open_position()` extended to `{"T4M-PROJ", "T1"}`, not `"T2"`). With no double-bump risk confirmed, D2 was actioned: a new boundary (epoch=6, resolving_gap="GG-123", commit_sha=`cc887e8`) appended to `logic_epoch.py`'s `_BOUNDARIES`, advancing `CURRENT_LOGIC_EPOCH` to 6. Confirmed `paper_trader.py::open_position()` needs no T2-specific band-gate change — T2 has no NO-direction branch, so the sign-flip logic GG-113/GG-119 fixed there never applies to T2. Test suite re-run post-bump: `tests/test_backfill_logic_epoch.py` required 3 fixture updates (new `_POST_GG122` marker, new epoch-5 test, `_pos()` default timestamp shifted past the new boundary) — all pre-existing tests asserted against `CURRENT_LOGIC_EPOCH` dynamically except one literal boundary-timestamp fixture, now corrected. A second, unrelated merge-reconciliation (this same ID-renumbering pass) was then required against `origin/main`'s independently-merged T-372/GG-122 (`governance_scan.sh`) and T-371 (GG-119 resolution) work — full suite re-confirmed post-renumbering, see DECISION_LOG.md. |
| Status | **RESOLVED (code + epoch) 2026-07-15 (T-373)** — D1 and D2 both implemented and full-suite verified. `00_ADMIN/APR-0028...md` updated to reflect both items closed and the ID renumbering. |

A future session may want to consider whether `governance_scan.sh` should flag any APR/ADR document whose own Status field contradicts a RESOLVED/DONE cross-reference elsewhere — not built here, flagged for future consideration only. **RECURRENCE + STRUCTURAL FIX, 2026-07-17 (Terminal B, same-day follow-up):** the same failure class recurred immediately, in the opposite direction of the original instance — this time the source documents were correct (all four self-report ACCEPTED in their own Status fields) and `APPROVALS_REGISTER.md` was the stale side, with **four** ACCEPTED decisions entirely missing from the register: APR-0028 (ACCEPTED 2026-07-15 — three days stale by discovery), APR-0026 (ACCEPTED 2026-07-16), and APR-0025 + ADR-0047 (both ACCEPTED 2026-07-17 — same-day sign-offs whose sessions never wrote back). That makes four instances of this class (GG-108, GG-122, GG-126-original, this recurrence) — manual write-back discipline has empirically failed, and the future-consideration note above is no longer optional. Building the structural fix below then surfaced a **fifth, older instance**: APR-0023 (MLB G1 kill-switch drill, COMPLETE 2026-06-27) had zero register presence for three weeks, despite NBA's equivalent drill having carried its APR-0013 row since 2026-05-28. Post-fix it reports parity-clean (53 docs checked, 27 legacy-exempt). This closes the detection gap named in the original Status text; the recurrence is recorded here rather than as a new GG number, per this entry's own class-consolidation framing. **RECURRENCE, 2026-08-01 (sixth instance):** `governance_scan.sh`'s own register-parity check flagged ADR-0050 (T4M-PROJ flat-stake reactivation, `03_DECISIONS/ADR-0050_t4m-proj-flat-measurement-stake-reactivation.md`, ACCEPTED 2026-07-30) as having zero row in `APPROVALS_REGISTER.md` — the originating session (`session/20260731T020022Z-t4-reactivate`) never wrote back, same failure mode as APR-0023/0025/0026/0028/ADR-0047 above. The detection mechanism worked exactly as designed (that's how this was caught, same-session, before it went stale for weeks like the earlier instances); only the underlying discipline (write back at sign-off time) keeps failing. No further structural fix proposed; the scan already catches this class reliably, the gap is purely in write-back discipline at the moment of sign-off. |

### GG-128 — `session_delta.sh`'s OPEN-gap parser undercounted OPEN gaps (10 vs. true 18) — GG-122's fix class, never ported to this script, plus two further bugs

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-128 |
| Arm | Core |
| Category | Session-start tooling — ADR-0041's default delta-first retrieval path (`scripts/session_delta.sh`) silently showed every session an incomplete open-governance-gap list, the same failure class as GG-122 (which fixed the analogous bug in `governance_scan.sh`'s grep) but on a sibling script that was never touched by that fix. |
| What was missed | `session_delta.sh` Section 2b parses `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` for OPEN gaps via an embedded Python heredoc. Three independent bugs compounded: **(1)** `status_text.strip().upper().startswith("OPEN")` does not match bold-markdown-prefixed cells (`**OPEN — ...`), the exact defect GG-122 already found and fixed in `governance_scan.sh`'s grep (`^\| Status \|\s*\**OPEN\b`) — that fix was never ported here. **(2)** The original entry-extraction walked forward from each `Gap ID` match with an unbounded `rest = text[m.end():]` blob search for the next `| Status |` cell; entries with no Status field at all (GG-035/GG-036 use a terminal `| Resolution |` field instead) caused the search to bleed forward into the *next* entry's Status text, misattributing it. **(3)** Even after bounding the search per-entry, a blob-level `re.search` for `\|\s*Status\s*\|` could match an inline quoted example of bad Status-line text embedded in a different entry's prose — GG-122's own "What was missed" field quotes the literal string `"| Status | **OPEN — ..."` as part of describing this exact bug class, and that quoted substring matched before GG-122's real, later Status row was reached, producing a false positive. Net effect measured directly: the buggy script reported **10** OPEN gaps against the true, `governance_scan.sh`-verified count of **18** — an 8-gap (44%) undercount, meaning every session that used this ADR-0041 default path since its introduction was shown a materially incomplete open-gap list, silently, without a size or freshness check on the discrepancy. |
| When it should have been caught | When GG-122 was fixed in `governance_scan.sh` (2026-07-xx per that entry) — a fix to one of two scripts that both parse the same file for the same purpose should have prompted a grep for the sibling script (`session_delta.sh`) implementing the same logic. It was not caught then, nor by any of the sessions that ran the ADR-0041 delta-first path since (the discrepancy between the delta path's OPEN-gap count and `governance_scan.sh`'s own count was never cross-checked in any prior session log). |
| Phases it survived | Every session since `session_delta.sh` was introduced (ADR-0041, T-300/Window A) that used the delta-first retrieval path as its default session-start mechanism, through Phase 6/7 ACTIVE — an unknown but plausibly large number of sessions, none of which caught the undercount. |
| Why it survived | `session_delta.sh` and `governance_scan.sh` independently reimplement the same "list OPEN gaps" logic rather than sharing one parser; a fix applied to one silently does not propagate to the other, and nothing diffs their outputs against each other to surface a divergence. The undercount also degrades gracefully (a shorter list still looks plausible) rather than erroring, so there was no crash or exit-code signal to notice. |
| Impact | MEDIUM — no capital/gate impact (this is a retrieval-path tooling bug, not a state-of-record error in `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` itself, which was always correct), but real session-quality impact: any session that trusted the delta path's "10 OPEN gaps" figure without independently re-running `governance_scan.sh` was operating on a view missing 8 real open items, including GG-046 (the live watch item this very session's originating task was about) and GG-045/GG-124/GG-125 among others. Discovered incidentally during this session's own `/session-start` protocol run, not by any dedicated check. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-20, this session, while running the mandatory `/session-start` protocol's Step 3 (open governance gaps) and cross-checking the ADR-0041 delta path's output against `governance_scan.sh`'s authoritative grep — the two counts (10 vs. 18) did not match, prompting direct investigation of `session_delta.sh`'s Python heredoc. |
| Resolution | `scripts/session_delta.sh`'s Section 2b rewritten to walk `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` line-by-line (mirroring `governance_scan.sh`'s own `^\| Status \|` line-anchored grep) instead of regex-searching the raw text blob: tracks `current_gid` via a `### GG-\d+` header match, then requires `^\|\s*Status\s*\|` to match at true line-start before associating a Status cell with the current gap ID — this is immune to bug (2) (an entry with no Status field simply contributes no row, no bleed into the next entry) and bug (3) (an embedded quote mid-paragraph cannot match a line-start anchor, since a markdown table row must be its own physical line). The `startswith("OPEN")` check was replaced with `re.match(r"\*{0,2}OPEN\b", s.strip())` plus the same two literal-substring exclusions (`"OPEN / IN PROGRESS"`, `"template"`) `governance_scan.sh` already uses, fixing bug (1). Verified by re-running `scripts/session_delta.sh` against the live checkpoint: output is exactly `18 OPEN gap(s)` listing `GG-007, GG-027, GG-037, GG-038, GG-039, GG-040, GG-041, GG-045, GG-046, GG-056, GG-066, GG-072, GG-078, GG-094, GG-098, GG-105, GG-124, GG-125` — matching `governance_scan.sh`'s authoritative count and list exactly. Sections 2a/2c/2d of the script (unrelated bankroll/EXP-deltas/gate-progress logic) were not touched and continue to run clean. |
| Status | **RESOLVED 2026-07-20.** Fix applied and verified same session (see Resolution). Not yet independently re-verified by a follow-on session with fresh `git log`/push confirmation — standard practice per this project's own ID-provenance precedent (e.g. GG-127) is for the next session touching this area to confirm the fix landed and matches `origin/main`, though this is a lower-stakes verification than a cross-session provenance gap since this session has full local git/push access and commits its own work directly (no Cowork-sandbox handoff involved). No further action anticipated unless `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`'s entry format changes again (e.g. a third field name replacing both `Status` and `Resolution`), which would require revisiting this parser a third time. |

</details>

### GG-129 — Missing None-guard on `kalshi` client in T4 MLB live poll loop

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-129 |
| Category | Defensive-coding gap surfaced incidentally by `mypy --strict` remediation (GG-091), not by any targeted review of `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s failure paths. |
| What was missed | `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s `main()` sets `kalshi = None` on Kalshi client init failure and deliberately falls back to `"local_only"` order mode for that degraded case — but the live poll loop's per-cycle call to `kalshi.fetch_player_points_markets(series_ticker=SERIES_MLB_PLAYER_HITS)` had no guard against `kalshi` being `None`. Any T4 MLB session that started with a failed Kalshi client init (network blip, auth token expiry, etc.) would not degrade gracefully into local-only mode as the surrounding code's own fallback logic implies it should — it would instead throw an unguarded `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fetch_player_points_markets'` on the very first poll cycle and crash the live loop entirely. |
| When it should have been caught | At the time the `kalshi = None` / local-only fallback path was originally written — any code path that assigns `None` to a variable used later without a null-check is a defect at the point of the later use, not something that should require a separate discovery pass. Should also have been caught by any test exercising Kalshi-init-failure behavior, but no such test existed. |
| Phases it survived | Unknown — `run_t4_mlb_live.py` predates this session; the exact commit/session that introduced the `kalshi = None` fallback was not traced. Survived through Phase 6/7 ACTIVE (T4 MLB live paper trading) up to this session without being triggered in production, i.e. Kalshi init has not failed at startup during a live T4 MLB session to date — this is a latent defect, not one that has yet caused an observed VPS outage. |
| Why it survived | `mypy` in non-strict / partially-typed mode does not flag `Optional[KalshiClient]`-typed attribute access as an error unless `--strict`'s `union-attr` checking is enabled and the module is in scope for it; `run_t4_mlb_live.py` was only brought into strict-mypy scope as part of this session's GG-091 remediation pass, which is what surfaced it. No runtime test exercised the Kalshi-init-failure branch. |
| Impact | Would have been HIGH if triggered live: an unhandled crash of the entire T4 MLB live poll loop (not a graceful degrade to local-only mode as the surrounding fallback logic intends), silently ending live evaluation for the rest of that game-day with no automatic recovery — the kind of dark-pipeline failure CLAUDE.md's Step 4 operational health check exists to catch after the fact, but this would have caused the outage in the first place. No live impact occurred; found and fixed before any production trigger. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-20, this session, during GG-091's `mypy --strict` union-attr remediation pass (commit `185cb16`) — flagged by mypy as a `union-attr` error on the `kalshi.fetch_player_points_markets(...)` call given `kalshi`'s `Optional[KalshiClient]` type, then confirmed as a genuine reachable-crash bug (not just a type-narrowing formality) by tracing the `kalshi = None` assignment on init failure. |
| Resolution | Fixed same session, same commit (`185cb16`): added an explicit `if kalshi is None:` guard immediately before the poll-loop's Kalshi call, logging a warning and sleeping/continuing the loop rather than crashing — matching the graceful-degrade intent already implied by the existing `"local_only"` order-mode fallback elsewhere in `main()`. See `03_DECISIONS/DECISION_LOG/DECISION_LOG.md` 2026-07-20 GG-091 close-out entry for the full commit-by-commit remediation context this fix landed within. |
| Status | **RESOLVED 2026-07-20.** Fix applied and verified same session (full pytest suite: 2751 passed / 28 skipped / 0 failed, no regressions). Not yet independently re-verified by a follow-on session confirming the fix is present on `origin/main` post-merge — standard practice per this project's ID-provenance precedent (e.g. GG-127) is for the next session touching `run_t4_mlb_live.py` or T4 MLB live operations to confirm this guard is live in the deployed VPS code, not just in this session's branch. |

### GG-130 — `deploy.yml` dirty-tree guard failed a 5th time (whack-a-mole pattern across GG-073/GG-102/GG-104/GG-117 never fixed as a class)

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-130 |
| Arm | Core |
| Category | Deploy-pipeline gap — same category as GG-073/GG-102/GG-117, but this entry is about the *pattern itself* surviving three prior individual fixes rather than a new specific file. |
| What was missed | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`'s pre-pull dirty-tree guard (T-171 origin) hard-fails whenever `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` shows a modified tracked file on the VPS. Every one of GG-073, GG-102, and GG-117 was this same guard tripping on a *different specific file* written by a scheduled `deploy/cron.conf` job into a git-tracked path — each was fixed by adding that one filename to `.gitignore`. No prior fix addressed the general shape of the bug (anything tracked under a cron-output root will eventually trip this guard again), so a 5th occurrence — this one, surfaced via a "Run failed: Deploy to VPS" GitHub notification email for commit `f33b7a9` (2026-07-22 05:41 UTC, `approval-path-tests succeeded`, `deploy failed`) — was effectively inevitable. |
| When it should have been caught | At GG-102 or GG-117, when the second and third instances of the identical failure shape occurred — either should have prompted generalizing the fix (auto-heal any regen-root drift) instead of enumerating one more filename. |
| Phases it survived | 2026-06-24 (GG-073 fix) → 2026-07-08/09 (GG-102 fix) → 2026-07-13 (GG-117 fix) → 2026-07-22 (this occurrence), spanning Phase 6/7 ACTIVE, MLB paper trading live the entire time. |
| Why it survived | Each prior fix was scoped to the specific file under investigation at the time (matching GG-117's own "Why it survived" note about GG-102's fix being symptom-scoped) rather than the underlying pattern; no check exists that cross-references `deploy/cron.conf`'s output targets against `git ls-files` to catch a *new* instance before it causes a live deploy failure. |
| Impact | LOW-MEDIUM direct impact (a failed `deploy` step means the VPS runs stale code until the next successful deploy — not a betting-capital risk, since C4-C8 correctness is independent of deploy freshness once code is loaded — see GG-104 for the separate concern about services not picking up new code), but real operator-attention cost: this is the *fifth* "Run failed: Deploy to VPS" email for what is structurally the same root cause, which is what prompted this session ("Thing blows up my inbox whenever it happens"). |
| Discovery | 2026-07-22, Cowork session, prompted directly by the operator forwarding the GitHub Actions failure-notification email and asking for both a fix and a standing protocol. **This session could not read the actual failed-step log** — no GitHub API/`gh` CLI, no SSH to `157.230.91.33` (confirmed via a direct `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` probe, `Permission denied (publickey)`), no Chrome extension connected (`list_connected_browsers` returned empty), and no git network access at all (`git pull` failed with `could not read Username for 'https://github.com'` — even read/fetch, not just push). The diagnosis above is inferred from this repo's own recorded incident history (GG-073/102/104/117 all being the identical failure shape, most recently 9 days prior) plus the fact that the failing commit merged a large multi-file mypy-remediation PR — not confirmed against the live failed-step log text. If the real cause turns out to be something else (e.g. GG-104's service-restart class, or an SSH secret rotation), this entry's Resolution below still stands as a structural improvement but does not by itself explain that run. |
| Resolution | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`'s Deploy step rewritten: guard logic moved from a single escaped SSH command string to a `bash -s` heredoc script (readable, testable, no bootstrap dependency on the VPS having already pulled it). Any tracked file modified under `exp_output/`, `data/`, `logs/`, or `models/` (`REGEN_ROOTS`) is now auto-reset to the committed version (`git checkout --`) before the guard evaluates anything further, logged as `AUTO-HEALED`; anything modified outside those roots still hard-fails exactly as before, preserving the original T-171 protection. Verified against three synthetic test cases in a scratch git repo (not the real VPS, which this session cannot reach): (1) mixed drift — a regen-root file plus a genuine `src/` edit — correctly auto-healed the former and hard-failed (exit 1) on the latter; (2) pure regen-root drift across `data/`, `exp_output/<nested>/`, and `logs/` simultaneously — full auto-heal, exit 0, clean tree after; (3) no drift — immediate pass. Full incident history + diagnosis flowchart for future `deploy` failures written to `10_INFRA_OPERATIONS/RUNBOOKS/RUNBOOK_deploy-dirty-tree.md` (new runbook) so a future session/operator doesn't have to re-derive this pattern from four scattered GG entries again. Deliberately did **not** split the guard into a separate `deploy/deploy_guard.sh` — GG-128 (2026-07-20, this repo) found that duplicating identical parsing logic across two files lets one drift from a fix applied to the other; keeping `deploy.yml` as the single source of truth, piped fresh every run, avoids that plus the bootstrap problem. |
| Status | **RESOLVED 2026-07-22 (2026-07-23 UTC).** Session provenance (same pattern as GG-127): the fix was originally drafted by a Cowork session with no VPS/git-push/git-fetch access, which self-assigned this entry as **GG-129** against its stale local copy of this file. A follow-on session with push access confirmed against `origin/main` that GG-129 had since been taken by an unrelated, already-merged entry ("Missing None-guard on `kalshi` client in T4 MLB live poll loop," commit `a3539a8`) and renumbered this entire entry to **GG-130** (verified next-free at renumbering time) consistently across `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, the runbook, and this entry. Landed as commit `dc8013b` and pushed. **Live verification:** every deploy run after landing (`dc8013b`, `71932f7`, `cb64e6e` — 6 runs total across ~30 min) still hard-failed, but log inspection (`gh run view 29896018050 --log-failed`) showed the guard was working exactly as designed — it correctly refused to auto-heal a genuine non-regen-root drift (`scripts/query_orderbook_depth_mlb.py`, modified directly on the VPS 2026-07-19, outside `REGEN_ROOTS`) rather than silently clobbering it. That drift (plus a second, same-shape untracked-file collision on `scripts/vps_gg045_sample3.py`) is a distinct pre-existing incident, not a bug in this fix — split out and registered separately as **GG-131**. Once GG-131's drift was cleared from the VPS (both files confirmed byte-identical to their already-committed `origin/main` versions, so discarding was safe — no data loss), a fresh `workflow_dispatch` run (`29968399803`, 2026-07-23T00:12 UTC) passed clean end-to-end: `approval-path-tests` ✓, `deploy` ✓ (guard found zero drift, neither the AUTO-HEALED nor the hard-fail branch fired — genuine no-op pass), service restart ✓, HEAD-freshness verification ✓ (VPS HEAD landed on `cb64e6e`, both `t4-mlb` and `pmbot-web-dashboard` timestamps within seconds of the pull). This is the actual clean-pass proof the fix works; the AUTO-HEALED branch itself remains verified only via the three synthetic scratch-repo cases in Resolution above plus code inspection, not yet via a real regen-root-only drift in production — acceptable given the logic is identical to the tested no-drift/hard-fail paths, but worth noting if a future regen-root AUTO-HEALED case is ever observed live, record it here as confirming evidence. |

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>

| When it should have been caught | Immediately after the 2026-07-20 21:42 UTC merge of `ffa88b8` (PR #44) — a `ssh ... git status --porcelain` at that point would have shown the VPS diverging from what had just been committed, since the VPS's in-place edit and the committed version were about to become redundant duplicates of each other. |

The deploy guard (GG-073/102/104/117/130) is a downstream symptom detector, not a source-of-drift preventer — it correctly refused to proceed, but nothing upstream of it either prevented the duplicate edit or caught it promptly once redundant. |
| Impact | MEDIUM operator-attention cost (9 failed "Deploy to VPS" emails, several hours of my own session time spent diagnosing this as "is GG-130's fix broken?" before finding it was actually pre-existing, unrelated drift) plus a real verification blocker — GG-130's live-pass proof could not be obtained until this was cleared. No betting-capital impact: both drifted files were confirmed byte-identical to their properly-committed `origin/main` counterparts before being discarded, so no work was lost and the VPS was never running materially different code than what shipped (the in-place-edited file was functionally equivalent to what later got committed). |

No code change to the guard itself was needed; this was purely VPS-side operational drift. Standing process gap not yet closed by a durable fix: nothing currently reminds a session doing VPS-side one-shot/manual work to `git status` the VPS after the equivalent change is later committed through the normal workflow. Deferred — a future session could add a lightweight VPS drift check to `governance_scan.sh` or Step 4 of the session-start protocol (e.g. `ssh ... git status --porcelain` as a standing health check, similar in spirit to the existing dashboard OOM-restart-loop probe added for GG-118) rather than relying on a deploy failure to surface it. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-23 (drift cleared, VPS confirmed at `cb64e6e` matching `origin/main`, live deploy run `29968399803` passed clean afterward). The standing-process-gap piece (no automatic VPS drift check outside of deploy-time) is left OPEN as future work, not blocking — register a T-number if picked up. |

### GG-135 — MAIN book's variance × cadence trips the 20% drawdown kill switch ~100%/yr even at zero edge; risk config self-terminates before any edge can prove out

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-135 (renumbered from a session-local GG-134 — collided with a concurrent session's own GG-134, the `mc_empirical_bootstrap.py` engine coverage-gaps entry directly above, both registered independently 2026-07-23; that session's GG-134 landed on `main` first at commit `6b21f52`) |
| Arm | MAIN (T1/T2/T3) risk sizing / kill-switch geometry |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a risk-control mechanism (permanent 20% peak-drawdown kill, `risk.py` `_HARD_LIMITS["max_drawdown_pct"]`) interacting with real position-sizing/cadence to produce near-certain self-termination independent of whether the underlying alpha thesis (T1/T2/T3 calibration edge) is ever proven true. |
| What was missed | Every prior ruin-risk study (GG-071/ADR-0040, 2026-07-04) modeled the *positive*-edge case only — it asked "given a real, measured positive edge, what's the ruin probability," found 17-46% under the old Kelly fraction, and de-rated Kelly to 0.061 to bring 1yr breach to ~5.6%. No study had asked the *zero-edge* question until the empirical-bootstrap MC (`05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/MC_EMPIRICAL_BOOTSTRAP_2026-07-22.md`, 2026-07-22): replaying real resolved bets (not a fixed win-rate/payoff assumption) across three cohorts (strict epoch-8, post-fix e6-8, full-history) — spanning edges from −0.062%/bet to +0.006%/bet, i.e. essentially zero-to-negative — found **all three cohorts hit the 20% drawdown kill ~100% within a year** (strict-e8: 85.8% at 30d, 100% by 90d; post-fix e6-8: 100% by 365d; full-history: 100% by 365d). At MAIN's real ~1.08% per-bet σ and ~15.8 bets/day cadence, pure variance trips a 20%-from-peak drawdown eventually regardless of edge sign. Window B2's follow-on sweep (`05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/MC_SURVIVABLE_EDGE_FRONTIER_2026-07-23.md`, this session) quantifies the gap precisely: **holding today's real sizing/cadence/kill-switch config, MAIN needs a per-bet edge of roughly +0.169%/bet to hold 1yr P(kill) ≤ 10%** — about 27× larger than the best real cohort mean ever observed (+0.006%/bet, full-history). No plausible near-term calibration fix (Window A / APR-0025 shrinkage) closes a 27× gap in mean edge; the sizing/kill-switch geometry itself is the binding constraint, not the model. |
| When it should have been caught | Should have been asked alongside GG-071/ADR-0040 (2026-07-04) as the natural null-hypothesis complement to "what's ruin risk if the edge is real" — but that study only had a positive win-rate estimate (53.06%) to work from at the time and had no reason to model zero/negative edge. Structurally, this is the kind of question CLAUDE.md's Hard Rule 9 framing (design throughput, dynamically-routed sizing) should prompt an adversarial "what if the model is wrong" pass on, but no session-start check computes it — Q1 of the "ARE WE COMPROMISED?" protocol checks whether hard limits are *calibrated to the current system's scale*, not whether the *combination* of limits is survivable at zero edge. |
| Phases it survived | Since ADR-0040 landed (2026-07-04) through 2026-07-22 (~18 days) — the entire period MAIN ran under the de-rated 0.061 Kelly fraction believing the ruin question was closed, when the closed question was conditional on the edge being real and GG-105 (2026-07-2x, still separately open) had by then already found the deployed model's edge structure to be anti-predictive. |
| Why it survived | ADR-0040's forward-time MC (`mc_forward_projection.py`) drew every bet from ONE fixed win rate and ONE fixed payoff multiple, hard-coding the (unproven) edge as a clean IID +EV coin — it structurally could not produce a zero-edge scenario because zero/negative edge was never a parameter it accepted. The empirical-bootstrap replacement engine (`mc_empirical_bootstrap.py`) was needed to surface this, because it resamples real resolved bets rather than assuming a fixed edge — and that engine did not exist until 2026-07-22. |
| Impact | **HIGH — structural, not cosmetic.** As currently configured, the MAIN book's risk engine will very likely (≈100%/yr per the empirical-bootstrap MC) permanently kill the book on pure variance before Window A's calibration fix (or any future fix) can accumulate enough resolved bets to prove or disprove a real edge (GG-004's `clean_n ≥ n*` sample-adequacy gate). This directly threatens the G6 gate's ability to ever be evaluated on MAIN: the book self-terminates before the statistical test it exists to run can complete. T4 (T4M-PROJ) is not affected the same way — its per-bet σ is ~26× smaller (0.041% vs 1.081%), and the same MC found T4 survives near-zero edge with 0% kill in the post-fix cohort; T4 is edge-limited, not ruin-limited (confirmed independently by this session's Part-A sweep: T4's own min-required-edge is ≈ −0.0005%/bet, i.e. it already tolerates slightly-negative edge at today's sizing). |
| Discovery | 2026-07-22 (empirical-bootstrap MC, prior session) surfaced the structural finding; formalized and quantified as a registered gap 2026-07-23, Window B1/B2 (this session), per explicit operator instruction following the iteration plan (`ITERATION_PLAN_MC_REMEDIATION_2026-07-22.md` § Window B). |
| Resolution | Not fixed this pass — registration precedes remediation per this log's own Invariant. Window B2 (this session) quantified the frontier: at zero-to-near-zero edge, cutting MAIN's Kelly fraction to ~10% of current is sufficient to survive (1yr P(kill)=1.2%), but cutting bet cadence to 10% of current is NOT sufficient (79%) and widening the drawdown kill to 50% is also NOT sufficient (71.5%) — because stake-size (Kelly) scaling hits total variance quadratically while cadence scaling only hits it linearly, and DD-width alone doesn't touch variance at all. This means **Kelly-fraction reduction, not cadence throttling or drawdown-switch widening, is the primary lever with enough leverage to matter** for MAIN's survivability absent a large edge improvement. Window B3 is tasked with drafting an ADR superseding ADR-0040 with variance-aware sizing once Window A's post-fix edge estimate lands (needs A2). Full frontier tables: `05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/MC_SURVIVABLE_EDGE_FRONTIER_2026-07-23.md`. **Addendum 2026-07-28 (Window B3):** A2/A3 (Window A) both FAILED the GG-105 monotonicity gate, so "once Window A's post-fix edge estimate lands" resolved to "there is no post-fix positive edge" — B3 was reframed mid-task from a point-Kelly de-rating to an edge-conditional framework and drafted as `03_DECISIONS/ADR-0048_edge-conditional-variance-aware-sizing.md` (PROPOSED): default `kelly_fraction=0` for all MAIN-book-model bands (T1_MULTI_DAY/T2_SAME_DAY/T3_PRE_TIP) plus T4M_PROJ, with reactivation gated on (a) a passing GG-105 monotonicity re-run reporting a validated edge and (b) a lookup against this gap's own B2 frontier table, re-confirmed by a fresh D2 (`mc_empirical_bootstrap.py`) run before any nonzero deploy. This closes the "safe pending edge proof" risk this gap warns against by construction (size=0 cannot self-terminate on variance), but does not resolve GG-135 itself — the underlying variance-vs-kill-switch geometry is unchanged, and this addendum records the sizing-side mitigation adopted while the edge signal (GG-105) remains unresolved. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (R1/T-398). ADR-0048 received operator/DS sign-off 2026-07-29 and was applied live the same session: `execution_bands.py`'s `kelly_fraction` and `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s `KELLY_T4` both set to `0.0` for T1_MULTI_DAY/T2_SAME_DAY/T3_PRE_TIP/T4M_PROJ, `logic_epoch.py` bumped 8→9, commit `6be807f` merged direct to `origin/main`. This closes the gap by construction (size=0 cannot self-terminate on variance) — it does not mean the underlying variance-vs-kill-switch geometry changed, and does not itself constitute an edge finding. Reactivation of any band remains gated on all three ADR-0048 §2.1 conditions (GG-105 monotonicity PASS, B2 frontier lookup, fresh D2 bootstrap re-run) — none has occurred as of this resolution. Historical record above (OPEN-period findings, B2 frontier, B3 addendum) is unchanged. |
| **Addendum 2026-08-27 (T-494, ADR-0058 reopen question)** | ADR-0058 proposes reopening T1 on nine game-market cells and explicitly deferred to this gap whether GG-135's ruin geometry — measured entirely on KXMLBHIT player-prop history — transfers to game markets (different variance, no lineup/scratch risk, far greater supply). **Method:** reused `mc_survivable_edge_sweep.py`'s `day_params`/`simulate_1yr_pkill`/`bisect_min_edge`/`sweep_lever`/`frontier_from_sweep` and `mc_empirical_bootstrap.py`'s `START_BANKROLL`/`KILL_DD`/`DAILY_BREAKER`/`SEED` unmodified, so figures are comparable to GG-135's by construction (`scripts/mc_gg135_game_market_variance.py`). No real T1 game-market positions exist (all nine cells `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), so a synthetic per-bet frac pool was built from archived quotes (`exp_output/PRICE_ARCHIVE/`, 27 files) joined to real resolved outcomes (`logs/t4_mlb_totals_outcome_store.jsonl`, 307/329 resolved; MONEYLINE/RUN_LINE reuse the same box-score ground truth as TOTALS since all three settle on one final score), at a $1-flat-stake-on-$1000-bankroll baseline (mirroring T4M-PROJ's real ADR-0050/ADR-0059 measurement-stake mechanism, since T1 has no real Kelly history on these cells) and net of T-488/GG-157's measured per-contract fill haircuts (MONEYLINE $0.0340, RUN_LINE $0.0515, TOTALS $0.0307). TEAM_TOTAL excluded — T-488 measured no haircut for it. **Finding 1 (variance):** net-of-haircut per-bet σ (log-return) is MONEYLINE 0.097%, RUN_LINE 0.138%, TOTALS 0.103% — 2.4-3.4× T4M-PROJ's real flat-stake σ (0.041%) but far below MAIN's real Kelly-sized σ (1.081%; not a clean comparator, since MAIN was Kelly-scaled and these are flat-staked). **Finding 2 (fill cost is not a footnote):** entry at observed mid-price is ~fair by construction (mean_gross ≈ 0, ±0.005%/bet), so the haircut alone drags mean_net negative for all three families before any model edge: MONEYLINE −0.005%/bet, RUN_LINE −0.021%/bet (worst — largest haircut relative to price), TOTALS −0.011%/bet. **Finding 3 (cadence is the dominant lever, and it's assumption-driven, not measured):** counting every priced strike-ladder contract as a bet massively overstates cadence for ladder families (RUN_LINE 104.6/day, TOTALS 157.2/day vs MONEYLINE 26.7/day) relative to the realistic "one bet per game per family" assumption, which is a flat 13.348/day across all three (307 distinct games / 23 distinct dates). At the inflated all-contract cadence, RUN_LINE and TOTALS show NO edge up to +2.0%/bet clearing 1yr P(kill)≤10% at kelly_mult=1×; at the realistic one-bet-per-game cadence, min-required-edge is *negative* for all three (MONEYLINE −0.0025%, RUN_LINE −0.0012%, TOTALS −0.0023%/bet) — each family's own observed net edge already clears the bar at 1× flat-stake sizing. The qualitative verdict flips entirely on which cadence assumption is used, and neither is a real measured T1 game-market cadence (none exists). **Finding 4 (edge-independence does NOT transfer — the key structural difference from GG-135):** at the all-contract cadence, sweeping edge scenarios at kelly_mult=1× shows max-surviving-Kelly flip sharply within a ~0.02-0.03%/bet band — from `None`/0.25× at each family's own small-negative edge to the 3.0× grid ceiling at +0.02%/bet and above. This is the opposite of GG-135's headline finding, where ~100%/yr kill held flat *independent of edge sign* because MAIN's real σ (1.081%) was large enough that no realistic edge scenario moved day_mu enough to matter against day_sig. Here σ is 8-11× smaller, so the same random walk is far more edge-sensitive. **This changes the shape of the argument**: on game markets, T1 survival is not a variance-dominated, edge-agnostic verdict the way GG-135 found for MAIN — it is a real question of edge sign/magnitude, meaning game-market commercial validation (once traded) is load-bearing here in a way it structurally could not be for GG-135's original finding. **What could not be measured:** true pregame decision-time entry price (used first archived quote as proxy), the `>=`-strike settlement convention (assumed, not verified against a Kalshi settlement spec), only 23 distinct price-archive dates exist (narrow vs. a season), no real T1 cadence to measure directly (both cadence figures are constructed), and a `RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply` in the unmodified, reused `mc_survivable_edge_sweep.py:108` at extreme kelly×edge grid points was observed but not independently verified harmless this session (did not appear to distort reported p_kill — overflowed paths read as very-large-but-alive bankrolls, never triggering a spurious kill — but this is an observation, not a proof). **Disposition:** answers GG-135's own deferred transfer question rather than a new phenomenon; amending here per operator instruction rather than opening GG-214, which is returned unused. Measurement-and-analysis-only; no `kelly_fraction` touched. Full output: `exp_output/T494_GG135_GAME_MARKET_RUIN/results.json`; script: `scripts/mc_gg135_game_market_variance.py`. |

### GG-138 — `build_t4_resolved_ledger.py`'s `pull_vps_cache()` fails silently on a fresh worktree (missing `mkdir`)

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-138 (renumbered a second time at merge, 2026-07-24 — originally landed session-local as GG-136 after a first renumber from GG-133, but at merge time against `origin/main` this collided with TWO other entries simultaneously: (a) the pre-existing canonical GG-136, T-396's `TODO_NEXT.md` archival-cadence gap, and (b) Window A1's shrinkage-discrimination finding, which had also independently and mistakenly landed on `main` as GG-136 via PR #53 — see that entry's own Numbering note, renumbered here to GG-137. With GG-137 taken by that renumber, this entry moves to the true next-free ID, GG-138, verified against the full merged range GG-124–GG-137.) |
| Category | Core — operational tooling reliability (VPS-cache pull path, `scripts/build_t4_resolved_ledger.py`) |
| What was missed | `pull_vps_cache(cache_path)` runs the SSH pull subprocess correctly (confirmed independently: standalone repro of the identical `ssh`/`scp` call succeeds, `rc=0`, full payload received) but then calls `tmp.write_bytes(result.stdout)` / `tmp.replace(cache_path)` without first calling `cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`. On a fresh git worktree with no pre-existing `logs/` directory (gitignored, so never checked out), the write throws — caught by a bare `except Exception: return False`, which surfaces to the caller only as `WARNING: VPS pull failed; falling back to existing...` followed by `ERROR: portfolio not found`, with no traceback and no indication the actual cause was a missing local directory rather than a real network/auth/remote failure. |
| When it should have been caught | Any prior session that ran this script from a freshly created isolated worktree (Hard Rule 10's default launch mode) — worktrees never inherit gitignored directories, so this is not a rare edge case but the expected state of every new worktree's first run of this script. |
| Phases it survived | Present since `build_t4_resolved_ledger.py` (T-254) was written; not previously surfaced because prior sessions using this script apparently always had a pre-existing `logs/` dir (shared `main` tree carryover) or pulled via a different path. |
| Why it survived | The bare `except Exception: return False` swallows the specific `FileNotFoundError` and reports it identically to an actual pull failure, so the misleading downstream message ("VPS pull failed... portfolio not found") reads as a connectivity/data problem, not a local-directory problem — nothing prompts a session to check `cache_path.parent.exists()` specifically. |
| Impact | LOW-MEDIUM — not a data-correctness bug (no wrong data is ever written; the pull genuinely fails-safe), but it silently blocks the VPS-pull convenience path for any fresh worktree until a session manually diagnoses and works around it by pre-creating `logs/`, which costs debugging time and could be mistaken for a real connectivity/auth incident. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-23, Window D (T-395 continuation / D1 harness validation) — diagnosed by reproducing `pull_vps_cache()`'s exact logic manually step-by-step after the standalone SSH call was confirmed to succeed on its own; root-caused to the missing `mkdir` before the write. Worked around by manually creating `logs/` in the worktree; the script itself was left unmodified as out of Window D's explicit scope. |
| Resolution | **Fixed 2026-07-29, G1 session (commit 343ce86).** Added `cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` immediately before `pull_vps_cache()`'s write, and narrowed the bare `except Exception: return False` to print the real exception type/message (and the subprocess's stderr on a non-zero return code) before returning `False`. The identical root cause — writing into `logs/*.tmp` with no prior `mkdir` — was independently reproduced in `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh`'s inline ssh-cache loop and fixed there in the same commit. Verified by deleting `logs/` in the worktree and calling `pull_vps_cache()` directly: no exception, directory recreated, live VPS pull succeeded. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (G1 session, commit 343ce86). |

</details>

### GG-139 — `session_end_prep.sh`'s Step 6 claim-row match was structurally broken (grepped for a string never written to the row)

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-139 |
| Category | Incremental architecture — the tooling built to make `/session-end` cheaper (Fix 2, 2026-07-24) introduced its own unverified bug |
| What was missed | `session_end_prep.sh` Section 6 ran `grep -F "$BRANCH" 04_EXECUTION/SESSION_CLAIMS.md` to find "this session's own claim row." But `claim_session.sh` writes rows as `\| timestamp \| range \| focus \|` — the branch name is never written into a row at all. On a real `session/<ts>-<slug>` branch this could only ever match by accident (if the slug text happened to appear in some row's free-text focus); on `main` specifically it degenerated into matching the literal substring "main," which appears throughout decades of unrelated historical rows ("merged to origin/main," "push to main," etc.) — dumping ~30KB of irrelevant history instead of "no match." |
| When it should have been caught | Before Fix 2 was merged (2026-07-24, commit `6c38e28`) — a single test run against a real `SESSION_CLAIMS.md` row would have shown the mismatch immediately. |
| Phases it survived | Zero sessions — caught on the very first live invocation of the just-merged `/session-end` tiering protocol, run directly on `main` at the user's explicit request to test-drive it. |
| Why it survived | Fix 2 was verified by inspection and a dry run during its own build session, but that dry run happened inside a `session/<ts>-<slug>` worktree with (evidently) no coincidental substring collision — the bug only became visible once run on `main`, whose branch name happens to be a common English word embedded throughout the file's own prose. |
| Impact | LOW — read-only precompute step, no data corruption risk; but the section was useless (or actively misleading, via the pasted wall of unrelated text) for every prior real use of `session_end_prep.sh` at Step 0, including the six close-outs it was used for earlier the same day. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-24, live test of `/session-end` on `main` (user-requested: "let's test it out now. /session-end"). Section 6 printed a ~30KB dump beginning with an unrelated 2026-07-07 T-247/GG-095 reconciliation row; traced to the grep pattern by reading `claim_session.sh`'s actual row-write format, which confirmed the branch name is never present in a row. |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED same-session.** Section 6 now extracts the session's own timestamp from the `session/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<slug>` branch-naming convention, converts it to the row's ISO format, and greps on that instead (unique per session, matches the schema `claim_session.sh` actually writes). When the branch doesn't match that convention (e.g. `main`, or any non-session branch), falls back to `tail -2` of the file with an explicit caveat, rather than attempting a substring match that was never going to be meaningful. `scripts/session_end_prep.sh`. |
| Status | **RESOLVED 2026-07-24.** |

</details>

Forward-looking impact: this is the one category A1 flagged as the most theoretically credible remaining lever for GG-105 (opponent starting-pitcher quality is a standard, well-motivated sports-forecasting signal), and it has been silently unavailable for the entire GG-105 remediation history to date — every session that treated "the current feature set" as exhausted did so without this category ever actually being in play. |

Full writeup: `05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/G3_GG141_OPP_SP_BACKFILL_2026-07-29.md`. Wired **proactively** into `generate_mlb_features.py` itself, immediately after the combined feature DataFrame is built and before the CSV is written — findings print to the cron log (same-day visible, not five weeks later) and are logged to the audit trail at WARNING severity via `AuditLogger`; non-fatal by design so a genuinely sparse-but-legitimate early-season column doesn't block that day's feature generation. Combined with GG-140 (calibration-layer levers exhausted) and T9 (existing-feature-set levers exhausted), the scoreable feature-level candidate space for a GG-105 fix is now exhausted — no further untested lever is currently identified. ### GG-142 — C4's minimum-edge gate tests `abs(edge)` on an already-direction-resolved edge, so the most confidently-wrong bets are the most certain to be approved; 46.1% of T4M-PROJ's clean epoch-8 book fired on negative direction-effective edge

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-142 |
| Arm | MLB (T4M-PROJ acutely; the defect itself is band-agnostic and sits in shared C4 code) |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a safety gate that is structurally incapable of rejecting the class of bet it exists to reject, in shared sport-agnostic code |
| What was missed | `c4_risk_engine/risk.py:594` gates on `if abs(edge) < MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE` (and `risk.py:412` mirrors it for the `edge_signal` audit field). The `edge` passed in has **already been direction-resolved** upstream — `run_t4_mlb_live.py:1055-1065` selects YES or NO and then computes `directional_net_edge` in that chosen direction's frame. At that point a negative value means "this bet is bad in the direction we chose", not "this bet is good in the other direction". `abs()` therefore converts a strongly-negative (bad) bet into an apparently-strong one, and the *worse* the bet the *more certainly* it clears the gate. `recommended_direction` is present in the forecast record but is only ever written to the audit trail (`risk.py:413,505,623`) — it is never used to validate the sign of `edge`. |
| When it should have been caught | At ADR-0020 (raising MIN_EDGE 0.02→0.04, which touched this exact line), at GG-087 (2026-07-05, epoch 2 — the change that made the T4 engine bidirectional and thus created the negative-directional-edge case in the first place), at GG-113/ADR-0043 (2026-07-15, epoch 4 — a dedicated audit of the NO-direction vig sign convention that examined the ledger-recording side of this same computation and did not check the gate side), or by ARE-WE-COMPROMISED Q1/Q5, which grep `MIN_EDGE` in `risk.py` every session and print the line without evaluating its semantics. |
| Phases it survived | Every session from GG-087's bidirectional fix (2026-07-05, epoch 2) through 2026-07-29 — including the entire GG-105 anti-predictive investigation (T-322 through T-400), which repeatedly measured T4M-PROJ's edge-tercile behaviour on a book that was ~46% composed of bets the gate should have rejected. |
| Why it survived | Three compounding reasons. (1) The check reads as obviously correct in isolation — "is the edge big enough" — and its defect is only visible if you know that the caller already resolved direction, which is 300 lines away in a different module. (2) The prior three sign-convention bugs in this family (GG-077, GG-087, GG-113) were all found and fixed on the **ledger-recording** side (`paper_trader.py::open_position()`); nobody carried the audit across to the **gate** side, even though ADR-0043's derivation shows the two must agree. They do in fact agree algebraically — `(mip - p_t4) - vig - fee` is identical in both — so the ledger's stored `fee_net_edge` faithfully records a negative edge for these bets, which is precisely the evidence that the gate approved them. (3) No monitor distinguishes them: `insufficient_edge` never fires for these rows, so the audit trail records them as legitimately APPROVED. |
| Impact | **HIGH — this is the entire measured loss of the T4 book, and it has corrupted the project's central commercial conclusion.** Measured on T4M-PROJ's clean epoch-8 cohort (n=518, VPS ledger cache 2026-07-29): 239 bets (46.1%) carry strictly negative stored `fee_net_edge`; all 239 are NO-direction; **239 of 239 have `vig > \|model_p - mid\|`** while **0 of 279** legitimate bets do (mean vig 0.1058 vs 0.0407). Mechanism: when vig exceeds the raw signal, `gross_edge = p - mip - vig` goes negative *because of vig alone*, the code reads that as "NO-side edge", correctly computes a negative direction-effective edge — and `abs()` rescues it into approval. P&L split: full book −$25.67 (−0.0496/bet); the 239 rescued bets −$34.99 (−0.1464/bet, bootstrap P(loss)=1.000); the 279 gate-valid bets **+$9.33 (+0.0334/bet, bootstrap P(profit)=0.892)**. **Removing the defect flips the book from negative to positive.** Consequence for governance: every artifact reporting "epoch-8 edge is negative on both books" — including `05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/MC_EMPIRICAL_BOOTSTRAP_2026-07-22.md` and the GG-004 T4M-PROJ line — is describing a defect, not a thesis. **The T4 live-latency alpha thesis must be treated as UNANSWERED, not answered negatively.** Compounding: `VIG_CEILING=0.30` (`run_t4_mlb_live.py:150-160`) was calibrated from 2026-07-02 production data, *before* GG-087 made the engine bidirectional on 2026-07-05, so it has never been calibrated for the NO side — the exact path where this defect lives. No live-capital impact (paper only). |
| Discovery | 2026-07-29, isolated worktree `session/20260729T054746Z-fable-strategic-analysis`, during an analysis-only end-to-end strategic review. Found by ledger-first reasoning, not by any scan: an edge-tercile monotonicity test on stored `fee_net_edge` showed T4's bottom tercile spanning [−0.296, −0.051], which should be impossible under a 0.04 minimum-edge gate. Traced from the ledger field back through `paper_trader.py::open_position()` (L462-468) to the gate at `risk.py:594`. The session-start protocol's Q1/Q5 printed the `MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE` line as designed and did not surface it. |
| Resolution | **Gate defect fixed 2026-07-29/30 (session `session/20260730T052831Z-r2-gate-fix`, R2, DS sign-off = operator 2026-07-29).** `risk.py` CHECK 3 changed from `abs(edge) < MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE` to a signed `edge < MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE`; the `edge_signal` audit-diagnostic field corrected identically. New CHECK 4b added validating `recommended_direction` against `gross_edge`'s sign when present on the record (catches a future GG-077-style direction/signal mismatch that a signed-but-consistent `edge` alone would not reveal). `logic_epoch` bumped 9→10 (`resolving_gap="GG-142"`, `bands_affected={ALL_BANDS}` — `risk.py::evaluate_forecast()` is shared, unconditional code with no band-gate around CHECK 3/4b, so every band's clean cohort re-accrues from this boundary, not just T4M-PROJ). New `ADR-0049` (Hard Rule 3 — does not amend ADR-0043/ADR-0045/ADR-0048). `tests/test_c4_risk.py`: corrected `test_full_no_approval_flips_probabilities` (previously encoded the bug — asserted approval for `edge=-0.15`), added `test_negative_directional_edge_rejected` and two CHECK-4b tests. Full suite: zero new failures vs. pre-fix baseline (differential `git stash` run). Commit `1b0a8f83d2d4b6294913b4f0864d04f41209d4bb`. **Remaining, not part of this fix's scope:** (c) `VIG_CEILING` recalibration on post-fix bidirectional data; (d) re-run `scripts/run_power_calc.py` and GG-105 tercile re-measurement against the fresh (epoch-10-clean) cohort before drawing any further T4 conclusion — both require live accrual under the fixed gate, which cannot happen while ADR-0048 holds `kelly_fraction=0`; (e) T1/T2/T3 exposure audit (measured pre-fix: 1 of 175 MAIN clean rows) — those bands share the same fixed gate as of this commit, no further action needed beyond monitoring their own epoch-10 accrual. |
| Status | **RESOLVED (gate defect) — 2026-07-29/30.** Sizing remains at ADR-0048 zero for all four bands; this fix is correctness for reactivation, not a re-activation. The "T4 edge is negative" premise in GG-135/ADR-0048's T4M_PROJ inclusion rationale was computed on pre-fix (gate-contaminated) data and must be re-derived once a clean epoch-10 T4M-PROJ cohort of adequate size exists — that re-derivation is NOT yet done and remains a live open item, tracked via GG-004/G6 sample adequacy against the fresh epoch. Does not change GG-105's status for MAIN/T1. |

</details>
