### GG-147 — `StagedOrderStore.stage_order()` rejected `kelly_fraction=0.0`, a second and independent blocking bug that would have zeroed T4M-PROJ's ADR-0050 reactivation via a different mechanism than the one the operator's own addendum diagnosed

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-147 |
| Arm | MLB (T4M-PROJ) |
| Category | Architectural placeholder / silent-swallow — a validation bound written for the Kelly-proportional sizing era was never revisited when a legitimate `kelly_fraction=0.0` fixed-stake mode was introduced (ADR-0050), and the call site's own error handling (broad try/except around `stage_order()`) converted a hard validation failure into silent no-op behavior indistinguishable from "the gate is just strict." |
| What was missed | `StagedOrderStore.stage_order()` validated `0.0 < kelly_fraction <= 1.0`, raising `ValueError` for exactly `0.0`. Every T4M-PROJ call passes `kelly_fraction=KELLY_T4==0.0` (ADR-0048, unchanged by ADR-0050 — see ADR-0050 §2's explicit statement that T4M-PROJ's Kelly fraction itself stays 0 throughout; only sizing mode changes). `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s `_run_cycle()` calls `store.stage_order(...)` inside a `try/except` that logs a warning and `continue`s on any exception — `trader.open_position()` is never reached on that path. Net effect: with ADR-0050's `fixed_stake_usd` bypass in `risk.py` correctly wired (verified separately, no defect there), every T4M-PROJ bet that cleared the risk-engine approval would still have failed to record a paper position, via the staging layer rather than the risk engine — the exact "empty cohort that looks like a strict gate" failure mode the operator's own addendum's Part A warned about, but from a cause the addendum itself did not diagnose. |
| When it should have been caught | At ADR-0048 landing (2026-07-29), when `kelly_fraction=0.0` first became a legitimate, load-bearing value for T4M-PROJ rather than an error condition — or by any test asserting an end-to-end path from `evaluate_forecast()` through to a staged order, which did not exist before this session. |
| Phases it survived | ADR-0048 (2026-07-29, R1) through this branch's first work block (ADR-0050 initial implementation, commits `b7ff281`/`c9c8263`) — the original `TestFixedStakeMeasurement` unit tests asserted correct behavior at the `risk.py` layer only and did not exercise `StagedOrderStore`, so this bug was invisible to that test suite despite sitting one call downstream of everything those tests covered. |
| Why it survived | Two independent silencing mechanisms stacked: (1) the validation bound itself predates the concept of a valid zero-Kelly fixed-stake mode and was never revisited when ADR-0050 introduced one; (2) `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s broad `try/except` around `stage_order()` converts any staging-layer exception into a logged-and-skipped no-op, which is operationally indistinguishable from "no bet cleared the gate today" — exactly the failure shape the operator's addendum's Part A already named as the project's central risk for this task, just realized through an unaddressed second path. A pre-existing test (`test_c4_staged_order_store.py::test_invalid_kelly_fraction_raises`) had encoded the old bound as correct behavior, so even a full-suite run before this bug's discovery would have shown "all green" rather than flagging the interaction. |
| Impact | Would have been CRITICAL if undiscovered before deploy — ADR-0050's entire purpose (accrue a clean T4M-PROJ cohort for GG-046) would have silently failed: zero positions recorded, zero data accrued, for an unknown number of game-days, discoverable only by manually checking `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` for new rows rather than by any log-level signal (the try/except logs a *warning*, not an error, and does not distinguish this cause from ordinary no-edge days). No capital impact (paper only) since it manifests as under-betting, not mis-betting. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-30/31, session `session/20260731T020022Z-t4-reactivate`, during the addendum's Part D verification-test-writing pass — an end-to-end test exercising `evaluate_forecast()` → approval → `StagedOrderStore.stage_order()` (the exact shape Part D.1 required) failed against the then-current code, surfacing this independently of the operator's own diagnosis. |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED, same session.** `StagedOrderStore.stage_order()`'s bound loosened to `0.0 <= kelly_fraction <= 1.0`. Two latent test regressions this fix necessitated were also found and fixed: `test_c4_staged_order_store.py::test_invalid_kelly_fraction_raises` (previously asserted the bug was correct behavior — split into a corrected invalid-range test plus a new `test_zero_kelly_fraction_accepted`) and `test_run_t4_mlb_live.py::test_fires_no_when_p_t4_clearly_below_mip` (asserted a stale pre-ADR-0050 sizing value, `$0.20`, that had been silently unreachable since ADR-0048 zeroed `KELLY_T4` — updated to the flat-stake value, `$1.00`). New end-to-end coverage: `tests/test_c4_risk.py::TestFixedStakeReachesStagedOrder` (2 cases). Commit `cafcf74`. See ADR-0050 §8(A′), DECISION_LOG.md 2026-07-30/31. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-30/31 (commit `cafcf74`). Live-deployment confirmation (that a real T4M-PROJ position is recorded on the first post-deploy live game-day) remains an open follow-up — ADR-0050 §8(D), item D.4, documentation-only and not CI-testable. |

</details>

### GG-148 — `logic_epoch.py`'s epoch-11 boundary recorded a stale `commit_sha` (`b7ff281`) that predates the two blocking-bug fixes (GG-147, contract cap) needed for epoch 11 to ever produce real data

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-148 |
| Arm | MLB (T4M-PROJ) |
| Category | Traceability drift — a `logic_epoch.py` boundary's `commit_sha` field is meant to be the literal commit whose behavior produced any row stamped with that epoch, but this boundary's field was never revisited after later commits on the same branch materially changed that epoch's actual sizing behavior. |
| What was missed | Epoch 11 was registered (R3, commit `b7ff2812d5471a33460b3853b53ed63c9bc5ce07`) for ADR-0050's `fixed_stake_usd` bypass. Per GG-147, that exact commit's `StagedOrderStore.stage_order()` unconditionally rejected `kelly_fraction=0.0`, so every T4M-PROJ call under `b7ff281` failed before a position could ever be recorded — zero real rows are possible under the commit epoch 11 pointed to. Separately, `cafcf74` (this session, later) added the contract cap (`T4_MEASUREMENT_MAX_CONTRACTS`, `measurement_stake_and_stratum()`), which changes the *stored size* on every sub-$0.10-entry bet relative to what `b7ff281`'s code would have produced had GG-147 not blocked it entirely — a sizing-path change that `logic_epoch.py`'s own stated convention ("any change altering a bet's stored edge/direction/size on the approval/sizing/execution write path requires a bump," established at the epoch-10/GG-142 boundary) would ordinarily require tracking. Neither change updated epoch 11's `commit_sha`, leaving it pointing at code that cannot have produced, and will never produce, any of the rows later stamped `logic_epoch=11`. |
| When it should have been caught | Immediately after `cafcf74` landed, in the same pass that wrote ADR-0050 §8 and registered GG-147 — the same session had all the context needed (both defects, both fix commits) and simply did not cross-check `logic_epoch.py` against them. |
| Phases it survived | The remainder of this session's work block: GG-147 registration, ADR-0050 §8 addendum, and the first DECISION_LOG entry for this segment all landed without this check. |
| Why it survived | `logic_epoch.py` is not in the diff of the commits that caused the drift (`cafcf74`) — nothing about editing `staged_order_store.py`, `run_t4_mlb_live.py`, or `paper_trader.py` naturally surfaces a stale pointer in an unrelated file, and no test asserts that a boundary's `commit_sha` is reachable/consistent with the code currently on the branch. This is the same class of gap as the R1 entry's rebase-SHA staleness (`DECISION_LOG.md` 2026-07-29 R1 row) — a boundary's `commit_sha` is a hand-maintained literal with no automated check tying it to actual HEAD state — but that precedent was about rebases changing SHAs, not about later same-branch commits changing an epoch's *behavior* without changing its *pointer*, so the existing precedent did not directly flag this case. |
| Impact | LOW in isolation (paper-only, epoch 11 had zero real rows under either commit_sha, so no existing data is mislabeled) but HIGH in intent — this is exactly the traceability guarantee `logic_epoch.py`'s docstring exists to provide (`CURRENT_APPROVAL_COMMIT` is read by verification tooling as "the commit that explains why rows from this epoch look the way they do"), and a future forensic session tracing epoch 11's behavior would have landed on `b7ff281` and drawn a wrong conclusion about why sub-$0.10 bets are capped or why any T4M-PROJ position exists at all. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-31, session `session/20260731T020022Z-t4-reactivate`, during the mandatory Q3/Q5/Q6 adversarial review ("ARE WE COMPROMISED?") deferred from earlier in this session — found by cross-referencing `logic_epoch.py`'s epoch-11 `commit_sha` against the GG-147 and contract-cap fix commits already known from this same session's own work, not by external report. |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED, same session.** Epoch 11's `commit_sha` corrected to `cafcf742ad2a5fd41c666a80c9d32b489b514b97` (`cafcf74`, full 40-char SHA), `commit_utc` updated to that commit's actual timestamp, and its description extended with a dated note explaining the correction and why it was folded into epoch 11 in place rather than bumped to a new epoch 12 (no real epoch-11 rows exist to protect from contamination under either SHA, since `b7ff281` produced none). `tests/test_backfill_logic_epoch.py` + `tests/test_check_epoch_activation.py` re-run clean (31/31); `scripts/check_epoch_activation.py --skip-vps` re-run: same pre-existing non-blocking stacking warning as R3's own run (epochs 9/10/11 all within the trailing 7-day window), no new warning introduced by this fix. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-31 (commit pending — see DECISION_LOG.md 2026-07-31). |

</details>

### GG-149 — 161 T4M-PROJ tickers held simultaneous open YES and NO positions (wash trades), and the existing per-ticker re-entry guard does not and cannot prevent this

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-149 |
| Arm | MLB (T4M-PROJ) |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a live-state re-evaluation strategy (T4's 45-90s cycle) can flip its own recommended direction on the same market between cycles, and nothing in the staging/execution path checked for an existing opposite-direction position before this fix. |
| What was missed | On the live T4M-PROJ ledger, 161 tickers were found holding both an open YES and an open NO position simultaneously (zero sequential — both open at once), a wash trade under Kalshi's CFTC-DCM rulebook (no manipulative intent — the model re-evaluated live state and took the other side without closing the first). 141 closed locked pairs / 374 legs, combined -$0.13 on $178.76 stake. Separately, 35 tickers carry opposite directions across the T1 and T4 books (a distinct, cross-process instance of the same underlying issue). Two problems: (1) measurement — 374 of 2,015 legs (18.6%) are deterministic wash pairs with zero edge information, contaminating any headline ROI/edge figure; (2) conduct — a hard control plus written policy is required before G6. |
| When it should have been caught | At T4's original re-entry-guard design (T-208/GG-050, T-225/GG-076) — those fixes addressed *duplicate identical-state* re-entry, not *opposite-direction* re-entry, and no test at that time asserted direction-awareness. |
| Phases it survived | T4M-PROJ's entire live paper-trading history through epoch 11 (ADR-0050 flat-stake reactivation) — the ledger accumulated 161 locked-pair tickers before this session's audit surfaced them. |
| Why it survived | Diagnosed this session: the existing `already_fired_game` guard (`run_t4_mlb_live.py`) is keyed on ticker as a bare string, but its blocking condition is `(h_so_far, ab_remaining)` state-equality — a live-state tuple with no direction field anywhere — and its source (`_reconstruct_fired_ticker_states`) merges open+closed positions, last-write-wins. An opposite-direction bet at a *changed* live state sails through by design (T-225's explicit intent was to allow re-entry once state moves), so the guard was never capable of catching this case regardless of how long it ran. |
| Impact | MEDIUM-HIGH: measurement (18.6% of legs are zero-information wash pairs, directly biasing any GG-046/EXP-T4-01 edge estimate computed over the raw ledger) and regulatory-conduct (wash trades are prohibited under Kalshi's CFTC-DCM rulebook regardless of intent) both require remediation before G6. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-31, session `session/20260731T020022Z-t4-reactivate`, via a timestamp-overlap query across the live T4M-PROJ ledger (per-ticker, opposite-direction, overlapping open intervals). |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED, same session.** Intra-book (T4 vs T4): before staging any order, check T4's own open positions for the same `kalshi_ticker` with the opposite direction; if found, SKIP (never close-and-reverse — out of scope, requires a separate ADR-0018-governed decision) and log `t4_offsetting_suppressed` with both edges. `logic_epoch.py` bumped 11→12, `bands_affected={"T4M-PROJ"}` only. ADR-0050 §9(h)/(i) pre-registers locked-pair cohort exclusion (both legs, retroactive+prospective) and suppression-count as a reported metric. 161 historical tickers (425 legs, open+closed) tagged via `scripts/tag_locked_pairs_t4_mlb.py` — filter-based exclusion only, no P&L altered. 8 new unit tests + full 203/203 T4 suite passing. See ADR-0050 §9, `logic_epoch.py` epoch 12, DECISION_LOG.md 2026-07-31. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-07-31 (commit pending — see DECISION_LOG.md 2026-07-31). |

</details>

### GG-152 — `BOT_ENV` vocabulary mismatch: `_kalshi_base_url()` silently routes any non-`"live"` value (including the documented `ENV-03`) to the demo sandbox

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-152 |
| Category | Silent-misrouting failure class — same shape as GG-141 (blank columns) and GG-145 (constant park factor): a wrong value that produces no error and is never asserted against. This one sits on the live-capital/order-submission path. |
| What was missed | `_kalshi_base_url()` (`kalshi_client.py:98-101`) selects the production base URL only when `os.environ.get("BOT_ENV", "paper").lower() == "live"`. But `.env.example:10` documents the project's actual `BOT_ENV` vocabulary as `ENV-01 (research) / ENV-02 (paper) / ENV-03 (live)` — there is no code path that ever produces the literal string `"live"` from that vocabulary. Setting `BOT_ENV=ENV-03` with intent to go live silently routes every authenticated call — including `submit_order()` — to the demo sandbox instead. No exception, no warning, no log line; the call succeeds and returns a normal-looking demo order. |
| When it should have been caught | ADR-0008 (order execution, authenticated endpoints) or whenever `.env.example`'s `ENV-0x` vocabulary was authored — the two were never reconciled against each other. |
| Phases it survived | Introduced at `_kalshi_base_url()`'s creation (T-111, 2026-05-31) alongside the ENV-0x vocabulary in `.env.example`; never triggered because the project has never run under `BOT_ENV=ENV-03` (no live capital yet, G6 not cleared). |
| Why it survived | Nothing asserts that `BOT_ENV` is one of the documented values; an unrecognized value falls through to the `else` branch (demo) with no logging. The only two BOT_ENV states exercised so far in this repo's history are the implicit default (`"paper"`, itself not in the documented vocabulary either) and `ENV-01` — never `ENV-03`, so the mismatch has had no live consequence yet. |
| Impact | LOW today (no live capital, G6 not cleared, `submit_order()` has never been called against a real `BOT_ENV=ENV-03` intent). **CRITICAL at G6**: if this ships unchanged, the first live-capital activation could set `BOT_ENV=ENV-03` exactly as documented and have every "live" order silently execute against the demo sandbox — the operator would believe capital is at risk when it is not, or worse, believe a demo-verified flow is production-verified when it has never touched production order submission at all. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-31, Phase 0-A raw-capture session, while investigating why the captured `/account/limits` tier read as demo-scoped despite `.env`'s `BOT_ENV=ENV-01` looking like a plausible "just read something" state — tracing `_kalshi_base_url()`'s literal `== "live"` check against `.env.example`'s documented vocabulary surfaced the mismatch. |
| Resolution | **RESOLVED 2026-08-01, operator sign-off obtained in-session (two `AskUserQuestion` confirmations — first approved this entry's originally-recommended shape, second approved a corrected shape after re-verification below).** **Correction to this entry's original diagnosis — it had the mismatch backwards.** Before implementing the recommended shape above, direct verification of every `BOT_ENV` consumer in the repo (`kalshi_client.py`, `run_paper_trade.py:55`, `deploy/cron.conf`, `deploy/setup.sh`, `deploy/healthcheck.sh`, `deploy/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`) showed the literal values actually consumed everywhere are `paper`/`live` (case-insensitive) — `ENV-01`/`ENV-02`/`ENV-03` are, and always were, human-readable documentation labels in comments/docstrings across ~30 files, never a literal value any code parses. `_kalshi_base_url()`'s logic was never the bug. The real defect was `.env.example:12` (`BOT_ENV=ENV-01`), which wrote the documentation label into the value slot as if it were valid — the one config file in the repo that got its own vocabulary wrong. Implementing the originally-recommended fix (teach `_kalshi_base_url()` to accept `ENV-01/02/03`) would have been backwards and broken every other real consumer, including the live cron pipeline (`cron.conf` sets `BOT_ENV=paper` literally). Actual fix shipped: (1) `.env.example` corrected to `BOT_ENV=paper` with a comment clarifying ENV-0x are labels, never values; (2) `_kalshi_base_url()` (`kalshi_client.py`) now fails loud (`ValueError`) on any explicitly-set, unrecognized `BOT_ENV` value instead of silently falling through to the demo sandbox — unset still defaults safely to demo, unchanged, so no back-compat break; (3) `tests/test_kalshi_client.py` updated — removed the stale `test_unknown_env_defaults_to_demo` (asserted the now-removed silent-fallback behavior) and added `test_unknown_env_raises` + `test_env03_label_raises` (confirms the `ENV-03` label itself is correctly rejected as a non-literal value). Verified: `tests/test_kalshi_client.py` 44/44 passing; full suite `pytest tests/ -q` → 8 failed / 2792 passed / 29 skipped, all 8 failures pre-existing GG-146 (`run_exp015.py:379` `ZeroDivisionError`, T1 `kelly_fraction=0` from ADR-0048, documented baseline in ADR-0050 §8(D)) — unrelated to this fix, zero new regressions. The `.env.example:22` venue-API-key/ENV-01 comment-vs-observed-behavior discrepancy noted in the original entry remains unresolved and is out of scope for this fix — do not conflate the two. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-08-01 (session `session/20260801T230707Z-session-bootstrap`). G6 precondition satisfied — no longer OPEN when live capital is authorized. |

</details>

### GG-155 — CLAUDE.md's "$500-$2,000" KXMLBHIT depth claim was never sourced and is contradicted by the first real measurement by roughly 2-3 orders of magnitude

**Status:** CLOSED-AS-ARTIFACT · **Severity:** UNSPECIFIED

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>


| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-155 |
| Category | Unsourced architectural claim — a specific numeric assumption embedded in CLAUDE.md's "Market efficiency gradient" section was carried forward across many sessions and used to justify a live position-sizing statement ("position sizing at $50-$250/bet is within the market") without ever being traced to a measurement. |
| What was missed | CLAUDE.md states: *"Kalshi KXMLBHIT lines at $500-$2,000 depth mean position sizing at $50-$250/bet is within the market."* This session (Phase 0-B, Step 0.9) ran the first-ever traced live measurement of Kalshi orderbook depth for the `PLAYER_PROP` family — which `KXMLBHIT`/`KXMLBHR`/`KXMLBRBI`/`KXMLBKS` classify into — sampling 20 markets via `GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook` (`exp_output/PHASE0_SURVEY/depth_sample.json`, `sampled_at_utc: 2026-07-31T20:13:03Z`). Result: only 3 of 20 sampled markets had a usable (two-sided) book at all; across those, **median depth within 5 cents of mid was $0.90, minimum was $0.00**. This is not a minor miss — it is roughly 550x below the low end of the $500 figure CLAUDE.md asserts, and the $50-$250/bet sizing conclusion built on top of it does not hold against the measured market. |
| When it should have been caught | At the time the $500-$2,000 figure was first written into CLAUDE.md — no citation, no script, no artifact was ever attached to it (confirmed by grep of the surrounding section and of `DECISION_LOG.md`; nothing traces this figure to a source). Per the standing "Verify External Claims" rule (this exact failure mode — citing a venue constraint as architectural rationale without sourcing — is the rule's own founding example, per user memory `feedback_verify_external_claims.md`), this should never have entered CLAUDE.md unsourced in the first place. |
| Phases it survived | Present in CLAUDE.md since at least the "Market efficiency gradient" section's authorship (predates this session); survived every subsequent documentation-remediation pass (2026-07-02, 2026-07-19) without being flagged, since none of those passes re-measured it — they only reorganized where other content lived. |
| Why it survived | No automated or manual check exists that traces CLAUDE.md's numeric claims back to a live measurement; the figure read as plausible (a specific, bounded dollar range) rather than as an obvious placeholder, so it did not trigger scrutiny the way a `# TBD` or stub comment would. |
| Impact | HIGH for any future live-capital sizing decision. CLAUDE.md's own text uses this figure to argue $50-$250/bet is "within the market" for KXMLBHIT-class markets — the measured reality is that most sampled markets in that family have no two-sided book at all, and the few that do average under $1 of absorbable depth within 5 cents of mid. Kelly sizing at the stated range would move these markets far more than the architecture assumes, degrading or eliminating edge before a position fills — the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md itself warns about in the same section ("Kelly criterion assumes infinite depth... position sizing... would move the market against the bot"), just with the wrong numbers. No live capital is at risk today (pre-G6), but this must be corrected before any G6/live-capital sizing decision relies on the old figure. |
| Discovery | 2026-07-31, Phase 0-B session, Step 0.9/0.10 (depth sample + gate verdict), cross-checked against CLAUDE.md while drafting `VENUE_REGISTRY.md`'s measured-depth section. |
| Resolution | `VENUE_REGISTRY.md` § V-001 updated this session with the measured figures and an explicit correction note (committed alongside this entry). CLAUDE.md's "Market efficiency gradient" section itself still contains the uncorrected $500-$2,000 claim as of this entry — it has not yet been edited, since CLAUDE.md's own preamble states architectural framing changes there require deliberate handling, not a routine session edit. Recommended next step: operator review of this finding, then a CLAUDE.md correction citing this GG and `depth_sample.json` directly, replacing the unsourced range with the measured one (or explicitly narrowing the claim to the families that did pass — `GAME_WINNER`, `PARTIAL_GAME_WINNER`, `TEAM_TOTAL`). Unstaffed, no T-NNN assigned. |
| **Update 2026-08-03 (Phase 0-G, T-411)** | The $0.90 figure above (and the "550x off" framing) is **not actually a KXMLBHIT measurement**. Direct inspection of `depth_sample.json`'s raw per-ticker samples shows the 20 tickers the `PLAYER_PROP`-family bucket sampled were **all `KXLEADERMLBHITS-26-*`** (a season-long hits-leaderboard series) — zero `KXMLBHIT` tickers. A same-shaped mid-slate resample (`depth/depth_midslate_20260803T233850Z.json`, 2026-08-03T23:40:53Z, T4M-PROJ live window) pulled the **identical 20 `KXLEADERMLBHITS` tickers in identical order**, confirming this is a deterministic sampling-methodology gap in `cmd_depth()` (no per-series balancing within a family bucket; `KXLEADERMLBHITS` alone exceeds the 20-per-family cap and starves out `KXMLBHIT`, which has 325 currently-open markets never once reached by this tool), not a one-off fluke. A **targeted** sample run directly against `KXMLBHIT` (20/20 currently-open markets from a freshly refreshed market list, same orderbook-fetch code path, t4-mlb confirmed active before/after, 0 anchored 429s) found: 20/20 usable, 0.5-1.0c half-spreads, **median depth within 5c of $4,313.72 — 431x the $10.00 gate floor, PASS**. `KXLEADERMLBHITS` independently fails the gate on its own thin-book merits (3/20 usable both pre-slate and mid-slate, 17/20 with no book at all) — that verdict stands, but it was never a KXMLBHIT verdict. Full delta table, FAIL-NOBOOK/FAIL-WIDE split, and the mandated TIMING-ARTIFACT-vs-STRUCTURAL verdict: `exp_output/PHASE0_SURVEY/MIDSLATE_VERDICT.md`. **This is a single KXMLBHIT sample run, not two runs confirming stability — CLAUDE.md's $500-$2,000 text is still not corrected pending a second confirming sample and operator review; do not treat $4,313.72 as a stable replacement figure yet.** |
| **Update 2026-08-04T00:04:50Z (Phase 0-G, T-411, same session)** | Second confirming `KXMLBHIT` sample run, ~14 minutes after the first (00:04:50Z vs 23:50:50Z), against a freshly refreshed open-market list (422 `KXMLBHIT` markets open at this point, up from 325). Result: **20/20 usable again, 0 FAIL-NOBOOK, 0 FAIL-WIDE, 0.5c median half-spread again — but median depth within 5c was $304.685, not $4,313.72 — a ~14x drop in 14 minutes.** Both runs clear the $10.00 gate decisively (431x and 30x respectively), so **KXMLBHIT's PASS status is now confirmed on two independent runs** — but the *magnitude* is not stable, it swung an order of magnitude in under 15 minutes. The same volatility shows up family-wide: a third family-level sample (00:03:56Z) found `TEAM_TOTAL` swinging ~67x between its two PASS points ($2,043.53 pre-slate vs $30.60 sample-3) and `GAME_WINNER`/`PARTIAL_GAME_WINNER` now FAIL on their two most recent, most temporally-adjacent points (pre-slate's PASS looks like the outlier). Full 3-point table: `exp_output/PHASE0_SURVEY/MIDSLATE_VERDICT.md` § "Third sample point". **Per the task's own stability rule, CLAUDE.md's "$500-$2,000" text is still not corrected** — decisive PASS is now confirmed twice, but a fixed dollar range would assert a stability neither run supports. |
| Status as of T-411 (superseded below — kept for history, not a live OPEN row) | unstaffed beyond this session's T-411 investigation. Not a G6 blocker today (no live capital), but must be resolved before any live-capital position-sizing decision for `KXMLBHIT`-class markets relies on CLAUDE.md's current text. Recommended resolution path at the time: (1) operator review of the KXMLBHIT-vs-KXLEADERMLBHITS conflation found this session — **now closed as a factual question** (KXMLBHIT is liquid, PASS confirmed 2/2 runs), the open question is purely how to phrase a stable CLAUDE.md range given ~14-67x intraday depth volatility observed across every family sampled tonight; (2) `cmd_depth()`'s per-family sampling should be fixed (per-series balancing) so the original conflation doesn't silently recur for any other multi-series family (e.g. `GAME_WINNER` also spans MLB+NBA+NFL+NHL+OTHER); (3) if CLAUDE.md is ever corrected, consider a range or order-of-magnitude statement rather than a point estimate, given the observed volatility. Both (1) and (2) done next session — see the T-412 update and final Status row below. |
| **Update 2026-08-04 (Phase 0-H, T-412) — CLOSED-AS-ARTIFACT** | Both remaining open items from the prior update are now done. (1) `cmd_depth()`'s per-series-balancing fix landed this session: `_balanced_sample()` round-robins across every series within a family instead of the prior `group[:args.per_family]` head-slice, which is the exact mechanism that let `KXLEADERMLBHITS` (a season leaderboard matched by an over-broad `PLAYER_PROP` regex on the substring "HIT") consume the entire `PLAYER_PROP` budget and starve out real `KXMLBHIT` markets. `FAMILY_PATTERNS` also gained a `SEASON_AWARD` family (`LEADER` pattern, checked first) so a leaderboard ticker can no longer be misclassified as a per-game prop at all — the collision is now structurally prevented, not just detected. Both changes covered by new tests (`tests/test_phase0_market_survey.py`) asserting balanced multi-series sampling and correct season-leaderboard classification. (2) CLAUDE.md's "Market efficiency gradient" section no longer states a dollar figure or a range — replaced with a mechanism statement citing this GG and the two T-411 KXMLBHIT reads (431x/30x the gate floor, ~14x apart in 14 minutes) as the reason no fixed number is safe to assert, directing any sizing decision to a live measurement (`phase0_market_survey.py depth` or the archiver's new `--depth-sample-per-family`, Task 2 this session) instead. **Root cause (for the record):** a measurement-tooling bug (unbalanced per-family sampling + an over-broad classification regex), not a finding about KXMLBHIT's actual liquidity — KXMLBHIT itself was liquid on every direct measurement taken (2/2 targeted runs, 431x and 30x the floor). **This closure is scoped to the sampler-bug/CLAUDE.md-sourcing question only.** It does not resolve, and should not be read as resolving, the separate open question of whether `GAME_WINNER`/`PARTIAL_GAME_WINNER` are reliably liquid — see the Phase 0 findings note in `MARKET_EXPANSION_ACTION_PLAN.md` (Task 6, T-412): those two families now have 2 FAIL / 1 PASS across three widely-spaced points, which is exactly the kind of small-n, high-variance read this GG's own history warns against over-reading in either direction. |

|---|---|

| Phases it survived | Untouched through GG-049 (T1 dark-pipeline detection), GG-108 (NBA log-path fix), GG-118 (dashboard OOM-loop probe) — all three added a detector for a *different* silent-failure shape (zero bets, wrong log path, crash-loop-under-is-active) but none check T4's own write-recency against wall-clock time. |
| Why it survived | Root cause: `site.api.espn.com`'s MLB scoreboard endpoint began returning `403 Forbidden` to the bot's game-ID discovery request at 2026-08-04 23:41:26 UTC and has not recovered — 723/723 discovery attempts failed, 0 successes since. Confirmed **not** an IP ban: a bare `curl` (no explicit UA) to the identical URL from the same VPS returns `200`, while `curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0' ...` to the same URL returns `403` — the block appears to key off request headers/UA fingerprint, not source IP, meaning the bot's HTTP client's current UA/header set is specifically what's being rejected. Because discovery never succeeds, the process never reaches any game-evaluation code path, so it writes nothing to `t4_mlb_cycle_log.jsonl`, `audit_mlb_t4.jsonl` (last write also 2026-08-04T04:15, i.e. before the 403s even started), or `audit_mlb_t4_edge_decisions.jsonl` — it just loops discovery failures forever, which systemd correctly reports as "active" since the process itself never crashes. |
| Impact | T4M-PROJ (the only live-measurement T4 band, currently `clean_n=157/n*=267` per Step 4's sample-adequacy scan) has accrued zero new evaluations for 24h+ of live MLB games, directly slowing its already-tracked path to commercial-validation sample adequacy (GG-046). Also directly relevant to **T-421** (this session): the cycle log this session is building a decoupled outcome-join store against is frozen at 64,396 rows as of this incident and will not grow via the daily re-run path until this is fixed — a fact this session's own deliverable's daily-backfill design must account for, not silently assume away. **Second affected consumer, found later in the same T-421 session:** `run_resolve_mlb.py`'s ESPN-fallback resolution path (`_espn_game_ids_for_date()`, used inside `fetch_actual_hits()` when both MLB Stats API attempts return `None`) hits the identical `_ESPN_MLB_SCOREBOARD` URL with the identical hardcoded `_ESPN_HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}` — a second, independent consumer of the same broken endpoint/header combination, not just `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s live discovery path. Reproduced from a network entirely outside the VPS (`curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0' <url>` → 403; bare curl and `python-requests` default UA → 200 on the identical URL), confirming the block keys off the UA string specifically and is not scoped to the VPS's datacenter IP — it will degrade *any* caller using this UA, regardless of source network. This means `run_resolve_mlb.py`'s resolution/backfill path (both the live 06:30 UTC cron and T-421's read-only historical backfill) silently loses its ESPN fallback for any row whose MLB Stats API lookup fails, with no distinguishing signal from a genuinely-unresolvable row. Not independently registered as a new gap — same root cause, same fix direction, folded in here rather than duplicated. |
| Discovery | This session (T-421, decoupled-outcome-store), 2026-08-05, while re-verifying a "last write 25.5h ago" observation flagged but left unresolved when the prior session-instance parked mid-task (`05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/T421_HANDOFF_PARKED_2026-08-05.md`) — re-checked after a full game night had passed and found the gap had grown to 43.5h with zero recovery, confirmed via direct SSH log/journal inspection and a live `curl` reproduction, not assumed from a stale note. |
| Resolution | **T-429 (2026-08-07):** confirmed live on the VPS — the bot's actual on-the-wire UA is exactly the literal `"Mozilla/5.0"` (not something stronger/different that would need "more" spoofing); direct Python reproduction on the VPS showed `"Mozilla/5.0"` → 403, an explicit empty-string UA → 403, and *omitting* the header entirely (`{}`/`None`, letting `requests` send its own default UA) → 200. Fix applied: `_ESPN_HEADERS` changed from `{"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}` to `{}` in both confirmed consumers — `run_t4_mlb_live.py` (module constant, 3 call sites: `_espn_mlb_game_ids_today()`, `_espn_game_status()`, `_espn_poll_once_mlb()`) and `run_resolve_mlb.py` (module constant, 2 call sites inside `fetch_actual_hits()`'s ESPN-fallback path). **Consumer enumeration (GG-072's rule), full list found:** in addition to the two fixed above, the identical hardcoded `_ESPN_HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}` pattern is duplicated in `run_t4_live.py` (NBA T4, DARK/FROZEN per operator directive — not fixed, out of scope) and inline in `run_paper_trade.py` (NBA — not fixed, out of scope), plus six one-off/investigation scripts not in the live cron path (`scripts/reconstruct_mlb_score_diff.py`, `scripts/poll_and_resolve_g1.py`, `scripts/vps_gg045_sample3.py`, `scripts/build_tss_cache.py`, `scripts/fetch_hits_unblocked_network.py`) — left as-is, not part of any active pipeline. **This constant is copy-pasted across at least 4 files with no shared HTTP helper backing it** — no C1/ingestion-level helper was found to centralize it in; that absence is itself worth noting for future ingestion work (a shared client would have made this a one-file fix instead of a grep-and-enumerate exercise) but centralizing it is out of this task's scope and not done here. `scripts/repair_stuck_mlb_positions.py` had already independently discovered and monkeypatched around this exact issue in-process (`rrm._ESPN_HEADERS = {}`) without touching the on-disk constant — that finding corroborated the fix before it was applied. VPS deployment and live recovery proof (new cycle-log row, `audit_mlb_t4.jsonl` writing again, stable `NRestarts`) tracked separately in this same T-429 session. **Addendum (T-429, same session, found during pre-merge full-suite triage):** a third consumer of the identical hardcoded `_ESPN_HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}` pattern was found in `tests/integration/test_mlb_api_connectivity.py` — a live-network integration test asserting the ESPN scoreboard endpoint returns `200` with this exact header set, which was failing with a literal `403 == 200` assertion failure (not a flaky network artifact — reproducible on every run) for the same UA-fingerprint reason as the two production consumers above. Fixed identically (`_ESPN_HEADERS = {}`), closing this gap's consumer enumeration per GG-072's "enumerate every consumer" rule — no shared HTTP helper exists, so this is a third independent copy-paste site, not a duplicate report of the same fix. |
| Status | RESOLVED (2026-08-07, T-429) — code fix applied and verified locally (both consumers); VPS deploy confirmed (`t4-mlb` restarted, `NRestarts=0`); live recovery proof confirmed via `t4_mlb_live_cron.log` showing clean ESPN discovery (correct game IDs/statuses, zero 403s) on every ~60s poll since the 05:06:47Z restart. Cycle-log/audit-log new-row write is pending only on tonight's games going live (all 15 tracked games were pregame `STATUS_SCHEDULED` at check time, 05:12 UTC) — that is expected idle behavior, not a residual failure; see top-of-entry Recovery proof note. |

### GG-169 — `claim_session.sh`'s collision check cannot distinguish "actively claimed" from "pre-reserved backlog ID awaiting staffing," blocking the exact workflow the project uses to hand off follow-on work

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-169 |
| Category | Incremental architecture — the collision check (GG-107's fix) was designed for one failure mode and silently also blocks a legitimate, common pattern it never considered. |
| What was missed | T-429's session closed by minting T-431 in `TODO_NEXT.md`/`SESSION_CLAIMS.md` as a named, unstaffed follow-on task — the project's normal pattern for handing off known future work. When this session (T-431) tried to formally claim that exact pre-reserved ID via `scripts/claim_session.sh "..." "T-431"`, it refused with `COLLISION: T-431 already appears in 04_EXECUTION/TODO_NEXT.md` / `SESSION_CLAIMS.md` — because `check_id_collision.sh` (`scripts/lib/check_id_collision.sh`) treats *any* prior appearance of an ID as a collision, with no way to tell "already actively claimed by a live/competing session" (the real GG-107 failure mode) apart from "previously reserved by a closed session specifically so a later session could staff it" (this case). |
| When it should have been caught | At GG-107's original fix — the script's design should have anticipated that this project routinely mints forward-referencing IDs (`T-431` inside T-429's own closure text) as part of normal handoff, since `04_EXECUTION/TODO_NEXT.md` and `SESSION_CLAIMS.md` closure rows do this constantly. |
| Phases it survived | Unexercised since GG-107's fix — likely because most claims to date used freshly-minted IDs rather than staffing a pre-reserved backlog ID from a prior session's closure note. |
| Why it survived | `check_id_collision.sh` does a flat substring/word-boundary grep for the ID across all three registries and returns collision on any hit; it has no notion of claim state (open/staffed vs. closed/reserved-for-later) to distinguish the two cases. |
| Impact | LOW, procedural: this session worked around it by hand-appending the claim row and pushing directly to `origin/main` (with operator confirmation, since the harness's own permission classifier treats a direct push to `main` as requiring explicit approval) rather than via the script. No data risk — but the script's collision guarantee (GG-107's actual purpose) was bypassed for this claim, and every future session that staffs a pre-reserved backlog ID will hit the same false positive and need the same manual workaround unless fixed. |
| Discovery | T-431 (2026-08-10/11), session-start Step 0, while claiming the exact ID T-429 had reserved for it — register-and-stop per Hard Rule 11, this task's deliverable is the B5 disagreement root cause, not claim tooling. |
| Resolution | Fixed by T-460 (2026-08-17, commit `d066bb5`, branch `session/20260817T230233Z-housekeeping-batch`). `scripts/lib/check_id_collision.sh` now distinguishes a canonical registry reference (GG-/ADR- entries, or a `TODO_NEXT.md`/backlog line with no matching active claim row) from an actual active claim: only a live, unclosed `SESSION_CLAIMS.md` id-column row counts as a collision. The T-247 race protection is preserved structurally — `claim_session.sh`'s fetch/rebase→check→push-retry sequence still serializes concurrent claims on the active-row check, so two sessions still cannot silently grab the same live ID; a closed/reserved-but-unstaffed ID is simply no longer treated as occupied. Covered by `tests/test_claim_session_collision.py`. |
| Status | RESOLVED — T-460, 2026-08-17. |

</details>

Note this ruling unblocks Phase 1 *itself* (abstraction repair, no new markets) — it does not retroactively pass PARTIAL_GAME_WINNER/PLAYER_PROP's depth FAILs from T-436; those remain live build-order inputs for whichever Phase 1 sequences new-market work later. |

### GG-173 — `test_t187e_mlb_resolve.py::TestFetchMlbHits::test_multiple_splits_matches_correct_date` computes its two mocked dates from the live clock at two different times (module-import time vs. test-execution time), so a CI run whose collection-to-execution window straddles UTC midnight can make both dates collide and the test fail

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-173 |
| Category | Test-infrastructure flakiness — a test asserting on two independently-computed `date.today()`-derived values with no fixed/frozen clock. |
| What was missed | `tests/test_t187e_mlb_resolve.py` line 31 sets a module-level constant `PAST_DATE = (date.today() - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()`, evaluated once at test-collection/import time. `test_multiple_splits_matches_correct_date` (~line 405) separately computes `two_days_ago = (date.today() - timedelta(days=2)).isoformat()` inside the test body, evaluated at test-execution time. The test mocks an API response with one split at each date and asserts `_fetch_mlb_hits` returns the split matching `PAST_DATE`. If real wall-clock UTC midnight passes between module import and this test's execution — as it did during PR #72's CI run (job `31652742167`; test executed at `2026-08-13T00:00:45Z` per the failure log, well after suite collection at `~2026-08-12T23:58Z`) — `PAST_DATE` (frozen at Aug-12 minus 1 day = Aug-11) and `two_days_ago` (computed fresh at Aug-13 minus 2 days = Aug-11) both resolve to the same date string. The two mocked splits collide on date, the function under test legitimately cannot disambiguate them, and the assertion fails (`assert 0.0 == 3.0`) — not because of a production-code defect. |
| When it should have been caught | Test authoring/review — any test asserting date-comparison logic should freeze or fix its clock references (e.g. `freezegun`, or compute both dates from a single `date.today()` call) rather than deriving two dates from two independent live-clock reads. |
| Phases it survived | Present since this test file's introduction (GG-069/T-221 era); never triggered before because it requires the rare coincidence of a CI run's test-collection-to-this-test's-execution window straddling a UTC midnight boundary. |
| Why it survived | Passes deterministically in every run that doesn't straddle midnight — which is the overwhelming majority of runs, local and CI alike. Local full-suite runs during this session (both pre- and post-merge) and an isolated re-run of just this test all passed, since none of them crossed midnight during execution. No CI/local timing-skew check exists to catch this class of test. |
| Impact | Blocked PR #72's merge (STANDARD-tier `/session-end` Step 8) via a required CI check failure unrelated to that PR's actual content (`market_type_registry.py`, T-439) — a false-negative gate. Re-running the same CI job outside the midnight window (`gh run rerun 31652742167 --failed`) is expected to pass, confirming this diagnosis; no production code was touched to work around it. Low severity: no live-trading or data-integrity impact, purely a test-fragility/CI-friction issue, and the failure window is astronomically narrow (~seconds per day, only when a CI run's timing happens to straddle it). |
| Discovery | T-439 close-out (2026-08-12/13), while investigating a CI-only failure that did not reproduce locally in full-suite or isolated runs. Root cause identified by comparing the failing test's CI execution timestamp against its two date-construction call sites, not by reproducing the failure directly. |
| Resolution | Fixed by T-460 (2026-08-17, commit `d066bb5`, branch `session/20260817T230233Z-housekeeping-batch`). Matched the existing fix pattern already established in `test_backfill_logic_epoch.py` rather than inventing a second approach — both mocked dates now derive from a single shared `date.today()` call, eliminating the module-import-time vs. test-execution-time split that could straddle UTC midnight. |
| Status | RESOLVED — T-460, 2026-08-17. |

</details>

### GG-176 — `scripts/lib_chain_archive.py`'s `archive_chain()` silently no-ops whenever a nav file's `**Last reviewed` chain has exactly 1 entry, so the pointer never advances and every session sees a stale "Last reviewed" line

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-176 |
| Category | Tooling defect — a generator step silently no-ops instead of doing the one thing its caller (the `/session-end` skill) documents it as doing. |
| What was missed | `scripts/lib_chain_archive.py`'s `archive_chain()` (lines ~83-84): `if n_entries <= 1: return None`, with the inline rationale "avoids archiving a single-entry 'chain' every session when there's nothing to compress yet." The intent (don't archive a trivial 1-line chain) is reasonable, but the implementation conflates "nothing to archive" with "nothing to update" — it also skips writing the *current* session's status line into that single entry, so the pointer itself never advances. As of this session, `TODO_NEXT.md`, `MEMORY_BANK.md`, and `PLAN.md` all sit at exactly 1 `**Last reviewed` entry each (dated 2026-08-10T23:49:00Z, T-434) and `scripts/generate_session_artifacts.py` printed `"nothing to collapse (0 or 1 chain entries)"` for all three on this session's real run — meaning every session since T-434 that ran `/session-end` has had its chain-advance step silently no-op, and the skill's own text ("that line is now collapsed and regenerated automatically by Step 6's `scripts/generate_session_artifacts.py` call") is not true under this condition. |
| When it should have been caught | At T-430 (2026-08-07), when `generate_session_artifacts.py` and `lib_chain_archive.py` were built — the single-entry boundary case was evidently considered (the inline comment shows deliberate intent) but the consequence (permanent staleness once a file drops to 1 entry) was not traced through. |
| Phases it survived | At least 3 sessions post-T-434 (2026-08-10) that ran `/session-end` against these three files, including T-443/this session, all silently affected. |
| Why it survived | The generator's console output ("nothing to collapse") reads as a benign no-op rather than a failure, and no prior session's close-out cross-checked the "Last reviewed" line's actual timestamp against the session's own date after running the generator. |
| Impact | Cosmetic/navigational only — the three nav files' "Last reviewed" pointer understates recency (currently showing T-434/2026-08-10 despite multiple sessions of real edits since), which could mislead a future session into under-trusting how current a file's content is, or over-relying on `session_delta.sh`'s checkpoint diff (which is unaffected — checkpoint pointer writes are a separate mechanism, confirmed still working correctly this session) instead of the chain line. No data loss, no incorrect archival. |
| Discovery | T-443 (2026-08-13), during `/session-end` Step 6-gen — the real (non-dry-run) `generate_session_artifacts.py` run printed the no-op message for all three files; source inspection of `lib_chain_archive.py` confirmed the `n_entries <= 1` short-circuit as the cause. Out of T-443's declared scope (merge/checkbox task); registered and not fixed, per Hard Rule 11. |
| Resolution | Fixed by T-460 (2026-08-17, commit `d066bb5`, branch `session/20260817T230233Z-housekeeping-batch`), closing T-447. `archive_chain()`'s single short-circuit was split into two independent behaviors: archiving old entries into `archive_path` still skips at `n_entries<=1` (correct as-is, nothing worth archiving), but the nav-file rewrite to `new_current_line` now always happens whenever a chain span exists at all — the pointer advances every session regardless of chain length. `scripts/generate_session_artifacts.py`'s caller message updated to match (no longer claims "nothing to collapse" when the current line was in fact just updated). Covered by 4 new tests in `tests/test_lib_chain_archive.py` (no-chain, single-entry, multi-entry regression, repeated-call idempotency). |
| Status | RESOLVED — T-460, 2026-08-17. |

</details>

| What was missed | `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` assertion N (`ticker_player_token_consistent`), band T4M-PROJ: `n_applicable=2644, n_violations=1 (0.04%)`, `first_seen_epoch=12=last_seen_epoch=12`. Example: `player_block=TEXNLOPE tok1=NLOPEZ tok2=NLOPEZ name=Nicky Lopez`. The ticker embeds a short player token (`NLOPE`) that the assertion's tokenizer doesn't reconcile cleanly against the stored full name for this specific player, despite the position's ticker/name pairing itself being correct. |
| When it should have been caught | Not applicable as a process-gate miss — assertion N is itself the catch mechanism (Q7, ALARM-ONLY per CLAUDE.md). This entry exists because the violation is live and unregistered, not because a gate failed to run. |
| Phases it survived | Present since at least epoch 12 (current logic epoch); single row, isolated. |
| Why it survived | Extremely low rate (1/2644 in this band) on a short, ambiguous token (`NLOPE` collides with multiple plausible name-abbreviation schemes); no prior session's pytest/invariant run flagged it as a stop condition because assertion N was added in a later retrofit (post-T-432's original A-H baseline) with no documented "was this ever clean" checkpoint to compare against. |
| Impact | None observed — the underlying position's ticker-to-player mapping is correct per the example (`Nicky Lopez` ↔ `NLOPE`); this is the assertion's tokenizer failing to confirm a true match, not a mismatched position. No P&L or sizing impact identified. |
| Discovery | T-443 (2026-08-13), STEP 2 (post-merge invariant-suite verification after merging T-442/PR #73). Out of T-443's declared scope (merge + checkbox verification only); registered and not touched, per Hard Rule 11 and the task's explicit instruction that a new-violating assertion is a stop-and-register condition rather than a fix-in-session condition. |
| Resolution | Fixed by T-460 (2026-08-17, commit `773c20d`, branch `session/20260817T230233Z-housekeeping-batch`). Root cause: Kalshi's own ticker generation truncates some player tokens to fit the field (`NLOPEZ`→`NLOPE` for Nicky Lopez) — the ticker-embedded token can be a shortened *prefix* of the full computed token, not just possibly preceded by extra characters (a team code), which the pre-existing `endswith` check already handled. Added `_token_matches()`: tries progressively shorter suffixes of the computed token down to `MIN_TRUNCATED_TOKEN_LEN=5` (first initial + 4 surname letters) before giving up — a general truncation-tolerance rule per the task's instruction to fix the matcher, not special-case the name. Strict superset of the old exact match, so no existing pass can regress; added a floor test confirming over-short truncations still flag. Covered by new tests in `tests/test_assert_ledger_invariants.py`. |
| Status | RESOLVED — T-460, 2026-08-17. |

</details>

Not previously enumerated by name; prior sessions (including the T-444 baseline this task continues) worked from the pass/skip/fail totals only ("arithmetic on the totals"), never the per-test dependency list. |

### GG-180 — T-427 replay gate only ever exercised T4M-PROJ and T1 (via real ledger data); T2, T3, and the band=None fallthrough had zero replay coverage, and T2/T3 can never get real coverage since their kelly_fraction=0.0 means they never reach `open_position()`'s write path

**Status:** RESOLVED (partial) — synthetic fixture coverage added for T1/T2/T3/None at current epoch; the real-ledger T1 gap (zero T1 positions at current logic_epoch 12) remains, mitigated but not eliminated, by the synthetic fixture · **Severity:** MEDIUM

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-180 |
| Category | Test/gate coverage gap — a determinism/replay gate whose branch coverage silently tracked only the bands that happened to have real trading history, with no mechanism to detect or flag the bands it never touched. |
| What was missed | `scripts/replay_harness_t427.py`'s `branch_for()` classified every non-YES, non-T4M-PROJ, non-T1 position into a single `ELSE-fallthrough` bucket. Direct measurement this session: across both MLB portfolio files (485 + 2994 = 3479 positions, all epochs), band counts were `T1=483, T2=2, T4M-PROJ=2629, None=365`, and **T3=0 — zero T3 positions have ever existed in either ledger.** T2 has exactly 2 historical positions, both at `logic_epoch=2` (2026-07-05), predating ADR-0048's `kelly_fraction=0.0` zeroing (GG-135) — T2 has had genuinely zero positions at any epoch since. At the **current** logic_epoch (12), band counts across both files are `{T4M-PROJ: 765}` — zero T1, T2, T3, or None-band positions exist at the live epoch, meaning the replay gate's real-ledger data provided **zero current-epoch coverage for every band except T4M-PROJ**, even though box 1.6's PASSED verdict (commit `ac5414a`, T-444) was read as validating "the replay gate" generally. T2 and T3 additionally can never be closed by waiting for more real data: `kelly_fraction=0.0` (ADR-0048/GG-135) means every T2/T3 forecast sizes to $0 and never reaches `open_position()`'s dict-literal write — synthetic fixtures are not a stopgap for these two bands, they are the only mechanism real coverage will ever have. |
| When it should have been caught | At T-427 (harness authorship) or T-444 (box 1.6 verdict) — either point where "the replay gate passed" was read as validating cross-band determinism rather than the specific bands the available ledger data happened to contain. |
| Phases it survived | From T-427's original authorship through box 1.6's PASSED verdict (T-444) to this session (T-450) — at least two prior sessions treated the gate's pass as full-band evidence without checking which bands the input data actually exercised. |
| Why it survived | `ELSE-fallthrough` reads as a residual catch-all, not as "every band except two has zero test coverage" — the label gave no visibility into which real bands it was hiding, and no prior session cross-tabulated `band` against `logic_epoch` on the source ledgers to check current-epoch coverage per band. |
| Impact | Analytical/gate-integrity only, not a live trading defect — T2/T3 are already sized to zero (ADR-0048) so no capital was ever at risk from the coverage gap itself. The impact is that a future regression in `open_position()`'s handling of T1/T2/T3/None-band positions (e.g. a change to `_directional_edge()`'s vig-coefficient lookup, or the `_NO_DIRECTION_VIG_COEFFICIENT` dict) could pass the T-427 gate undetected for any of those four branches, since real ledger data alone could never exercise them at the current epoch. |
| Discovery | T-450 (2026-08-14), this session — explicit task: extend the T-427 harness with synthetic current-epoch fixtures for T1/T2/T3/None, discovered and quantified this gap as the task's own stated premise, then independently re-verified the underlying counts (485+2994 positions, per-band, per-epoch) directly against the source ledger JSON rather than trusting the figure as given. |
| Resolution | `scripts/replay_harness_t427.py` extended (this session): `branch_for()` now labels T2/T3/None-band positions distinctly (`T2-NO`/`T3-NO`/`NONE-NO`) instead of collapsing them into `ELSE-fallthrough`, making the gap visible in the harness's own printed output rather than hidden inside an aggregate bucket. Four synthetic current-epoch fixtures were added (`build_synthetic_fixtures()`) — one each for T1, T2, T3, and band=None — with every fixture's `fee_per_contract`/`fee_net_edge` hand-derived from the closed-form vig-cascade formula and independently re-verified via a standalone, non-importing arithmetic check at fixture-construction time (per the session brief's "correctness trap" constraint: a fixture whose expected value comes from calling the code under test proves nothing). All four fixtures were then run through the *real* `replay_one()` → `open_position()` → `compare()` path (not a parallel/duplicate mechanism) and **all four PASS** (`synthetic_fixtures (T-450, current epoch)`: PASS=4 FAIL=0 ERROR=0; per-branch `T1-NO n=1 pass=1`, `T2-NO n=1 pass=1`, `T3-NO n=1 pass=1`, `NONE-NO n=1 pass=1`). This closes the *coverage-existence* gap (every band now has at least one current-epoch, independently-verified assertion) but does not, and cannot, close the *real-data* gap for T1 at the current epoch (still 0 real T1 positions at epoch 12) or for T2/T3 at any epoch (structurally zero going forward under ADR-0048) — hence RESOLVED (partial) rather than RESOLVED. The pre-existing real-ledger FAILs surfaced by this same run (T1-NO: 254 mismatches across older epochs; T4M-PROJ-NO: 470 mismatches; NONE-NO: 196/196 failing) are GG-170-class historical/epoch-provenance drift, out of this session's scope per Hard Rule 11 — not touched, not re-registered here. |
| Status | RESOLVED (partial) — see Resolution. Full resolution is not achievable for T2/T3 by design (ADR-0048) and for T1 depends on a future current-epoch T1 bet actually being placed. |

</details>

### GG-181 — T4 MLB cycle-log 14.6h stale during live MLB game day, `systemctl is-active`/`ActiveState=active`/`NRestarts=0` healthy throughout — same GG-163-class blind spot recurring after GG-163 itself was marked RESOLVED

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** MEDIUM

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-181 |
| Category | Operational health blind spot — recurrence of a previously-RESOLVED gap class (GG-163), surfaced by the very probe GG-163's own remediation (T-429) built. |
| What was missed | `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh`'s T4 MLB cycle-log write-recency probe fired a `GG-163-CLASS ALERT` this session: `t4_mlb_cycle_log.jsonl`'s last row is `2026-08-14T04:49:39Z`, 14.6h old at scan time. Per CLAUDE.md's Step 4 guidance, cross-checked against T1's same-day player-match count rather than trusting the alert alone: T1's last 3 cron runs this same day show `35`, `19`, `32` players matched in live MLB markets — real games are/were live today, so this is a genuine T4 write-path outage, not an idle off-day. `systemctl is-active t4-mlb` = `active`, `NRestarts=0`, `ActiveState=active`/`SubState=running` throughout — the exact healthy-looking/blind pairing GG-163's own text warned would recur. |
| When it should have been caught | Same-day, by whatever monitoring (if any) watches the GG-163-class probe's alert output outside of a session happening to run the governance scan — this was caught only because `/session-end`'s Step 0 governance scan ran incidentally, not by a dedicated alert path. |
| Phases it survived | GG-163 (2026-08-04→07) was fixed and RESOLVED; this is a fresh recurrence discovered 2026-08-14, one week later — the underlying discovery-call failure mode (or a related one) was not permanently eliminated by GG-163's fix, only that specific instance was. |
| Why it survived | The probe added by GG-163/T-429 is diagnostic-only — it prints an alert when run, but nothing appears to page or block on it between sessions; a 14.6h-stale write path can persist silently through any gap between sessions that happen to invoke the governance scan. |
| Impact | T4 MLB (live-market-latency band) has been producing zero cycle-log rows — and therefore, most likely, zero evaluations/bets — for at least 14.6h spanning a day T1 confirms had live MLB markets. Financial impact bounded by T4's existing `kelly_fraction`/sizing (unchanged, not investigated this session), but the band is functionally dark for that window. |
| Discovery | T-450 (2026-08-14), incidental — surfaced by `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh`'s auto-run during `/session-end` Step 0, not sought out; verified via a read-only SSH check (T1 cron log grep + `systemctl show`) before registering, per Hard Rule 11 ("register and stop," not "assume and stop"). |
| Resolution | RESOLVED, T-451 (2026-08-15). Root cause confirmed via source read + file-timestamp evidence, not assumed: `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s pregame-context reload guard (`if not by_player_id:`) only ever fires on a cold/empty start. The process runs continuously (no restart) across days; its UTC-midnight date-rollover merges in whatever `pregame_mlb_*.json` is "most recent" at that instant, but PIPE-06pre (the daily pregame pipeline) typically writes the real same-day file hours later (confirmed: `pregame_mlb_20260815.json` timestamped 16:25 UTC, well after the ~00:00 UTC rollover). Once any file has been merged in — which happens at every rollover — the empty-guard never fires again, so a same-day-later PIPE-06pre write was permanently invisible for the rest of that day. Downstream, `_run_cycle`'s per-player loop does `if ls is None: continue` for any live-boxscore player absent from the stale `by_player_id` keys, producing zero evaluations AND zero `CONTAMINATION_HALT` events — exactly matching the observed simultaneous freeze of both counters despite continuous live ESPN polling. Fix: track the specific pregame file last merged (`_loaded_pregame_file`, via new `_latest_pregame_file()` helper) and reload whenever the latest file on disk differs from it, not only when the dict is empty. Implemented, full suite green (2864 passed / 0 failed / 28 pre-existing skips), merged `main` via PR #75 (`bf8c138`), deployed to VPS (fast-forward pull, two untracked-file conflicts verified byte-identical before removal), `t4-mlb` restarted. **Live proof:** fresh cycle-log rows written 2026-08-15T19:47:02Z with real live game state (STL@CHC, inning 5, Crow-Armstrong/Bregman with correct `ab_so_far`/`h_so_far`/`p_t4`/`mip`/`net_edge`), age_hours=0, no exceptions in the journal across the restart. Outage window: last stale row `2026-08-15T04:34:04Z` → first fresh row `2026-08-15T19:45:42Z`, ≈15.2h spanning live T1-confirmed MLB markets; that window's T4 in-play evaluation opportunity is irrecoverable (not backfilled, per explicit task scope — no fabricated cycle-log rows for the dark window). No sizing/edge-gate/kill-switch/`logic_epoch` changes made. |
| Status | RESOLVED — proof captured live per ADR-0052 (see Resolution row). Diagnostic-only-alert gap this entry originally flagged (nothing pages between sessions) remains true and is NOT fixed by this change — that is a separate, still-open concern; register a fresh GG- for it if it recurs undetected again. **Renumbered from this session's original GG-179 to GG-181 at merge time (2026-08-14) — collided with a concurrent session's (T-449) independently-registered GG-179 ("22 data-dependent tests silently SKIP...") landed on `origin/main` via PR #74 after this session's own merge commit was already created; T-449's GG-179 kept its number, this entry renumbered instead since it was the later of the two to reach `origin/main`.** |

</details>

### GG-191 — Ticker-date derivation was hardcoded to KXMLBHIT's literal shape and silently fell back to wall-clock date on any non-match, duplicated across five call sites

**Status:** RESOLVED 2026-08-20 · **Severity:** HIGH

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-191 |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a single-series-shaped regex, copy-pasted rather than shared, standing in for a series-agnostic contract. |
| What was missed | `_TICKER_DATE_RE` (or an equivalent inline regex) hardcoded to KXMLBHIT's literal prefix and shape (`^KXMLBHIT-(\d{2})([A-Z]{3})(\d{2})(\d{4})`) existed independently in `run_t4_mlb_live.py` (3 sites), `run_resolve_mlb.py`, `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, `run_paper_trade.py` (NBA — a differently-shaped grammar, no HHMM token), and `scripts/build_t4_outcome_store.py::group_by_ticker()` — six sites total, five files. On any non-match (unregistered series, malformed tail, or a genuinely different series like KXMLBF5/F7) every one of these silently substituted the session's wall-clock `game_date` instead of refusing the write. This is the exact mechanism behind GG-166 (44% of epoch-12 clean cohort corrupted), GG-170 (69.9% assertion-A violations concentrated in epoch 12), and GG-185 (46 stuck-open positions). |
| When it should have been caught | At GG-166's original remediation (2026-07-xx) — that fix corrected the *symptom* (wrong dates already written) but left the *fallback mechanism* itself in place and uncorrected in four of the five other call sites, and left the grammar unregistered as a shared contract. |
| Phases it survived | Ships pre-166, survives 166's fix, survives 170's discovery, survives 185's discovery — three separate incidents traced back to the same root cause before the mechanism itself was addressed rather than its outputs. |
| Why it survived | No single shared, series-agnostic ticker grammar existed for any call site to depend on; each file grew its own regex independently, so fixing one never touched the others. Nothing enforced "refuse on parse failure" as a contract — silent wall-clock substitution was the path of least resistance at each site's original authorship. |
| Impact | Wrong `game_date` values written to paper-trading ledgers and cycle logs feed directly into C4 Kelly sizing, drawdown kill-switch state, and commercial-validation clean_n counts (GG-004/APR-0024) — a corrupted date can silently misroute a record's cell, epoch, or resolution window. KXMLBF5/F7 (MLB_PARTIAL_GAME) tickers were previously unregistered entirely, meaning any live activation of those series would have hit the fallback on every single record with zero warning. |
| Discovery | T-472 (2026-08-20), tasked explicitly with making date derivation series-agnostic and refusal-only. |
| Resolution | RESOLVED this session. (1) Registered a shared `TickerGrammar` per `MarketType` in `market_type_registry.py` (`parse_ticker_date()`, `derive_game_date()`), covering MLB (`has_hhmm=True`) and NBA (`has_hhmm=False`) shapes, with KXMLBF5/F7 aliased to `MLB_PARTIAL_GAME`. (2) All six call sites across five files rewritten to delegate to the shared grammar and refuse (return `None` / raise, caller skips the write) instead of falling back to wall-clock — verified against real production data with zero refusals on any currently-live ticker (2948/2948 in `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s ledger, 1764/1764 in `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, 133/133 in `run_paper_trade.py`). (3) `scripts/run_power_calc.py` now counts and surfaces unregistered-series drops (`_UNREGISTERED_SERIES_COUNTS`) instead of silently excluding them with no visibility. (4) Regression tests added: `test_market_type_registry.py` (grammar itself, 9 tests), `test_power_calc.py` (drop-surfacing, 4 tests), `test_run_mlb_paper_trade.py` (rewrote a pre-existing test class that had encoded the OLD wrong model — leading ticker token treated as an irrelevant "creation day" with the year reconstructed from wall clock, rather than the leading token being the actual embedded year; the bug was masked because every fixture happened to use "26" matching both roles), `test_run_t4_mlb_live.py` (3 new tests; also had to correct a pre-existing fixture ticker, `TICKER_SOTO`, that was itself malformed and never matched the grammar even before this fix — same masking pattern), `test_run_resolve_mlb.py` and `test_run_paper_trade.py` (new files, 3 tests each, wrapper-contract smoke coverage). Full touched-file test run: green. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-08-20 (T-472). |

</details>

<details>

| Field | Detail |

| Gap ID | GG-197 |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — same surface as GG-046/APR-0024 (commercial-validation sample adequacy), and the exact failure mode ADR-0052's executable-verification rule exists to catch: a check that confirms a computation ran, not that its inputs were sound. |
| What was missed | `governance_scan.sh`'s GG-046 threshold block called `run_power_calc.run_all_bands()` and printed `T4M-PROJ clean_n=719 / n*=608 -- MET` whenever `status == "COMPUTED" and met`, with zero awareness of whether the underlying `clean_recs` cohort (epoch-12, per `filter_clean`'s per-band clean-epoch floor) was itself trustworthy. GG-170/GG-185 had already established that 532/719 (74.0%) of that exact cohort carries a `kalshi_ticker`-derived date that disagrees with the stored `game_date` field — meaning `outcome`/`pnl` for those rows may have been computed against the wrong day's box score. T-477's dry-run (`scripts/t477_dryrun_epoch12_repair.py`, cited in ADR-0055 Addendum A) recomputed n* on the repaired figures (mean +0.0652, sd 1.4800 vs. the uncorrected mean +0.2325, sd 1.7412): n* = 5,580, meaning clean_n=719 is 4,861 SHORT — the "MET" verdict was an artifact of the corruption, not a real threshold crossing. |
| When it should have been caught | At GG-170/GG-185's own registration (2026-08-11/2026-08-19) — once a cohort was known to be substantially corrupted, every downstream consumer of that cohort's derived statistics (not just the ledger-repair track) should have been re-examined for whether it was still safe to emit a verdict. It was not; GG-046's alert kept firing "MET" through the entire GG-170/GG-185/ADR-0055 investigation. |
| Phases it survived | Every session-start `governance_scan.sh` run between GG-170's registration and this session (2026-08-20) — an unknown but non-trivial number of sessions, since the hook runs automatically on every `UserPromptSubmit`. |
| Why it survived | Q1-Q7 of the "ARE WE COMPROMISED?" checklist (including Q7/T-432's ledger-invariant assertions) check hard limits, stub survival, interface drift, decision traceability, and field-level ledger corruption directly — but nothing in the stack cross-checked a *downstream statistical consumer* (the power calc) against a *known* corruption finding already registered elsewhere in the same log. Each governance check verified its own narrow computation completed correctly; none asked whether the computation's input cohort had already been flagged untrustworthy by a sibling gap. This is the ADR-0052 executable-verification gap in its purest form: the hook could prove `n_star` was computed, never that `clean_recs` meant what its name claimed. |
| Impact | A false "commercial-validation sample threshold crossed" signal on the single most consequential gate in the project (G6 / APR-0024) — the standing GG-046 alert text explicitly warns against silently re-running EXP-T4-01 without registering the decision first, i.e. this alert is designed to trigger operator attention on a gate-crossing event. A MET verdict computed on a 74%-corrupted cohort risked exactly the kind of premature "the sample floor has been met" conclusion the alert exists to prevent, undermining its own purpose. |
| Discovery | T-479 (2026-08-20 session), tasked directly with fixing this exact defect (pre-diagnosed and pre-verified figures supplied at task assignment; independently reproduced in full via direct ledger read — 532/719=74.0%, uncorrected n*=608 — with zero discrepancy from the supplied figures). |
| Resolution | RESOLVED same-session. `scripts/run_power_calc.py`'s `analyze_band_power()` now computes a live `ticker_date_mismatch_n`/`ticker_date_mismatch_pct` per band/cohort via a new `_ticker_date_mismatch_n()` helper, reusing (not reimplementing) the canonical series-agnostic parser `market_type_registry.derive_game_date()` (T-472/GG-191's refusal-only replacement for the old KXMLBHIT-only regex) — computed over whatever `clean_recs` the caller passes in, not hardcoded to T4M-PROJ, epoch 12, or the count 532, so it self-clears once a cohort's ticker dates agree with stored dates and self-fires again if the same corruption recurs in a future epoch or cell. `governance_scan.sh`'s GG-046 block now checks this count when `nstar_crossed` is true: if `mismatch_n > 0` it prints `VERDICT WITHHELD` with the live count/percentage and a static citation to ADR-0055 Addendum A's repaired-figure n*=5,580, instead of `MET`; if `mismatch_n == 0` it prints `MET` exactly as before. Verified directly against the live ledger (bypassing the hook's hardcoded `PROJECT` path, which always tests the shared main-tree checkout rather than a worktree): produces `T4M-PROJ clean_n=719 / n*=608 -- VERDICT WITHHELD: 532/719 rows (74.0%) carry a ticker-vs-game_date mismatch (GG-170/GG-185). n* recomputed on ADR-0055's repaired figures = 5,580 (NOT met). See ADR-0055.` — exact match to the target message shape. Self-clear/self-fire behavior confirmed with synthetic clean and corrupted cohorts, and confirmed the refusal-only contract (unparseable ticker => not counted as mismatch) holds. Per this task's explicit scope: does NOT apply the ADR-0055 repair, does NOT touch `kelly_fraction`/sizing/`logic_epoch`/cell status/the ledger, and does NOT mark ADR-0055 ACCEPTED — ADR-0055 remains PROPOSED with D1-D4 unsigned. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-08-20 (T-479). Re-verify once ADR-0055's D1 is decided and any repair is applied to origin's live ledger — the withholding should self-clear at that point without further code changes. |

</details>

### GG-199 — `scripts/new_session_worktree.sh`'s single-branch fetch left new worktrees blind to sibling `session/*` branches pushed by concurrent sessions

**Status:** RESOLVED 2026-08-21 · **Severity:** MEDIUM

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-199 |
| Category | Concurrent-session isolation defect (GG-101 class) — the launcher that exists specifically to make concurrent sessions safe had an unrelated blind spot in what it made *visible*, not just what it made *safe*. |
| What was missed | Line 34 ran `git fetch --quiet origin main` — a single-branch refspec. This fetches `origin/main` correctly (satisfying the isolation requirement: `git worktree add` still branches from a fresh `origin/main`, confirmed unchanged at line 40) but does nothing to update `refs/remotes/origin/*` for any other branch. A concurrent session's pushed `session/*` branch is therefore invisible to a newly-launched worktree until someone manually runs a wider fetch — the launcher never does this itself. |
| When it should have been caught | At GG-101's original fix (worktree isolation, T-259) — that work verified sessions could no longer destructively collide via shared working-tree git ops, but never checked whether one session's worktree could still *see* another's branch once isolation was in place. Visibility and destructive-collision-prevention are different properties; only the second was tested. |
| Phases it survived | Every worktree launched via this script since GG-101's fix — an unknown number of sessions, since sibling-branch visibility was never a scanned invariant and a missing branch produces no error, only a silent `fatal: ... not found`-style failure at the point someone tries to check it out by name. |
| Why it survived | No governance check inspects the worktree launcher's fetch scope, and the failure mode is silent by construction — a narrow fetch doesn't fail, it just fetches less than a session going looking for a sibling branch will assume it fetched. Nothing in Steps 0-4 or Q1-Q7 exercises multi-worktree branch visibility. |
| Impact | T-478 (2026-08-2x) spent a full session unable to find T-477's already-pushed branch, and had to manually run a wide fetch to recover it before it could proceed — a session-length cost paid to work around a one-line refspec. **This is causally upstream of Assertion 1 (claim/CLOSED lifecycle checks, `scripts/lib/claim_closure_check.py`, this same session/T-476): that check can only DETECT a claim that never produced a visible CLOSED row or mergeable branch — it cannot PREVENT the underlying cause when the cause is that the branch was never visible to the session that needed it.** A narrow fetch scope is exactly the kind of defect that manifests downstream as an apparently-abandoned claim. |
| Discovery | T-476 (2026-08-21 session), tasked directly with widening this refspec as one of three landing-integrity assertions (T-476/claim-and-id-assertions). |
| Resolution | RESOLVED same-session. Line 34 widened to `git fetch --quiet origin main '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'`, updating every remote-tracking ref for every `origin` branch (all `session/*` branches included) on every worktree launch, while leaving `git worktree add -b "$BRANCH" "$WT_PATH" origin/main` (line 40) untouched — isolation still starts from a fresh `origin/main` base; this change widens visibility only, it does not change what a new session branches from. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-08-21 (T-476). Atomic GG-number reservation at claim time (GG-162, the sibling defect Assertion 2 detects rather than prevents) remains a separate, unstaffed task. |

</details>
