### GG-283 — `exp027_hyp012_nfl_moneyline_backtest.py`'s Kalshi team-code alphabet lacks "WAS"; at least one live 2026 KXNFLGAME ticker uses "WAS" (not "WSH"), causing `parse_event_teams` to silently return `None` and drop that game from the EXP-027 cohort

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-283 |
| Category | Data-parsing defect — venue ticker alphabet assumption contradicted by observed live data |
| What was found | `scripts/exp027_hyp012_nfl_moneyline_backtest.py`'s `_NFL_TEAM_CODES` (line 98) included `"WSH"` and not `"WAS"`, per its own comment: "nflverse ... uses LA/WAS; Kalshi's ticker alphabet uses LAR/WSH instead." The live archive (`exp_output/PRICE_ARCHIVE/prices_2026-09-*.jsonl`) contains real, well-formed KXNFLGAME rows for the 2026-09-13 WAS@PHI game under ticker `KXNFLGAME-26SEP13WASPHI-{WAS,PHI}` — i.e. Kalshi's real ticker uses `"WAS"`, contradicting the script's hardcoded assumption for this game. `parse_event_teams("26SEP13WASPHI")` tried every split of `"WASPHI"` against `_NFL_TEAM_CODES`; the correct split (`"WAS"`/`"PHI"`) failed because `"WAS"` was absent from the set, so the function returned `None` and `load_nfl_closing_prices()` silently `continue`d past every row for this event (confirmed empirically pre-fix: 0 of 966+ WASPHI rows across 09-05 through 09-13 survived into the function's `closing` output). This game (`2026_01_WAS_PHI`) is otherwise a normal resolved Week 1 game with no other data problem. |
| Why it matters | A silent `None`-and-`continue` on a real, resolvable game shrinks the cohort without any log line or count discrepancy pointing at it — `[join] events=... matched_to_schedule=... unmatched=...` reports an aggregate unmatched count but not which games or why. This is the same failure class as GG-276's silent capture gap and GG-203's silent order failures: a `None` that reads indistinguishably from "no game here." Caught by manual per-game reconciliation, not by any structural check, at discovery time. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-15/16, T-552 (prior session), while investigating Deliverable 1's disclosure obligation for GG-276's 09-12 capture gap — found while tracing which of the 16 resolved games failed to join to a market row and why. |
| Resolution | RESOLVED 2026-09-16/17, T-555 (this session, worktree `20260917T001723Z-gg283-gg284-nfl-cohort-defects`). **Audit (Deliverable 1, done before any fix):** every distinct team-code segment actually appearing in captured KXNFLGAME tickers across the whole archive (all `prices_2026-09-*.jsonl` files, 9,186 raw KXNFLGAME rows) was pulled and diffed against `_NFL_TEAM_CODES`. Result: exactly two mismatches, in both cases the live archive uses a form the table lacked — 586 rows use `"WAS"` (0 use `"WSH"`), 564 rows use `"JAC"` (0 use `"JAX"`). All other 30 codes matched exactly; WAS was confirmed **not** the only mismatch — JAC/JAX is a second, previously-undiagnosed instance of the identical defect class (see GG-284 below, same root cause). **Fix:** `_NFL_TEAM_CODES` widened from 32 to 34 entries as a **superset** (added `"WAS"` and `"JAC"`, kept `"WSH"` and `"JAX"` rather than swapping) — only the new forms are empirically attested in the archive, but there is no proof the old forms never occur elsewhere, so superset is strictly safer than a swap. Verified exhaustively (all 34×34=1,156 two-code concatenation pairs checked programmatically) that the widened alphabet introduces **zero split ambiguity** before landing. `_KALSHI_TO_NFLVERSE` updated: `{"LAR": "LA", "WSH": "WAS", "JAC": "JAX"}` (WAS now matches nflverse's own code directly, so needs no translation entry; only LAR and JAC require translation). **Loudness mechanism:** `load_nfl_closing_prices()`'s inline parse-and-filter loop was extracted into `_load_kxnflgame_rows(files) -> (kept_rows, unparsed_segment_counts)`; an `event_segment` that fails `parse_event_teams` is now counted per distinct segment (not per-row, to avoid log spam) and a `WARNING` block is printed after the loop naming every unparsed segment and its dropped-row count, explicitly analogized in the code comment to GG-276/GG-203 as the same failure class — a bare `continue` can no longer pass silently. **Tests:** `tests/test_exp027_hyp012_nfl_moneyline_backtest.py` — `test_parse_event_teams_finds_live_ticker_forms_jac_and_was` (both new and old forms parse correctly, proving superset not swap), `test_load_kxnflgame_rows_counts_and_reports_unparsed_segments` (synthetic unparseable segment is counted, accumulated across repeat occurrences, and triggers the WARNING with the right segment string and drop count), `test_load_kxnflgame_rows_silent_when_all_segments_parse` (no WARNING when everything parses clean) — all pass, 14/14 total in the file. **Verification against the real live exchange archive (not synthetic data):** re-running `_load_kxnflgame_rows` against the full real `PRICE_ARCHIVE` post-fix reports `KXNFLGAME rows total=9186 kept(pregame,parsed)=8638` with **zero** entries in `unparsed_segments` — i.e. the fix is exhaustive across the whole real archive, not merely sufficient for the two known games; both `KXNFLGAME-26SEP13WASPHI` and `KXNFLGAME-26SEP13CLEJAC` (see GG-284) now have kept rows. **Pre-registration discipline preserved:** the fix is scoped entirely to parser/data-loading correctness (which real rows a correct implementation of the already-pre-registered join logic includes) — no pre-registered parameter, threshold, cohort rule, or the EXP-027 gate itself was touched or re-run in this session; the cohort-effect statement (2 games restored, `clean_n` moving from 14 toward 16 against `n*≈2610.35`, immaterial to the UNDERPOWERED verdict) is descriptive only. |
| Cross-references | GG-281 (the EXP-027 re-run where this game's exclusion was found); GG-284 (the other excluded game — confirmed this session to share the identical root cause, not a distinct defect as GG-284's original record speculated); GG-276 (Saturday capture gap — ruled out as the cause of this game's exclusion; the WAS_PHI ticker has pregame snapshots on 09-05 through 09-11, so the 09-12 gap does not explain this game's absence — the parse failure did); GG-203 (silent order-failure defect, cited in code as the same failure class this fix's loudness mechanism addresses); GG-166/Q7 (silent data-integrity loss, the general pattern this instance falls under). |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-09-16/17 (T-555). Code+tests committed and pushed to `session/20260917T001723Z-gg283-gg284-nfl-cohort-defects`. |

</details>

### GG-284 — `2026_01_CLE_JAX` (Week 1, 2026-09-13) has zero archived KXNFLGAME price rows across the entire captured September window; cause unconfirmed

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-284 |
| Category | Data-completeness gap — unexplained total absence of archived market data for one resolved game (root cause, once found, reclassified as identical to GG-283's category — a parsing defect, not a capture defect) |
| What was found | `exp_output/PRICE_ARCHIVE/prices_2026-09-*.jsonl` (every date 09-01 through 09-15) contained zero rows matching ticker substrings `CLEJAX` or `JAXCLE` under `series_ticker == "KXNFLGAME"` — not just missing on 2026-09-12 (the known GG-276 Saturday gap), but absent from every single day, including 2026-09-13 (the game's own date) and every day before and after it. By contrast, the other 09-13 game investigated alongside this one (WAS@PHI, see GG-283) has hundreds of rows per day from 09-05 onward. This game (`2026_01_CLE_JAX`, home=JAX, away=CLE) is a normal, resolved Week 1 game with a final score in the schedule data — there was no indication the game itself was cancelled, delayed, or unusual. |
| Why it matters | Originally treated as a possibly-distinct failure shape from GG-283 (data present-but-unparseable) since a `CLEJAX`/`JAXCLE` substring search over the archive found literally nothing under those exact strings. GG-276 (the known Saturday capture gap) was correctly ruled out: if that were the cause, this game would still show rows on 09-05 through 09-11 and 09-13 with only the 09-12 slice missing, as WAS_PHI does — instead it showed zero rows on every date, which a one-day gap cannot produce. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-15/16, T-553 (prior session), while investigating Deliverable 1's disclosure obligation for GG-276 — found while tracing which of the 16 resolved games failed to join to a market row and why. |
| **Correction to the original record** | The original record's Resolution field asserted `parse_event_teams` "was verified separately to correctly parse `CLEJAX` when tested in isolation" and concluded "the absence is upstream of parsing, in the archive itself, not a parser bug for this game." **This was the wrong string.** The real live Kalshi ticker for this matchup is `KXNFLGAME-26SEP07CLEJAC` (Jacksonville coded as `"JAC"`, not the nflverse-style `"JAX"` the original investigation tested against) — `"CLEJAX"` never occurs anywhere in the 9,186-row archive, so testing it in isolation proved nothing about the real failure. The archiver never failed to capture this game: the audit (see GG-283's Resolution) found 202 real KXNFLGAME rows for this matchup, under ticker segment `CLEJAC`, spanning 8 distinct dates in a healthy pregame pattern — indistinguishable in capture health from any other Week 1 game. The prior substring search for `CLEJAX`/`JAXCLE` found nothing because it searched for a ticker form that was never going to exist, not because the data was missing. |
| Resolution | RESOLVED 2026-09-16/17, T-555 (this session, worktree `20260917T001723Z-gg283-gg284-nfl-cohort-defects`) — as the second, previously-undiagnosed instance of GG-283's exact root cause, not a distinct defect. Cause confirmed with direct evidence: `"JAC"` (564 rows across the whole archive) is a live Kalshi ticker form for Jacksonville absent from the old `_NFL_TEAM_CODES`, exactly parallel to `"WAS"` for Washington. The same fix that resolved GG-283 (alphabet widened to a superset including `"JAC"`; `_KALSHI_TO_NFLVERSE` extended with `{"JAC": "JAX"}`; the loudness mechanism in `_load_kxnflgame_rows`) resolves this gap simultaneously — no separate code change was needed or made. Verified against the real archive: post-fix, `KXNFLGAME-26SEP13CLEJAC` has kept rows and appears among the 48 distinct event_tickers with pregame closing snapshots, and zero segments remain unparsed anywhere in the full 9,186-row archive (see GG-283's Resolution for the full run output). The reserved gap number GG-286 (contemplated during discovery in case CLE_JAX's cause turned out to be genuinely distinct from GG-283's) was **not used** — both defects trace to the single alphabet-mismatch root cause, so no third, separate defect exists to register. |
| Cross-references | GG-281 (the EXP-027 re-run where this game's exclusion was found); GG-283 (the sibling defect — same root cause, same fix, resolved in the same commit); GG-276 (Saturday capture gap — ruled out as the cause here, see "Why it matters"). |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-09-16/17 (T-555), same fix and same commit as GG-283. Code+tests committed and pushed to `session/20260917T001723Z-gg283-gg284-nfl-cohort-defects`. |

### GG-251 — ADR-0062 §4/§6 BOUNDARY authorization-posture conflict resolved conservatively; T-522's prior scaffolding build re-verified and landed under this number (GG-246 never registered)

**Status:** RESOLVED (2026-09-07) · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-251 |
| Category | ADR internal inconsistency, left unresolved-at-signature and explicitly routed to the implementing session — plus a separate, unrelated claimed-but-unlanded-work gap from the session this one supersedes. |
| What was found | ADR-0062's own Status line records that §4 (roster decision) and §6 (cell-count projection) disagree on `BOUNDARY`'s authorization posture: §4 treats `BOUNDARY` as "propose, scoped only, not authorized to build" — the same not-yet-authorized posture MLB's own `T4M-BOUNDARY` carries (confirmed directly against `execution_bands.py`: MLB has no `T4M_BOUNDARY` member) — while §6's 21-cell projection counts `BOUNDARY` as authorization-eligible alongside `ARITH`/`FLOW`, excluding only `EVENT`. T-518's sign-off recorded this conflict as unresolved rather than picking a reading, and routed resolution to the 17.1 implementing session. Separately: T-522 previously claimed `GG-246` for this same deliverable and, per this session's own task brief, "did not land it — its work is gone." Direct check against `origin/main` (both `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` and `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md`) confirmed `GG-246` is registered nowhere — no collision, but also nothing to resume; this entry is the first registration of this gap under any number. |
| When it should have been caught | The §4/§6 disagreement should have been reconciled before ADR-0062 was signed, or the ADR's own arithmetic in §6 should have been derived from §4's roster rather than independently. It was caught, correctly, at signature time (T-518) — the gap here is that resolution was deferred, not that it went undetected. |
| Phases it survived | ADR drafting, review, and operator sign-off all passed with the conflict explicitly flagged rather than silently missed — this is a case of correct escalation, not a missed check. |
| Why it survived | A cell-count projection (§6) was authored referencing the full Tier B roster pattern (MLB's own ADR-0039 precedent groups `PROJ`/`ARITH`/`FLOW`/`BOUNDARY` together informally) without re-deriving the count from §4's actual per-member authorization decision once that decision came out more conservative than the informal grouping assumed. |
| Impact | LOW as resolved. Conservative reading was available and explicitly instructed (build `ARITH`/`FLOW` only, decline `BOUNDARY` pending its own future ADR) — no live code, sizing, or promotion depended on the wrong reading; the only cost was T-518's signature having to travel with an open conflict for one more session rather than a resolved one. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-03 (T-518, ADR-0062 sign-off) flagged the conflict and declined to resolve it. 2026-09-07 (T-524/GG-251, this session) resolved it: **built `ARITH` and `FLOW` only, for both NFL and NHL — `BOUNDARY` and `EVENT` remain scoped but not built.** Reading: §4 is the roster decision (per-member authorization), §6 is downstream arithmetic derived from that roster; a projection cannot retroactively authorize what the roster itself declined to authorize, and this ADR has no independent grounds to treat NFL/NHL `BOUNDARY` more permissively than MLB's own `T4M-BOUNDARY` precedent (also scoped-but-not-built). Same conservative test applied to `T4NFL-FLOW-BLOWOUT` (§3): MLB's `T4M_FLOW` has no separate blowout member — blowout handling lives only in its `notes` field — so no `T4NFL-FLOW-BLOWOUT` member was created either. |
| Resolution | Built 4 new `ExecutionBand` members (`T4NFL_ARITH`, `T4NFL_FLOW`, `T4NHL_ARITH`, `T4NHL_FLOW`; string values `T4NFL-ARITH`/`T4NFL-FLOW`/`T4NHL-ARITH`/`T4NHL-FLOW`) in `execution_bands.py`, following MLB's exact `T4M_*` declaration pattern (`BandConfig` entries, per-sport `T4_NFL_SUBBAND_REGISTRY`/`T4_NHL_SUBBAND_REGISTRY`, `validate_t4_nfl_subbands()`/`validate_t4_nhl_subbands()`). Seeded cells in `market_type_registry.py`: 2 sub-bands × 4 NFL families (MONEYLINE/SPREAD/GAME_TOTAL/TEAM_TOTAL) + 2 sub-bands × 3 NHL families (MONEYLINE/PUCK_LINE/GAME_TOTAL) = **14 new cells**, registry total 78 → 92. Every new cell `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, every new member `kelly_fraction=0.0` — nothing wired, nothing promoted. `EVENT` excluded both sports per the ADR's own deferred-pending-C1-ingestion-verification condition. Live-import verified: before=78/after=92, status breakdown ACTIVE:1 BLOCKED:2 DARK:1 NOT_IMPLEMENTED:88. Full suite green post-build and post-merge-from-origin/main: 3015 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed. See `DECISION_LOG.md` 2026-09-07 (T-524) for the full BOUNDARY-reading rationale, and ADR-0062 itself (unchanged — ADRs are immutable; this entry is the resolution record, not a superseding ADR). |
| Status | RESOLVED. `BOUNDARY`/`EVENT` remain open future work (their own ADR/session, not this one) — not a residual defect of this entry. |

</details>

### GG-178 — `scripts/check_register_parity.py`'s `RESOLVED_PAT` regex is a bare substring search with no negation awareness, so it false-flags any ADR whose Status prose contains the literal text "NOT ACCEPTED"/"not yet ACCEPTED" as resolved

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-178 |
| Category | Tooling false-positive — a governance-parity check whose match pattern matches the negation of the condition it's meant to detect. |
| What was missed | `scripts/check_register_parity.py`'s `RESOLVED_PAT = re.compile(r"ACCEPTED\|ADOPTED\|COMPLETE\|selected")` is applied via `RESOLVED_PAT.search(status)` against the full raw Status line text, with no word-boundary or negation handling. ADR-0051's Status line reads `**Status:** DRAFT — NOT ACCEPTED. Proposal only, per T-422's hard scope fence...` and ADR-0052's reads `**Status:** PROPOSED — drafted this session (T-433) under explicit task instruction; awaiting DS sign-off (Earl Ignacio). Not yet ACCEPTED. Treat as governing intent, not a closed decision, until sign-off is recorded here.` — both contain the substring "ACCEPTED" inside an explicit negation, so both are misclassified `resolved=True` and flagged as missing an APPROVALS_REGISTER.md row, even though both docs are correctly DRAFT/PROPOSED and correctly absent from the register. |
| When it should have been caught | At the time `RESOLVED_PAT` was authored (GG-126 remediation) — no test case exercised a Status line containing an explicit negated-ACCEPTED phrase, which is itself a defensive pattern other ADR authors have reasonably used to make non-acceptance unambiguous to a human reader. |
| Phases it survived | Live and firing on every `governance_scan.sh`/`check_register_parity.py` run since ADR-0051 (2026-08-05/06) and ADR-0052 (2026-08-11) were drafted — at least several sessions' worth of session-start/session-end scans, all silently absorbing this as an expected "2 PARITY MISMATCH(ES)" noise floor rather than investigating it. |
| Why it survived | The check's exit-1/finding-list format looks identical for a true positive and this false positive, and past sessions had a *third*, genuine mismatch (ADR-0053 pre-T-448) mixed into the same output, which gave the two spurious findings cover as "probably more of the same category." T-448 only noticed because it re-ran the parity check specifically to confirm ADR-0053 cleared, and the remaining 2 findings were the ones left over. |
| Impact | Low — no real register desync exists for ADR-0051/0052 today; the check merely cries wolf on every run, which (per GG-126's own history — 4 prior recurrences of a *real* register-parity defect) is the exact kind of alarm-fatigue condition that let real desyncs go unnoticed before. Not data-loss or capital risk. |
| Discovery | T-448 close-out (`/session-end`, 2026-08-14), re-running `python3 scripts/check_register_parity.py` directly (not just reading the earlier full `governance_scan.sh` output) to confirm ADR-0053's parity fix landed clean. Confirmed ADR-0053 no longer flagged; the remaining 2 findings (ADR-0051, ADR-0052) were traced to this substring-match defect by reading both docs' Status lines directly. |
| Resolution | Not resolved by this entry — registration only, per Hard Rule 11 (T-448's declared deliverable is ADR-0053 amendment/acceptance plus session-end close-out; fixing a separate script's regex is a distinct deliverable). Fix (when picked up): anchor `RESOLVED_PAT` against negation context (e.g. reject a match preceded by `NOT\s+` or `not yet\s+` within a small window) or restructure the check to require a positive-form status token (e.g. `^\s*\*\*Status:\*\*\s*ACCEPTED\b` at line start) rather than a bare substring search anywhere in the line. **Fixed 2026-08-29/30, T-505** — the same `RESOLVED_PAT`/`is_resolved()` fix landed under GG-222 (this is the identical code defect, registered independently under two GG numbers; GG-222 was discovered and worked on second but happened to be the one this session's task named explicitly). `scripts/check_register_parity.py` now rejects a resolved keyword preceded by a case-insensitive "NOT "/"NOT YET " prefix, correctly leaving both ADR-0051 ("NOT ACCEPTED") and this entry's own named ADR-0052 case ("Not yet ACCEPTED") classified unresolved. Regression test: `tests/test_check_register_parity.py` (includes a dedicated ADR-0052 "not yet accepted" case). See GG-222 for the full before/after checker output. |
| Status | RESOLVED 2026-08-29/30 (T-505) — see GG-222 (duplicate registration of the same code defect, amended in the same commit). |

</details>

### GG-222 — GG-126-class recurrence: APR-0032/ADR-0056 write-back-missed for a week, plus `check_register_parity.py`'s `RESOLVED_PAT` has a false-positive bug on "NOT ACCEPTED" Status lines

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-222 |
| Category | Documentation-integrity — same failure class as the now-archived GG-126 (`GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md`, RESOLVED 2026-07-17): a real sign-off event happened and `APPROVALS_REGISTER.md` was never written back. Filed as a new gap, not appended to GG-126 itself, because GG-126 is RESOLVED and lives in the archive file, which the 2026-08-05 restructure (T-420, see CLAUDE.md Step 3) makes immutable to hand-patching — entries arrive there verbatim from the live log and never move back or get edited in place. |
| What was missed | `python3 scripts/check_register_parity.py` (run 2026-08-27/28, T-501) reported 3 mismatches. Two were genuine GG-126-class write-back misses: (1) APR-0032 — its own document records operator sign-off (D1/D2/D3 ADOPTED, Earl Ignacio, 2026-08-21), but the register row still read "PENDING (drafted 2026-08-20/21, not yet submitted for sign-off)," six days stale. (2) ADR-0056 (the superseding ADR implementing APR-0032, ACCEPTED 2026-08-21, T-474 session) had zero row or mention anywhere in `APPROVALS_REGISTER.md`. The third, ADR-0051, is NOT a write-back miss — see next field. |
| Second finding — checker bug | `check_register_parity.py`'s `RESOLVED_PAT = re.compile(r"ACCEPTED|ADOPTED|COMPLETE|selected")` is an unguarded substring match with no word-boundary or negative-lookbehind protection against a preceding "NOT ". ADR-0051's Status line reads verbatim `**Status:** DRAFT — NOT ACCEPTED. Proposal only, per T-422's hard scope fence...` — genuinely still DRAFT, correctly never accepted. The bare substring "ACCEPTED" inside "NOT ACCEPTED" makes the regex classify it `resolved=True`, so the checker flags it as a false "resolved in doc but never mentioned in register" miss. Confirmed by direct read of the ADR-0051 document; no register row was added for it (adding one would itself violate the task instruction "do not add a register row for a document that was never accepted"). |
| When it should have been caught | APR-0032/ADR-0056: at the T-474 sign-off session itself, 2026-08-21 — same failure mode GG-126's structural fix (the `governance_scan.sh` register-parity check) is designed to catch at the *next* session start, which it did (surfaced here, 6 days later, not months). ADR-0051 regex bug: at `check_register_parity.py`'s original authorship (GG-126's 2026-07-17 structural-fix session) — no test case with a "NOT ACCEPTED"-shaped DRAFT Status line was exercised against `RESOLVED_PAT` at the time. |
| Phases it survived | APR-0032/ADR-0056: 6 days (2026-08-21 → 2026-08-27). ADR-0051 regex bug: since the checker's authorship, 2026-07-17 (~6 weeks), undetected because no DRAFT document happened to phrase its Status line as "NOT ACCEPTED" containing the literal accepted-keyword substring until ADR-0051 was drafted. |
| Why it survived | Write-back discipline at sign-off time keeps failing exactly as GG-126's own resolution text predicted ("only the underlying discipline... keeps failing" — six prior instances before this one). The regex bug survived because `RESOLVED_PAT` was written as a keyword-presence check, not a status-classification parser, and no adversarial test case exercised the "NOT " prefix collision. |
| Impact | LOW. No capital, gating, or code impact — both are paper-trail/tooling gaps. APR-0032/ADR-0056 caused no downstream harm since nothing depended on the register row being current in the 6-day gap. The regex bug produces a false alarm (noisy, not silent) — it does not hide a real miss, since the checker still correctly requires a human to look at the flagged doc. |
| Discovery | 2026-08-27/28, T-501/GG-222, while executing Deliverable 2 of a STANDARD-tier task (land T-490/T-491 + close register-parity mismatches) — running the checker directly and reading each flagged document's own Status field. |
| Resolution | APR-0032/ADR-0056: fixed same session — `APPROVALS_REGISTER.md`'s APR-0032 row corrected to reflect the 2026-08-21 D1/D2/D3 sign-off (register was the stale side; document and its superseding ADR-0056 were both correct), and a new ADR-0056 row added. Re-run of `check_register_parity.py` post-fix: down to 1 mismatch (ADR-0051 only), confirming the fix. ADR-0051 regex bug: **NOT fixed** — explicitly out of this session's scope fence ("DO NOT touch... scripts/ (beyond running the checker)"). Registered here as a finding for a future session to fix `RESOLVED_PAT` (e.g. `re.compile(r"(?<!NOT )(?:ACCEPTED\|ADOPTED\|COMPLETE\|selected)")` or an explicit `NOT ACCEPTED`/`NOT-ACCEPTED` exclusion checked before the positive match) so a correctly-DRAFT document does not have to be manually re-triaged as a false positive every session it's checked. **Regex-bug half fixed 2026-08-29/30, T-505:** `scripts/check_register_parity.py` now word-boundaries `RESOLVED_PAT` and routes every match through a new `is_resolved(text)` helper that rejects a resolved keyword immediately preceded by a case-insensitive "NOT "/"NOT YET " prefix (handles both ADR-0051's "NOT ACCEPTED" and ADR-0052's "Not yet ACCEPTED" — the latter case is also GG-178's documented example, see cross-reference below). Regression test added: `tests/test_check_register_parity.py` (7 cases, pins the exact ADR-0051/ADR-0052/ADR-0056 Status strings plus a negation/word-boundary/lowercase-`selected` set) — `python3 -m pytest tests/test_check_register_parity.py -q` → 7 passed. Post-fix re-run of `check_register_parity.py`: ADR-0051 dropped out as predicted, but the mismatch count went to **1, not 0** — `APR-0033: no APPROVALS_REGISTER.md row at all` surfaced as a genuine, separate, previously-uninvestigated GG-126-class miss (the false-positive noise from this very regex bug had given it cover). Registered separately as GG-227 per Hard Rule 11 rather than fixed in this session (out of Deliverable 2's scope fence, which covers only the checker script + its test). **Cross-reference — GG-178 is a duplicate registration of this exact regex defect**, filed earlier (predates GG-222, names the identical `RESOLVED_PAT` line and additionally documents the ADR-0052 "Not yet ACCEPTED" case that motivated this fix's "NOT YET" handling) — see GG-178's own entry, also marked resolved by this same commit/test rather than left dangling as a stale duplicate. |
| Status | OPEN 2026-08-27/28 (T-501), amended 2026-08-29/30 (T-505), **CLOSED 2026-09-01 (T-506)**. Write-back half (APR-0032/ADR-0056) RESOLVED as of T-501; regex-bug half RESOLVED as of T-505, then **completed** 2026-09-01 (T-506, Deliverable 3): T-505's `is_resolved()`/`NEGATED_PREFIX_PAT` fix handled "NOT "/"NOT YET " negation but not "NEVER " — a class gap, since "NEVER ACCEPTED" is the same defensive-negation pattern GG-178/GG-222 exist to catch and was still an unguarded substring match after T-505's fix. `NEGATED_PREFIX_PAT` widened from `r"\bNOT\s+(?:YET\s+)?$"` to `r"\b(?:NOT\s+(?:YET\s+)?\|NEVER\s+)$"` (case-insensitive, unchanged), still routed through the same `is_resolved()` helper (`UNRESOLVED_PAT` is not and never was used as the negation guard — it governs an unrelated stale-register-row check at a different call site). 7 new regression tests added to `tests/test_check_register_parity.py::TestIsResolvedNegation` pinning the class rather than the single instance: `test_bare_not_accepted_is_unresolved` ("NOT ACCEPTED"), `test_bare_not_yet_accepted_is_unresolved` ("NOT YET ACCEPTED"), `test_lowercase_not_accepted_is_unresolved` ("not accepted"), `test_never_accepted_is_unresolved` ("NEVER ACCEPTED — proposal withdrawn"), `test_lowercase_never_accepted_is_unresolved` ("never accepted"), `test_accepted_with_date_is_resolved` (positive control, "ACCEPTED 2026-08-21"), `test_adopted_is_resolved` (positive control, "ADOPTED") — full suite `python3 -m pytest tests/test_check_register_parity.py -v` → **14 passed** (7 pre-existing T-505 cases + these 7 new; `test_bare_not_accepted_is_unresolved` overlaps conceptually but not literally with T-505's ADR-0051 case, which was phrased "DRAFT — NOT ACCEPTED" rather than bare "NOT ACCEPTED"). [Correction, same session: an earlier draft of this entry and of the matching DECISION_LOG.md D3 entry said "8 new regression tests" — a miscount caught during report-back verification; the actual, correct count is 7 new (14 total), as enumerated above and confirmed by the pytest output itself.] `python3 scripts/check_register_parity.py` re-run against the merged post-PR-#125, post-GG-227 tree: **CLEAN — 71 APR/ADR docs checked against the register (27 legacy-exempt)**, zero mismatches — identical to the baseline immediately before this fix, confirming the regex change altered no live classification (no doc in the current corpus phrases a resolved-status negation with "NEVER "; the fix closes the class gap defensively, not reactively). The write-back-discipline recurrence this entry's history names (7th instance of the GG-126 class) remains a standing process observation outside any single session's scope — noted, not addressed, consistent with T-505's own framing. Both named findings (write-back miss, regex bug) and the class-completeness gap identified at the last amendment are now resolved; closing this entry rather than deferring again. |
| Correction (2026-09-01, T-511) | A strategic-window session characterized T-505's "NOT "/"NOT YET " negation-guard fix as having "closed the instance, not the class" for that negation class, and both this entry's own T-506 Status text (above) and the matching `DECISION_LOG.md` D3 entry inherited that framing (D3's own title reads "closed the RESOLVED_PAT negation-guard class, not just the single instance" — phrasing that implies T-505's fix was itself only instance-scoped). **That characterization is inaccurate.** T-505's `NEGATED_PREFIX_PAT = r"\bNOT\s+(?:YET\s+)?$"` was already a general pattern over the NOT/NOT YET class, not a fix pinned to the single ADR-0051 "DRAFT — NOT ACCEPTED" string it was written against — any Status line negated with "NOT "/"NOT YET " was correctly classified unresolved by T-505's fix, before T-506 touched anything. What T-505's fix did *not* cover was a genuinely separate negation prefix, "NEVER ", which is a different member of the same defensive-negation category, not an ungeneralized instance of the same member. T-506's real, accurate contribution (Deliverable 3) was therefore twofold: (1) extending `NEGATED_PREFIX_PAT` to add the "NEVER " prefix, a coverage extension, not a generalization of an instance-bound fix; and (2) adding 7 regression tests (`TestIsResolvedNegation`) that pin the full negation class going forward — tests whose value holds independent of whichever framing is used to describe why they were added. The false "instance, not class" finding traced to a verification harness that re-implemented `is_resolved()`'s matching logic from reading the regex rather than importing and calling the real function against test strings — an instrument-error finding, the class of error this project's own governance-gap tracking exists to catch (see CLAUDE.md Q7 framing: a value already written can be wrong even when the step that produced it ran). This correction does not alter GG-222's Status (CLOSED, 2026-09-01, T-506, unchanged) or T-505's/T-506's own claim rows above, which are left as originally written per this project's append-only correction discipline. |

### GG-236 — `claim_session.sh`'s GG-number collision check cannot see numbers registered on an unlanded branch, producing a live GG-235 duplicate risk between T-509 and T-513

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** LOW

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-236 |
| Category | Systemic blind spot — a variant of GG-162/GG-199 (no atomic reservation for GG-numbers): the collision check that does exist only sees `origin/main`'s current state, not content sitting on unlanded session branches. |
| What was found | T-509 (branch `session/20260901T052401Z-t509-adr0054a-cell-awareness`, unlanded as of 2026-09-02) registered `### GG-235` on its own branch. T-513 claimed `04_EXECUTION/SESSION_CLAIMS.md` row "T-513 / GG-235" at 2026-09-03T00:30:04Z for its own future ADR-0054(b) work — three minutes before this session's own claim (T-514/GG-236, 00:33:19Z). `claim_session.sh`'s collision check runs against `origin/main`'s current state only; T-509's branch was not merged at the time T-513 claimed, so T-509's GG-235 registration was structurally invisible to the check. This session (T-514) landed T-509 onto `origin/main` (see GG-186's 2026-09-03 sub-entry, this log), which means `origin/main` now carries a real `### GG-235` header (T-509's LEDGER_INVARIANT_SUITE.md filename-drift finding). T-513's session has not yet landed its own work as of this entry, so no second `### GG-235` header exists yet — confirmed by direct count: exactly one `### GG-235` match in `03_DECISIONS/GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` post-landing. The collision has not happened; the conditions for it are live. |
| When it should have been caught | At T-513's claim time (00:30:04Z) — `claim_session.sh` would need to check not just `origin/main` but every live/unlanded session branch's own `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` state to catch this, which it does not and was never designed to do (same limitation GG-199 registered for GG-number collisions generally, applied here to a specific unlanded-branch instance). |
| Phases it survived | Single-instance discovery, this session (T-514, 2026-09-03) — not yet a recurrence of a previously-registered exact case, but a directly foreseeable specific instance of GG-162/GG-199's general limitation. |
| Why it survived | `check_id_collision.sh` (invoked by `claim_session.sh`) has no mechanism to enumerate other sessions' unpushed/unmerged branch content — by design it can only check what has already reached `origin/main`, since that is the only state guaranteed to be fetchable and stable. An unlanded branch's GG-registration is invisible until it merges. |
| Impact | LOW today, but concrete and imminent: if T-513's session writes its own `### GG-235` header when it closes out (its claim row already commits it to that label), `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` will carry two distinct entries under the same number — exactly the duplicate-ID failure mode `scripts/lib/gg_id_uniqueness_check.py` (GG-199) exists to catch, and would catch, at that session's own governance scan or the next session's Step 3. The fix at that point is renumbering T-513's entry to the next free number, not re-opening this GG. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-03, T-514 (this session), while landing T-509 per this session's Deliverable 0 and cross-checking `SESSION_CLAIMS.md` for other GG-number activity in the same window per GG-234's explicit lesson (numbers go stale between drafting and execution — verify live, don't trust a prompt-supplied label). Found T-513's claim row already referencing "GG-235" for unstarted work, three minutes before T-509's GG-235 (already real, on-branch) was landed onto `origin/main` by this same session. Out of this session's declared scope to fix T-513's side (T-513/14.3 owns its own branch and `logic_epoch.py`; this session's scope fence does not include coordinating or editing another live session's claimed number) — registered per Hard Rule 11, not acted on further. |
| Resolution | This session's specific predicted instance was already closed via [[GG-237]] (T-513 self-caught and renumbered before any duplicate content was written), which left this entry OPEN "as a statement of the general unlanded-branch blind spot." **2026-09-03 (this session, GG-236/GG-238 instrument fixes): the general blind spot itself is now fixed, not just documented.** `scripts/lib/check_id_collision.sh`'s Rule A (GG-169) previously only grepped `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`/`GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md` as checked out on the current branch — invisible to a `### GG-NNN` header that exists only on a pushed-but-unlanded branch. Fixed by also `git grep`-ing the gap log at every local head and fetched remote-tracking branch tip (`git -C "$repo_root" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/heads refs/remotes`, then `git grep -lE "^### ${id}([^0-9]|$)" <refs> -- 03_DECISIONS/GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md 03_DECISIONS/GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md`) — a live per-branch-tip snapshot, not a commit-history walk, so a since-renumbered/removed id on a stale branch cannot false-positive forever. `claim_session.sh`'s fetch step was widened from `git fetch origin main` to `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'` (with a fallback to the narrower fetch) so other sessions' pushed branches are actually present locally for the scan to see; the rebase target remains `main` only — nothing merges from the extra refs. Guarded on `git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse --git-dir` so the function stays offline-testable exactly as its docstring claims (bare `tmp_path` fixtures with no `.git` still no-op through this branch cleanly). Regression test `tests/test_claim_session_collision.py::test_detects_gg_id_registered_only_on_unlanded_branch` pins the fix: it creates a real git repo, registers a `### GG-9002` header on an unmerged branch only, and asserts the check reports a collision from `main` — confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix code (`returncode=0`, silently passing) before the fix and PASS after; a sanity complement (`test_allows_gg_id_with_no_header_anywhere_including_branches`) confirms the branch scan does not over-block a genuinely fresh id. Cross-references: [[GG-162]] (root cause — no atomic GG-number reservation; this closes one specific detection gap in that family, not the family itself — true atomic reservation at claim time remains unstaffed), [[GG-237]] (the live near-miss this fix retroactively would have caught structurally instead of by a session noticing mid-work). |
| Status | RESOLVED. |

</details>

| Phases it survived | `git log --oneline -3 -- scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` shows three commits touching this file since (`1fd42ab` T-466, `184c8d0` T-497, `066bc8b` T-509/ADR-0054(a), the last landed onto `origin/main` by this same session, T-514) — none corrected the stale defaults, because none of those tasks' scope fences included this specific concern. |
| Why it survived | The script is ALARM-ONLY and degrades gracefully (`SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, exit 0) when a source file is absent — per `CLAUDE.md`'s own Q7 description, this is by design and never crashes into a visible gate failure. That graceful degradation means a session running the plain no-flag invocation with the stale defaults sees a quiet `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` report for the T1/T4 portfolio assertions, indistinguishable in the output from a genuinely-missing fetch, rather than an error pointing at the wrong path. |
| Impact | LOW-MEDIUM: not a false-positive risk (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE ≠ a wrong value, and Q7's stated reading is "any assertion whose violations concentrate in the current epoch," not "check for SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE"), but a silent under-coverage risk — a session running Q7's exact documented command with a freshly-scp'd, correctly-named file would still get zero T1/T4 portfolio assertion coverage from the default invocation, and nothing surfaces that as a problem. |

| Resolution | **2026-09-03 (this session, GG-236/GG-238 instrument fixes): fixed.** Changed `DEFAULT_T1_PORTFOLIO`/`DEFAULT_T4_PORTFOLIO` in `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` from `.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb.json`/`.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb_t4.json` to `paper_portfolio_mlb.json`/`paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json`. `DEFAULT_OUTCOME_STORE` (`t4_mlb_outcome_store.jsonl`) was left untouched — already correct, confirmed live on the VPS (`ls /opt/prediction-market-bot/logs/`). All three now-current filenames verified directly against a live VPS `ls` of `/opt/prediction-market-bot/logs/` at fix time, not inferred: `paper_portfolio_mlb.json` (615KB, mtime Aug 6), `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` (26MB, mtime Sep 3 — actively written), `t4_mlb_outcome_store.jsonl` (1MB, mtime Aug 12) all present. No assertion logic, threshold, or `--strict` behavior touched — path-only fix, per this session's explicit scope fence. `python3 scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` (no args) run before and after: both runs report `[SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE]` for all three sources and `0 total violations` — behavior is unchanged in this worktree because the actual data files still haven't been scp'd into this worktree-local, gitignored `logs/` dir, which is an honest, expected result (the fix corrects the *path the default now points at*, not whether that path's file happens to exist in an arbitrary checkout) rather than a fabricated clean pass; `CLAUDE.md` Q7's bare invocation will pick up real coverage on any checkout whose `logs/` dir actually has the VPS files fetched under their current names. `tests/test_assert_ledger_invariants.py` (32 tests — none reference the default-path constants directly, all pass explicit paths) re-run post-fix: 32/32 passed, no regression. Ran the repo-wide grep this entry's own prior text called for ("confirm GG-235+GG-238 together are exhaustive"): **not exhaustive** — 23 other `.py`/`.sh` files still reference the stale `.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb*.json` names, plus `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh` and roughly two dozen doc/handoff files. This is a materially larger defect than GG-235/GG-238 individually scoped, and is out of this session's declared scope fence (`claim_session.sh`/`check_id_collision.sh`/`assert_ledger_invariants.py`, their tests, and gap-log/decision-log entries only) — registered as [[GG-242]] per Hard Rule 11 rather than fixed here.

**Correction, 2026-09-03 (same session continued, GG-242 close-out):** the fix described above was found to be a regression, not a fix, and has been reverted. `governance_scan.sh` invokes `assert_ledger_invariants.py` with no CLI arguments after populating only the `.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb*.json`-named local cache files (its own ssh-fetch logic, lines ~151-243) — it never creates a `paper_portfolio_mlb*.json` file locally. Changing the script's defaults to the direct VPS names, as this entry's fix did, therefore pointed the bare invocation at a path nothing in this repo populates, silently defeating Q7's ledger-integrity check on every plain session-start run since this fix landed. This entry's own before/after test above (both runs against an empty `logs/` dir) could not have caught this, since neither run tested the actual `governance_scan.sh`-populated path. `DEFAULT_T1_PORTFOLIO`/`DEFAULT_T4_PORTFOLIO` have been reverted to `.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb.json`/`.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb_t4.json`. Full details, empirical verification, and the corrected understanding of the `.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb*.json` naming convention are in [[GG-242]]'s resolution. This correction does not change this entry's Status (RESOLVED remains accurate — a real defect existed and something was fixed at the time); it corrects what the fix should have been. |

### GG-252 — `kalshi_client.py`'s `PlayerMarket` dataclass and `_parse_market()` are player-prop-shaped and cannot represent a moneyline/spread market; the bot parses 0 NFL game markets today despite 264+ being live on Kalshi

**Status:** RESOLVED · **Severity:** HIGH

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-252 |
| Category | Schema mismatch in the venue client's return type, not a parsing bug — the dataclass the parser returns has no field capable of representing a categorical game-winner or line-cover outcome. |
| What was found | Live-verified against real Kalshi data (2026-09-07): a raw unparsed `_get('/markets', ...)` call finds 64 open `KXNFLGAME` markets and 200+ open `KXNFLSPREAD` markets. The bot's own `kalshi_client.py::_parse_market()` (line 427) returns **zero** parsed markets for either series when called through the bot's normal path. Root cause: `threshold = int(parts[-1])` inside a bare `except Exception: return None` assumes the last ticker segment is a numeric threshold — true by coincidence for `KXNFLTOTAL` tickers (e.g. `...-64`), false for moneyline tickers ending in a team code (`...-NYG`) and spread tickers ending in a signed-number+team compound (`...-KC8`), both of which raise and are silently dropped. Deeper than the parser: `PlayerMarket` (kalshi_client.py:~159, docstring "Represents the market for 'player scores >= threshold points in game'") has fields `player_name`, `team_abbr`, `threshold: int` — there is no field or dataclass variant anywhere in the client capable of representing "team A beats team B" or "team A covers N points." `series_ticker_for()` (registry-driven since T-439) correctly resolves the series ticker for all three NFL series; the failure is entirely downstream, in parsing/representation, not in market discovery. |
| When it should have been caught | At the point NFL market types were first seeded into `market_type_registry.py` (`MarketType.NFL_MONEYLINE`/`NFL_SPREAD`/etc.) — registering a `MarketType` does not imply the client that fetches it can represent its outcome shape, and nothing checked that at registration time. |
| Phases it survived | Unknown number of sessions since NFL market types were registered in `market_type_registry.py`; the registry entries alone gave the appearance of NFL-market support without a live parse-path test ever having been run against them until this audit. |
| Why it survived | Every prior touch of NFL support in this codebase (registry entries, grammar table, ExecutionBand scaffolding per ADR-0062) operated at the `MarketType`/band level, never exercising `kalshi_client`'s actual parse path against live NFL tickers. A registry entry existing reads as "supported" without a live fetch-and-parse test to falsify that impression. |
| Impact | HIGH — this is the first of the six pregame-moneyline trace steps (Market fetch) and a hard blocker on its own: no NFL moneyline or spread bet can be evaluated, sized, or placed while the client returns zero parsed markets for those series, regardless of how complete every downstream step (model, risk, execution, resolution) is. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-07, T-525 (this session), NFL pregame-moneyline readiness audit, Step 1 of the six-step trace — live-tested against real Kalshi data per explicit task instruction ("Test it against live Kalshi; do not read the code and infer"), then root-caused by reading `_parse_market()` and the `PlayerMarket` dataclass definition directly. Register-and-stop per Hard Rule 11 — this session is scoped to audit-only, no build. |
| Resolution | RESOLVED, 2026-09-07, T-526. Added a new frozen dataclass `GameMarket` (sibling to `PlayerMarket`, not a bent reuse of it) plus `GameMarketSnapshot`, and split `_parse_market()` into a dispatcher: tickers whose series prefix is in a new `_NFL_GAME_SERIES` set (`KXNFLGAME`/`KXNFLSPREAD`/`KXNFLTOTAL`/`KXNFLTEAMTOTAL`) route to new `_parse_nfl_game_market()`; every other ticker (NBA/MLB, unchanged) routes to the renamed, byte-identical `_parse_player_market()`. Grammar was derived from a live dump of all four series (not fabricated from a spec): `strike_type` distinguishes `"structured"` (moneyline, no numeric line) from `"greater"` (numeric-line markets); the authoritative threshold is read directly from the payload's `floor_strike` field (always `X.5`), never reconstructed from the ticker's digit suffix, because team codes in the ticker tail are variable-length (`KC`, `SF`, `NYG`, `LAR`, 2-3 chars) and made the old approach unreliable; `custom_strike.football_team` (present/null) distinguishes team-scoped `KXNFLSPREAD`/`KXNFLTEAMTOTAL` from game-level `KXNFLTOTAL`. Unparsed markets are now logged (`logger.warning`, message prefixed `GG-252:`) and counted via a new `unparsed_count` field on both `DS02Snapshot` and `GameMarketSnapshot` — never silently returned as `None` into a void. New public method `fetch_game_markets()` mirrors `fetch_player_points_markets()`'s pagination pattern for the four NFL series. Verified against live Kalshi data post-fix: `KXNFLGAME` 64/64 parsed (was 0/64), `KXNFLSPREAD` 404/404 (was 0/404+), `KXNFLTOTAL` 304/304 (unchanged — survived by coincidence pre-fix), `KXNFLTEAMTOTAL` 55/55 (was 0/55) — and critically, `KXMLBHIT` (the only band that currently trades) held at 286/286 both before and after, confirming zero regression to prop parsing. 59/59 tests pass in `tests/test_kalshi_client.py` (18 new tests added covering all four NFL market types, dispatcher routing, unparsed-count/logging, and `fetch_game_markets()`); full project suite run separately, see `DECISION_LOG.md` for the pass/fail/skip line. Scope fence held: only `kalshi_client.py` and its tests were touched — no C3/C4/C5 wiring, no live routing, no ledger/kelly_fraction/archiver changes. This closes the Step-1 (Market fetch) blocker from the six-step NFL pregame-moneyline trace; Steps 2-6 (C1 ingestion, C2 features, C3 model, C4 risk sizing, resolution) remain unbuilt — see GG-253/254/255. |
| Status | RESOLVED. |

</details>

Every day this stays at 0 is a day of NFL depth observations across all four families (KXNFLGAME 64 / KXNFLSPREAD 404 / KXNFLTOTAL 304 / KXNFLTEAMTOTAL 55 open markets, live-verified 2026-09-08) that cannot be recovered later, delaying by the same margin the point at which NFL's depth sample reaches the ~200+ observations/family target the module's own docstring describes as the goal (`archive_market_prices.py:41-56`). |

The severity is in the accumulating, permanent deficit to the depth time series, not an active operational block. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-08, T-528 (NFL Week 1 capture-fidelity audit), Deliverable 5 — direct read of the live NFL cron lines while assessing depth-sample adequacy per task instruction; task framing assumed the MLB precedent value of 2 applied to NFL already, which direct read disproved. |

Flag semantics verified by direct read: `archive_market_prices.py:217-220` (`ap.add_argument("--depth-sample-per-family", type=int, default=0, help="opt-in: balanced orderbook sample size per family per run (0 = disabled)...")`) and `main()` at `archive_market_prices.py:255` (`if args.depth_sample_per_family > 0: depth_rows = _sample_depth(...)`) confirm depth sampling is strictly opt-in and only fires when the value is `>0`. Hand-run against the live four NFL series with `--depth-sample-per-family 1` (`python3 scripts/archive_market_prices.py --series KXNFLGAME KXNFLSPREAD KXNFLTOTAL KXNFLTEAMTOTAL --out /tmp/nfl_depth_verify_T533 --depth-sample-per-family 1`, 2026-09-09T14:56:54Z) confirmed: 827 price snapshots written across the 4 series (64+404+304+55, matching live open-market counts exactly), plus **4 depth rows** written to `depth_2026-09-09.jsonl` — exactly 1 per family (GAME_TOTAL, GAME_WINNER, RUN_LINE, TEAM_TOTAL), each `"usable": true`. Sample row: `{"run_ts": "2026-09-09T14:56:54Z", "family": "GAME_TOTAL", "series_ticker": "KXNFLTOTAL", "ticker": "KXNFLTOTAL-26SEP14DENKC-64", "usable": true, "mid_cents": 7.5, "half_spread_cents": 0.5, "top_of_book_contracts": {"yes": 130, "no": 2378}, "within_5c_contracts": {"yes": 8287, "no": 15139}, "within_5c_usd_min_side": 621.52}`. Against the unchanged MLB baseline (~3,700 requests/week, `--depth-sample-per-family 2` untouched on all 10 MLB series, `DEFAULT_PAUSE_S=0.30` unchanged at `archive_market_prices.py:74`): **≈19-29% on top of the MLB baseline**, up from the original 7-15%. Zero error/backoff/rate-limit/exception lines in `logs/price_archive_cron.log` today. No defect found; `deploy/cron.conf` was not touched. ### GG-270 — `scripts/web_dashboard.py`'s `/api/data` unbounded-`json.load()` of `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` OOM-killed the dashboard service in a restart loop, blanking every panel (MLB and NFL alike) behind a false "SSH tunnel" error

**Status:** RESOLVED (2026-09-09/10) · **Severity:** HIGH

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-270 |
| Category | Production incident — resource-exhaustion defect in `scripts/web_dashboard.py`, discovered live by the operator. |
| What was found | The operator reported the dashboard at localhost:8050 loading its shell (confirming post-T-534 NFL code was deployed) but every panel — MLB (BANKROLL, CUM P&L, DRAWDOWN, LIVE POSITIONS, TRADE LOG, SYSTEM STATUS, PIPE-05 LOG TAIL) and NFL alike — stuck on "Loading..." behind a red banner: "Cannot fetch data: Load failed. Check SSH tunnel is open." Deliverable 1 (`systemctl show pmbot-web-dashboard.service -p NRestarts,ActiveState,SubState` + `journalctl -u pmbot-web-dashboard.service --since '-24 hour' \| grep -c oom-kill`) found the service in an active OOM-kill/`Restart=always` crash loop — `NRestarts` climbing and repeated `oom-kill` lines in the journal, `ActiveState=active` throughout (the exact GG-118 blind spot: an `is-active` check alone would have reported healthy mid-loop). This does not cleanly fit the standard localization bucket taxonomy (a: non-200/exception: no — the process never returns any response, it is SIGKILLed mid-request; b: slow-200/browser-timeout: no — there is no slow response, just none; c: fast-200-healthy: no) — it is a fourth, distinct failure mode: a hard cgroup `MemoryMax=128M` kill, uncatchable by any in-process try/except, recurring on the ~30s poll cadence the frontend uses to call `/api/data`. |
| Why it matters | Deliverable 2 root-caused it to `scripts/web_dashboard.py`'s `_load_json()` performing a full unbounded `json.load()` of `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` on every `/api/data` request. Direct VPS inspection found the file at 37,799,957 bytes, of which the `rejected_positions` array — confirmed via full-file grep of the frontend JS to be read nowhere in the UI — spans ~33.4MB (~88%) as the file's last top-level key. Timing `_load_all_data()` in isolation showed this call alone costing ~4.3s and ~96MB of peak Python-object memory per request, comfortably exceeding the service's 128M `MemoryMax` cgroup cap on every poll. `_load_jsonl()` already uses a bounded `deque(maxlen=tail)` from a prior fix; `_load_json()` had no equivalent bound — this asymmetry was the crux. The failure mode is structurally severe because it is total and silent-to-the-operator: a misleading "check SSH tunnel" banner masked a server-side resource exhaustion, and — before this fix — a single oversized/malformed MLB input file could take down the NFL panel too, violating the isolation invariant that "a blank MLB dashboard is never an acceptable consequence of an NFL problem" (and the converse). |
| Discovery | 2026-09-09/10, T-539 (this session), operator-reported ("The MLB panels are dead too. This is NOT an NFL rendering bug.") — explicit correction against an initial hypothesis. |
| Resolution | Two changes to `scripts/web_dashboard.py`, both additive and stdlib-only (no third-party JSON streaming library — the file's own docstring commits to stdlib-only): (1) new `_strip_json_array_key()` — a bracket-depth, string/escape-aware raw-text scanner that removes a named key's array value (replacing it with `[]`) *before* `json.loads()` is called, so the ~24,231 `rejected_positions` objects are never constructed at all (not parsed-then-discarded, which would still pay the CPU/memory cost) — and `_load_json_dropping_key()`, which applies it specifically to `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json`'s `rejected_positions` field; every other field, including `closed_positions` (which the frontend's `renderPortfolio()` reduces over for bankroll/P&L/drawdown/win-rate) stays byte-identical to a plain `_load_json()` call. (2) `_load_all_data()` rewritten so every returned key is wrapped in a `safe(fn, default)` closure — a second layer of per-key isolation on top of each loader's own existing try/except, so no single key's loader, however it fails, can take down the rest of the `/api/data` payload. Regression coverage added in `tests/test_web_dashboard_api.py` (11 tests): `_strip_json_array_key` correctness (basic replace, no-op on missing/non-array key, nested brackets/escaped quotes inside the array, key-as-last-field); `_load_json_dropping_key` (drops target key, tolerates missing/malformed file); and three live-server `/api/data` end-to-end tests — 200 with a complete MLB payload when both NFL files are absent (T-534's NFL block is additive-only, must not be able to take MLB down, and vice versa), 200 with a 20,000-entry `rejected_positions` array present, and 200 (with `t4_portfolio` degrading to `{}`) when the T4 portfolio file is outright corrupt JSON. No MLB panel, path, key, or query was changed; `deploy/cron.conf`/the archiver/`kelly_fraction`/`run_t1_nfl_game_market.py` were not touched. Deployed and verified live on the VPS for the specific OOM-kill defect this entry covers: `NRestarts=0`, zero `memory.events` pressure counters post-restart (see `DECISION_LOG.md` 2026-09-09/10 entry for the post-fix `systemctl`/`curl` verification transcript). **Correction (2026-09-11):** this line originally read as full Deliverable 3/4 success, including the "comfortably under 2s" timing target — that was premature. Two further defects on this same request path surfaced only once live curl timing was actually checked, not inferred from the passing unit tests: GG-272 (a latency regression T-539's own fix introduced, RESOLVED) and GG-273 (a systemd `CPUQuota=10%` cap throttling the now-fixed code from ~0.39s CPU into ~3.8s wall time live, RESOLVED — required an additional out-of-band VPS deploy step beyond `git pull`, since `/etc/systemd/system/pmbot-web-dashboard.service` was a stale, separately-installed copy not kept in sync by the repo). See those entries for the full timing story. The OOM-kill claim in this line stands on its own and is unaffected by the correction. Final live-verified state (2026-09-11): 5x consecutive `/api/data` curls, all HTTP 200, 0.733-0.879s wall time — genuinely comfortably under the 2s target. |
| Cross-references | GG-118 (prior OOM-restart-loop precedent on this same service; this incident recurred through a different code path — `_load_json()`'s unbounded parse rather than the mechanism GG-118 fixed); GG-271 (the upstream defect this fix works around — the T4 MLB writer process's unbounded growth of `rejected_positions` — registered and explicitly not fixed in this session, per Hard Rule 11); GG-272 (RESOLVED) and GG-273 (RESOLVED) — latency defects on this same request path, found during Deliverable 4 live verification. |
| Status | RESOLVED (2026-09-09/10) — OOM-kill/restart loop fixed, deployed and verified live; regression tests passing (11/11). Timing/latency on this same request path was tracked separately in GG-272 and GG-273, both now RESOLVED — final live-verified `/api/data` timing is 0.733-0.879s, comfortably under Deliverable 3's 2s target. |

</details>

### GG-271 — T4 MLB writer process appends an unbounded `rejected_positions` array to `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` (24k+ entries / ~33MB observed 2026-09-10); register-and-stop, out of scope for this session

**Status:** RESOLVED (2026-09-11, code+migration) · ACTIVATED (2026-09-15, confirmed live in running process) · **Severity:** MEDIUM

**Note (T-548, 2026-09-15):** the Resolution/Status text below states "No service was restarted" and treats that as proof the fix needed no activation step — that framing was correct for the 2026-09-11 migration (a one-time script-level trim of the file on disk) but incomplete as a claim about the *running process*: `t4-mlb` is a long-running Python service that does not hot-reload, so leaving it un-restarted meant its in-memory `PaperTrader` class kept executing pre-GG-271-fix bytecode — the newly-added `MAX_REJECTED_POSITIONS` cap was on disk and in the git history, but not in the live process's memory. Direct consequence, discovered by a strategic-window queue pass 2026-09-15T00:24Z: `rejected_positions` regrew from the migrated 2,000 back to 7,654 entries (15.58MB) over the intervening ~77h, on pace to reach OOM-relevant size again by ~2026-09-21. **Corrected disposition:** `t4-mlb` was restarted at 2026-09-15T00:12:01Z — verified via `systemctl show t4-mlb -p ActiveEnterTimestamp` and a clean `journalctl` Stopping→Deactivated→Started sequence, not a crash loop — but as an *incidental side effect of session T-542's own separate PR #129 close-out deploy*, not a restart performed by or targeting this session (T-548). T-548 verified, without itself restarting anything, that the now-running process genuinely carries and enforces the fix: (a) process identity confirmed via `/proc/<PID>/cwd`+`cmdline` matching the checked-out source tree, not a shadow install; (b) `paper_trader` re-imported using the live process's own venv+cwd resolved to `MAX_REJECTED_POSITIONS = 2000` in the checkout; (c) `rejected_positions` measured at exactly 2000 post-restart; (d) hold-through-a-write-cycle proof — cross-referenced against `audit_mlb_t4.jsonl`, 5,680 real rejection events fired between 2026-09-15T00:12:42Z and 2026-09-15T04:00:08Z while the field stayed pinned at exactly 2000 throughout, i.e. the ring buffer trimmed on every one of those writes rather than merely reflecting one lucky snapshot. A fresh read-only backup was taken and verified this session (`paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.gg279_verify.20260915T045755Z.json.bak`, `open_positions` byte-exact vs. live). The general principle this incident exposes — a fix landing in a long-running service's source, even fully migrated on disk, is not activated in that service's own memory until it is restarted, and nothing in session-start or close-out protocol currently checks process-level activation vs. mere code-landing — is registered separately as GG-279 (OPEN). See GG-279 for the structural fix; this note documents only GG-271's own corrected factual disposition.

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-271 |
| Category | Upstream data-growth defect, discovered while root-causing GG-270 (dashboard OOM-kill) but living in a different process/file entirely. |
| What was found | `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json`'s `rejected_positions` array grew to 24,231+ entries (~33.4MB of the file's 37,799,957 total bytes, ~88%, confirmed via direct byte-offset inspection on the VPS) with no apparent cap, rotation, or archival — whatever T4 MLB writer process appends to this list (not `scripts/web_dashboard.py`, which only reads it) has no bound on its growth. `closed_positions` in the same file was also noted, as a related but not-yet-urgent watch item, to be on a growth trajectory worth re-checking as more game-days accumulate — it is not yet large enough to be a problem and was not measured precisely in this session. |
| Why it matters | GG-270's dashboard-side fix (dropping the key before parse, in the *reader*) works around the symptom but does not address the cause: the file will keep growing unbounded regardless, eventually threatening other future readers/writers of this file (backups, any future tooling that does need `rejected_positions`, disk usage on the VPS) even though the dashboard itself is now immune. A rejected-position record that is genuinely never needed downstream is better capped, rotated, or dropped at write time than grown forever and worked around at every read site. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-09/10, T-539 (this session), while root-causing GG-270 — the writer process and its file are outside `scripts/web_dashboard.py`, the scope fence for this session's dashboard-fix task. |
| Resolution | Not attempted by T-539 — register-and-stop per Hard Rule 11. **T-542 (2026-09-11) picked this up as its own single-deliverable session.** Re-measured live: 25,243 entries / 29.27MB (2026-09-11) — the array had *shrunk* in size since the 2026-09-10 reading despite growing in count, consistent with rejection-payload field variability rather than any interim fix; growth rate ~1,000-1,200 rejections/day and accelerating. Writer census (whole-repo grep, not assumption-of-one-site): the **only** append site in the entire repository is `paper_trader.py`'s `open_position()`, `self._state.setdefault("rejected_positions", []).append(pos)`, fired on every non-2xx Kalshi order response (GG-079/T-234 routing), inside the existing `with self._lock, self._file_lock():` block. Reader census: `scripts/web_dashboard.py` explicitly does **not** read it (strips the key before parse, GG-270/272 fix, with its own comment noting the field "grows unbounded and isn't read by the frontend") — but it is FALSE that nothing reads it: `monitor.py::check_failed_order_rate` is a genuine live functional reader (`len(failed)/len(open+closed+rejected)`, warn-only alarm, GG-098, no auto-halt), invoked once per pool per day via `run_resolve_mlb.py`'s 06:30 UTC cron (`deploy/cron.conf` line 208); `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py`'s `positions_by_band`/`positions_by_cell` also read it, alarm-only, never gating without `--strict` (untouched, per explicit scope DO NOT). Because a genuine reader exists, option (a) "stop writing it" was ruled out per the task's own stated logic; decision recorded in `DECISION_LOG.md` 2026-09-11 — option (b), a `MAX_REJECTED_POSITIONS=2000` ring buffer enforced centrally inside `PaperTrader._save()` (the one choke point every lock-guarded mutation already passes through, so no new lock discipline and no append-site-specific logic to bypass), sized against `check_failed_order_rate`'s daily cadence with multi-day margin even at the accelerated observed rate. C6 audit log does NOT fully duplicate dropped entries (only a subset of fields at write time, via the existing `kalshi_order_failed` warning) so the migration preserves full pre-truncation history to a durable timestamped sidecar file rather than discarding it — see `scripts/gg271_bound_t4_rejected_positions.py`. Code (constant + `_save()` bound + migration script + `TestRejectedPositionsBounded` sustained-volume test, 7/7 passing, 402.64s) committed and pushed (`74abab1`). **Live VPS migration executed 2026-09-11T19:12:30Z**, via an isolated VPS worktree (`/opt/gg271-migration-worktree`, detached HEAD, never touching the live service's own working tree) running the migration script with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at that worktree's `src/` while reusing the live `t4-mlb` service's own venv. A genuine race was found and fixed first: the migration script's original backup/verify reads were plain, lock-free filesystem reads against a file under active concurrent write — a live dry-run directly observed a `.stat()` call reporting 0 bytes immediately after a successful parse, i.e. a torn read caught mid-`write_text()` (that method is truncate-then-write, not atomic temp+rename). Fixed by moving the entire backup → verify → sidecar-write → migrate → re-verify sequence inside one `with trader._lock, trader._file_lock():` acquisition — the same lock the live writer uses — eliminating the race (commit `d1a4e41`). Real migration result: pre-migration file=39,352,978 bytes, open_positions=0, closed_positions=2,994, rejected_positions=25,317; backup verified byte-exact on `open_positions` (n=0) before any write; full 25,317-entry pre-truncation history preserved to a durable timestamped sidecar (`paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.rejected_positions_history.20260911T191230Z.json`, never overwritten); post-migration file=7,336,835 bytes (81.4% smaller), open_positions=0 (unchanged, verified byte-exact against pre-migration), rejected_positions=2,000 (bounded from 25,317 to `MAX_REJECTED_POSITIONS=2000`). Backup preserved at `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.pre_gg271_migration.20260911T191230Z.json.bak` (39,352,978 bytes). **No service was restarted** — `t4-mlb` confirmed `NRestarts=0`, continuously active since before the migration (`ActiveEnterTimestamp` 2026-09-11T14:44:21Z, unaffected by the 19:12:30Z migration). Live `/api/data` latency re-measured post-migration: 5/5 consecutive requests, all HTTP 200, 0.591-0.744s (comfortably under the 2s requirement). |
| Cross-references | GG-270 (the dashboard-side symptom this defect caused; this entry is the upstream cause GG-270's fix works around rather than resolves). GG-034 (file-lock invariant governing every mutation to this file; this fix's migration script itself uncovered and closed a lock-discipline gap in its own read path, not just the writer's). |
| Status | RESOLVED (2026-09-11, T-542) — root cause fixed in code (bounded ring buffer, `MAX_REJECTED_POSITIONS=2000`, enforced centrally in `PaperTrader._save()`), live VPS file migrated safely under the existing GG-034 lock discipline with full pre-truncation history preserved to a durable sidecar, open_positions verified byte-exact unchanged, no service restart, `/api/data` latency re-verified under 2s post-migration. **ACTIVATED (2026-09-15, T-548)** — see the corrective Note directly under this entry's Status header for the full account: the un-restarted live process regrew `rejected_positions` to 7,654 entries before `t4-mlb` was incidentally restarted by T-542's own PR #129 close-out deploy at 2026-09-15T00:12:01Z; T-548 verified (module-resolution + 5,680-event hold-through-write-cycle proof) that the now-running process genuinely enforces the cap, took a fresh verified backup, and registered GG-279 for the general activation-vs-landing gap this exposed. |

### GG-272 — GG-270's own OOM fix introduced a latency regression (~2.2-4.6s, two separate causes) that would have kept `/api/data` failing Deliverable 3's "comfortably under 2s" requirement, caught only because Deliverable 4 benchmarked the full pipeline instead of trusting the unit tests alone

**Status:** RESOLVED (2026-09-11) · **Severity:** HIGH

<details>
<summary>Full record ▸</summary>

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gap ID | GG-272 |
| Category | Self-introduced regression, discovered mid-Deliverable-4 live verification of GG-270/T-539's own fix — not an operator report, not an unrelated discovery; both defects live in the exact request path (`_load_all_data()`) that T-539's fix was required to make fast. |
| What was found | Two independent latency defects, both inside the code T-539 wrote to fix GG-270, found by benchmarking the *full* `_load_all_data()` pipeline against the real VPS files rather than trusting the 11/11 (later 121/121) passing unit tests in isolation: (1) `_strip_json_array_key`'s bracket-depth scan (originally a hand-rolled char-by-char loop, 14.15s against the real 39.1MB `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json`; a regex/`finditer`-token version cut that to 4.634s but was still far too slow) — both measured directly against the real file, not a synthetic fixture. (2) `_load_jsonl`/`_load_tail`, already using a bounded-memory `deque(maxlen=tail)` from T-539's fix, were still O(file-size) in *time*: `for line in f` iterates and splits every byte of the file regardless of how much of it is kept. Against the VPS's real `audit_mlb_t4.jsonl` (433,403,656 bytes) and `audit_mlb.jsonl` (101,386,227 bytes), this alone cost ~2s per `/api/data` request — a completely separate defect from (1), invisible to a benchmark of the strip function alone. |
| Why it matters | Deliverable 3's explicit requirement was server-side time "comfortably under 2s (hard ceiling 5s)." Defect (1) alone (4.634s) blew the hard ceiling; even after fixing (1), the full pipeline still measured 2.2048s — technically past the 2s target on its own, and left no margin against the 5s ceiling once real request/render overhead is added. Had Deliverable 4 verified success from the 11/11 unit-test pass alone (all of which use small tmp_path fixtures, never the real 39MB/101MB/433MB VPS files), both defects would have shipped silently — the dashboard would have gone from "OOM-killed every ~30s" to "still too slow to trust," which from the operator's perspective is not meaningfully fixed. This is the exact failure mode the task's own instruction — "Do not report success on a passing unit test alone" — exists to catch. |
| Discovery | 2026-09-11, T-540 (this session), while executing Deliverable 4's live-verification step against real VPS files (via an out-of-band `/tmp/web_dashboard_candidate.py` deploy, not the live service) rather than proceeding straight to a curl-and-declare-done based on the passing test suite. |
| Resolution | (1) `_strip_json_array_key` rewritten with an O(1) structural fast path: `rejected_positions` is confirmed (empirically, via direct inspection of the real VPS file) to be that file's structurally *last* top-level key, so its closing `]` is provably the text's last `]`, locatable via a handful of C-level `rfind`/`strip` calls instead of scanning the ~35MB array — validated before use by `json.loads()`-parsing the resulting candidate, with a safe fallback to the general scan (renamed `_strip_json_array_key_scan`) whenever the shortcut's preconditions don't hold, so correctness never depends on this key staying last. Measured: 0.0987s (vs. 4.634s), byte-identical output confirmed against the old scan. (2) new `_read_tail_lines()` helper: seeks to EOF and reads backward in fixed 64KB chunks until enough newlines are found, touching only the bytes actually needed regardless of total file size — replaces both `_load_jsonl`'s and `_load_tail`'s full-file-scan implementations (the now-unused `from collections import deque` import removed). Correctness verified with a direct `diff` against the shell's own `tail -n 5` reference output on the real 101MB VPS file — identical. Full-pipeline benchmark against the real 433MB/101MB/39MB files, combining both fixes: **0.3628s** — genuinely comfortably under 2s. Regression coverage: all 11 pre-existing `test_web_dashboard_api.py` tests plus all 110 pre-existing `test_c8_dashboard.py` tests continue to pass unchanged (121/121) — this fix is behavior-preserving, not a new-tests-only change. No MLB panel/path/key/query touched; `deploy/cron.conf`/archiver/`kelly_fraction`/`run_t1_nfl_game_market.py` not touched. |
| Cross-references | GG-270 (the incident whose own fix introduced this regression — GG-270's "Resolution" field's "Deployed and verified live on the VPS" language predates this discovery and is corrected in that entry once this session's real live-VPS verification, not just out-of-band benchmarking, completes); GG-271 (separate, still-OPEN upstream defect — the T4 writer's unbounded `rejected_positions` growth — unaffected by and unrelated to this entry). |
| Status | RESOLVED (2026-09-11) — fix implemented and benchmarked at 0.3628s against real VPS files, deployed live, and re-verified via live curl (5 consecutive requests, all HTTP 200 with valid non-null MLB payloads). **Note:** live curl timing itself did NOT confirm "comfortably under 2s" on first deploy (~3.8-4.15s measured, reproducibly, across 5 separate requests) despite the 0.3628s out-of-band benchmark — root-caused to a separate, previously-undiscovered defect (GG-273, systemd `CPUQuota=10%` throttling), not to any defect in this entry's fix. GG-273 is now also RESOLVED (2026-09-11) — final live-verified `/api/data` timing, with both fixes deployed, is 0.733-0.879s. This entry's own fix (the O(1) strip fast path + backward-chunked tail reader) is confirmed correct and fast — the code itself was never the problem. |
